.t0 <- Sys.time()

# Baseline table per stratum at fixed horizons (6/12/36/60 months).
# Per imputation: refit the Cox model, extract the Breslow cumulative baseline
# hazard per stratum and evaluate it at the horizons; then average across
# imputations (pragmatic MI pooling of H0 -- declare this in the text).
# n/events are the across-imputation means, rounded.
bh_table <- function(f, train_list, times = c(6, 12, 36, 60)) {
  tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels")
  sv <- gsub("^strata\\(|\\)$", "", tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)])
  status_var <- all.vars(f[[2]])[2]   # status from Surv(time, status)
  per_imp <- lapply(train_list, function(d) {
    fit <- survival::coxph(f, data = d, model = TRUE)
    bh  <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
    # Evaluate the step function at the horizons (last jump <= t; flat tail)
    H <- sapply(split(bh[, c("time", "hazard")], bh$strata), function(z)
      stats::approx(z$time, z$hazard, xout = times, method = "constant", f = 0, rule = 2)$y)
    # coxph's combined strata label uses the bare level for a FACTOR strata
    # variable, but prefixes "var=value" for a non-factor (numeric/logical)
    # strata variable -- verified empirically against survival::basehaz().
    lab <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(sv, function(v) {
      x <- d[[v]]
      if (is.factor(x)) as.character(x) else paste0(v, "=", as.character(x))
    }), sep = ", "))
    if (!setequal(colnames(H), unique(lab)))
      stop("Stratum labels from basehaz() do not match the data; inspect the strata variables.")
    list(H = H, n = table(lab), ev = tapply(d[[status_var]], lab, sum))
  })
  g <- sort(colnames(per_imp[[1]]$H))
  if (!all(vapply(per_imp, function(x) setequal(colnames(x$H), g), logical(1))))
    stop("Stratum set differs across imputations; inspect imputed strata variables before pooling.")

  Hm <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(per_imp, function(x) x$H[, g, drop = FALSE])) / length(per_imp)
  n_mean  <- rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, function(x) as.numeric(x$n[g]),  numeric(length(g))))
  ev_mean <- rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, function(x) as.numeric(x$ev[g]), numeric(length(g))))

  out <- data.frame(stratum = g, n = round(n_mean), events = round(ev_mean), check.names = FALSE)
  for (k in seq_along(times)) {
    out[[paste0("H0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(Hm[k, g], 4)
    out[[paste0("S0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(exp(-Hm[k, g]), 4)
  }
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

# NOTE: error bars are the across-imputation spread (tiny: outcomes are shared across
# imputations). Sampling uncertainty is given by the ipeval bootstrap CIs further below.

set1_colors <- rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(3, "Set1")[1:2])
plot_metrics <- function(s, ttl) {
  df <- dplyr::filter(s, Time != "Global") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      Time_num = as.numeric(as.character(Time)),
      Risk = factor(Risk, levels = c("Readmission", "Death")),
      Metric = ifelse(Metric == "Uno's C-Index", "Discrimination (C-index)", "Prediction error (IBS)"),
      ScoreType = ifelse(is.na(ScoreType), "n/a", ScoreType),
      # nudge lp vs risk +-1 month on the x-axis so points/error bars at the same
      # horizon don't sit exactly on top of each other; IBS ("n/a", single score)
      # is not nudged.
      Time_plot = Time_num + dplyr::case_when(ScoreType == "risk" ~ -1, ScoreType == "lp" ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
    )

  n_imp <- max(s$n, na.rm = TRUE)
  message(
    "holdout-cindex-ibs-plot: solid line = risk (1-S(t) at each horizon, PRIMARY score under stratified baseline ",
    "hazards); dashed line = lp (linear predictor, audit/stability check). Error bars show the 2.5-97.5 percentile of ",
    "`mean` ACROSS THE ", n_imp, " IMPUTATIONS (q025/q975 columns) -- NOT a bootstrap sampling CI; with only ", n_imp,
    " imputations this spread is small by construction and must not be read as sampling uncertainty (the ipeval/",
    "bootstrap cells further below give the real sampling CIs). lp and risk are nudged +-1 month on the x-axis so ",
    "they don't overlap when close in value."
  )

 ggplot(df, aes(Time_plot, mean, color = Risk, fill = Risk, linetype = ScoreType,
                 group = interaction(Risk, ScoreType))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q025, ymax = q975), width = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = set1_colors) + scale_fill_manual(values = set1_colors) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(risk = "solid", lp = "dashed", `n/a` = "solid"), breaks = c("risk", "lp")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 108, 12)) +
    labs(x = "Months since discharge", y = "Value (2.5-97.5 percentile across imputations)",
         color = "Outcome", fill = "Outcome", linetype = "Score", title = ttl) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

The IBS under the pred23 convention is recalculated solely as a control to demonstrate that the adjustment reproduces the number already reported by the notebook.

# SEPARATE robustness check, complementing (not replacing) holdout-ibs-classical-delta-death
# above. That cell's paired bootstrap treats G (the training-fold censoring KM) as part of the
# frozen model: train is never resampled there, so G cannot vary across replicates by
# construction (Target 1: frozen-model performance uncertainty in this evaluated population,
# Collins et al. 2024 part 1). This cell instead jointly resamples BOTH the training fold (to
# re-estimate ONLY the censoring KM, G) and the test/validation fold (to re-score), while the
# Cox coefficients and the predicted S(t) curves themselves stay frozen -- no model refitting,
# no re-imputation, no re-selection. It propagates sampling uncertainty in the training-side
# censoring-weight ESTIMATE itself, which the cell above cannot capture. Label this as what it
# is: a training-side censoring-weight robustness check, not a development-process bootstrap.
# Expect roughly 2-4 minutes with parallel = TRUE (measured serial: about 12 minutes at this
# cohort's size for B = 1000); lower B_JOINT_DEATH if a faster turnaround is needed.
source(file.path(if (exists("project_root")) project_root else getwd(),
                 "cons/_alt_scripts/ibs_classical_joint_resample_g.R"))
stopifnot(exists("pred_bp1"), exists("pred_bp2"), exists("ibs_grid"), exists("IBS_CLASSICAL_HORIZONS"))
B_JOINT_DEATH <- 1000L
JOINT_SEED <- 2125L
W_cl_death <- sweep(.ibc_trap_weights(ibs_grid[ibs_grid > 0], IBS_CLASSICAL_HORIZONS), 2, IBS_CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, "/")
scorer_death_delta <- ibsjr_make_simple_scorer(
  time_train = pred_bp1$y_train$time, event_train = pred_bp1$y_train$event,
  time_test  = pred_bp1$y_test$time,  event_test  = pred_bp1$y_test$event,
  surv_list = list(best_perf1 = pred_bp1$S[, ibs_grid > 0, drop = FALSE],
                   best_perf2 = pred_bp2$S[, ibs_grid > 0, drop = FALSE]),
  grid_pos = ibs_grid[ibs_grid > 0], weight_list = list(classical = W_cl_death))
cat(sprintf("Joint train+test resampling robustness bootstrap: n_train = %d, n_test = %d, B = %d\n",
            nrow(pred_bp1$y_train), nrow(pred_bp1$y_test), B_JOINT_DEATH))
flush.console()
boot_death_jointG <- ibsjr_bootstrap_core(
  n_train = nrow(pred_bp1$y_train), n_test = nrow(pred_bp1$y_test),
  scorer = scorer_death_delta, B = B_JOINT_DEATH, seed = JOINT_SEED, parallel = TRUE)
death_jointG_summary <- ibsjr_summarize(boot_death_jointG, IBS_CLASSICAL_HORIZONS)
# Paired delta: the scorer draws ONE (bi_train, bi_test) pair per replicate and scores both
# arms with it, so these two columns line up row-for-row and the difference is genuinely paired.
delta_jointG <- boot_death_jointG[, grepl("^best_perf1__classical__", colnames(boot_death_jointG)), drop = FALSE] -
                boot_death_jointG[, grepl("^best_perf2__classical__", colnames(boot_death_jointG)), drop = FALSE]
delta_jointG_summary <- data.frame(
  horizon_months = IBS_CLASSICAL_HORIZONS,
  delta_mean = colMeans(delta_jointG, na.rm = TRUE),
  delta_lower_95 = apply(delta_jointG, 2, stats::quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE),
  delta_upper_95 = apply(delta_jointG, 2, stats::quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE))
knitr::kable(death_jointG_summary, "markdown", digits = 6,
  caption = "Robustness check (does not replace the Target-1 table above): classical mortality IBS with censoring weights G re-estimated inside every bootstrap replicate on a jointly resampled training fold. Cox coefficients and S(t) stay frozen. Compare interval widths against holdout-ibs-classical-delta-death-print's Target-1 intervals; materially wider here indicates the training-side censoring estimate itself contributes non-trivial uncertainty.") |> print()
knitr::kable(delta_jointG_summary, "markdown", digits = 6,
  caption = "Robustness check: paired delta IBS (best_perf1 minus best_perf2) under joint train+test resampling with G refit. Compare against ibs_delta_death's delta_lo/delta_hi.") |> print()

  utils::write.csv(death_jointG_summary, file.path(out_dir, "holdout_ibs_classical_death_jointG.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(delta_jointG_summary, file.path(out_dir, "holdout_ibs_classical_delta_death_jointG.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}

# Absolute "per 1000" translation of the HELD-OUT DCA, with replicate CIs.
.per1000_holdout <- function(sm, rk, thr_show, horizons = c(12, 36, 60)) {
  d <- sm[sm$risk == rk & sm$strategy == "Model" & sm$horizon %in% horizons, , drop = FALSE]
  f1 <- function(v) formatC(round(v, 1), format = "f", digits = 1)
  ci <- function(m, lo, hi) sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", f1(m), f1(lo), f1(hi))
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(thr_show, function(t) {
    r <- d[abs(d$threshold - t) < 1e-9, , drop = FALSE]; if (!nrow(r)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(
      horizon = r$horizon, thr = paste0(t * 100, "%"),
      in_focus = ifelse(t >= r$focus_lower & t <= r$focus_upper, "*", ""),
      event_per1000 = f1(r$observed_event_risk_mean * 1000),
      captured_vs_none = ci(r$net_benefit_mean*1000, r$net_benefit_q025*1000, r$net_benefit_q975*1000),
      avoided_vs_all  = ci(r$interventions_avoided_mean*10, r$interventions_avoided_q025*10, r$interventions_avoided_q975*10),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  out[order(out$horizon), ]
}

# ---- Purpose ----------------------------------------------------------------
# This chunk performs patient-level bootstrap DCA for all readmission and mortality prediction specifications.
# Readmission includes cause-specific net risk and both competing-risk CIF constructions.
# Mortality includes the Full PH and SHAP-informed Cox models.
# Treat-all and treat-none are retained as reference strategies.
# Models and individual predictions remain frozen. Only held-out patients are resampled.

# survival is required by the sourced DCA helpers (Kaplan-Meier / Aalen-Johansen
# estimators of the observed event risk used inside the net-benefit calculation).
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
# Guard: stop early with a clear message if the notebook setup chunks were not run.
if (!exists("project_root")) stop("project_root is missing. Run the notebook setup chunks first.", call. = FALSE)
# out_dir: where the CSV tables are exported (falls back to cons/_out if unset upstream).
if (!exists("out_dir")) out_dir <- file.path(project_root, "cons", "_out")
# data_out: where the archived RDS bundle is intended to live.
data_out <- file.path(project_root, "data", "20241015_out")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(data_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Frozen holdout prediction objects produced by the upstream validation chunks:
# bp1 = Full PH specification, bp2 = SHAP-informed specification,
# *_cif = competing-risk cumulative-incidence variants of the readmission predictions.
required_objects <- c("results_boot_val_bp1", "results_boot_val_bp2", "results_boot_val_bp1_cif", "results_boot_val_bp2_cif")
missing_objects <- required_objects[!vapply(required_objects, exists, logical(1), inherits = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_objects) > 0L) stop("Missing prediction objects: ", paste(missing_objects, collapse = ", "), ".", call. = FALSE)
# Helper script providing .extract_replicates() (pulls replicate blocks out of the
# results objects) and .compute_replicate_curves() (computes net-benefit curves
# for a single prediction block over thresholds x horizons).
DCA_ADCA_SOURCE <- file.path(project_root, "cons/_alt_scripts/adca_from_results_boot.R")
source(DCA_ADCA_SOURCE)
# ---- Bootstrap configuration --------------------------------------------------
DCA_BOOT_B <- 1000L                      # number of patient-level bootstrap resamples
DCA_BOOT_SEED <- 2125L                   # seed making the resample indices reproducible
DCA_BOOT_HORIZONS <- c(6, 12, 36, 60)    # horizons (months) at which net benefit is evaluated
DCA_BOOT_DENSE_GRID <- TRUE              # TRUE: dense threshold grid for curves; FALSE: few reference thresholds
# Readmission thresholds span 1%-40% (higher expected event rates).
DCA_THR_READMISSION <- if (DCA_BOOT_DENSE_GRID) seq(0.01, 0.40, by = 0.01) else c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30)
# Mortality thresholds span 0.5%-10% (death is rarer, so clinically relevant thresholds are lower).
DCA_THR_MORTALITY <- if (DCA_BOOT_DENSE_GRID) seq(0.005, 0.10, by = 0.005) else c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10)
# ---- Parallel backend ---------------------------------------------------------
# Use future + future.apply only if all three packages are available.
DCA_USE_PARALLEL <- requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("parallelly", quietly = TRUE)
if (DCA_USE_PARALLEL) {
  # Make PSOCK worker startup deterministic and patient: sequential node setup and
  # a long connect timeout avoid spurious failures on slow machines; raise the
  # globals size limit because each worker receives the pooled prediction block.
  options(parallelly.makeNodePSOCK.setup_strategy = "sequential")
  options(parallelly.makeNodePSOCK.connectTimeout = 600)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 10 * 1024^3)
  # Use at most half the available cores, capped at 12, always at least 1.
  DCA_N_WORKERS <- min(12L, max(1L, parallelly::availableCores() %/% 2L))
  # Try to start a multisession plan; on any error fall back to serial execution.
  parallel_ok <- tryCatch({
    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = DCA_N_WORKERS)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Parallel setup failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    FALSE
  })
  if (!parallel_ok) {
    DCA_USE_PARALLEL <- FALSE
    future::plan(future::sequential)
  }
}
message("DCA bootstrap workers: ", if (DCA_USE_PARALLEL) DCA_N_WORKERS else 0L)
# ---- Helper: pool replicate blocks --------------------------------------------
# Each results_boot_val_* object contains several replicate blocks over the same
# held-out patients. Pool them by averaging the patient-level predicted-risk
# matrices element-wise (all blocks must have identical row counts), keeping the
# first block's structure (times, events, competing-risk fields) with replicate_id
# reset to 1 to mark it as the single pooled block.
.dca_pool_blocks <- function(blocks) {
  nr <- nrow(blocks[[1]]$pred_risk)
  stopifnot(all(vapply(blocks, function(b) nrow(b$pred_risk) == nr, logical(1))))
  b0 <- blocks[[1]]
  b0$pred_risk <- Reduce("+", lapply(blocks, function(b) b$pred_risk)) / length(blocks)
  b0$replicate_id <- 1L
  b0
}
# ---- Helper: bootstrap DCA for one model specification ------------------------
# block: pooled predictions plus observed times/events for the held-out patients.
# thresholds/horizons: evaluation grid. observed_method: how the observed event
#   risk is estimated ("aalen-johansen" for readmission with death as competing
#   risk, "km" for mortality). model_id/model_label/prediction_scale: metadata
#   carried into the output. B: number of resamples. seed: resampling seed.
.dca_boot_one_arm <- function(block, thresholds, horizons, observed_method, model_id, model_label, prediction_scale, B, seed) {
  message(sprintf("Running DCA bootstrap for %s with B = %d.", model_label, B))
  thresholds <- sort(unique(thresholds))
  n <- nrow(block$pred_risk)
  # Columns retained from the point-estimate curves before merging with CIs.
  keep <- c("horizon", "threshold", "n_obs", "positive_rate", "observed_event_risk", "nb_model", "nb_treat_all", "nb_treat_none", "std_nb_model", "std_nb_treat_all", "interventions_avoided")
  # Point estimates: DCA curves on the full (un-resampled) holdout set.
  point_results <- .compute_replicate_curves(block, thresholds, horizons, readmit_method = observed_method)
  if (!nrow(point_results)) stop("No DCA point estimates were produced for ", model_id, ".", call. = FALSE)
  point_results <- point_results[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  # Key "horizon_threshold" used to align bootstrap outputs with point-estimate rows.
  point_key <- paste(point_results$horizon, point_results$threshold, sep = "_")
  # Draw all B resample index vectors upfront under a fixed seed; the same
  # resamples are then used whether execution is serial or parallel.
  set.seed(seed)
  bootstrap_indices <- lapply(seq_len(B), function(i) sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE))
  # One bootstrap replicate: subset the block to the resampled patients
  # (predicted risks, follow-up times, event indicators, and competing-risk
  # time/status when present), recompute the curves, and return named vectors
  # keyed by horizon_threshold for later alignment.
  one_replicate <- function(index) {
    # Parallel workers start with a fresh session: reload survival and the
    # sourced helpers there if they are missing.
    if (!exists(".compute_replicate_curves", mode = "function")) {
      suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
      source(DCA_ADCA_SOURCE)
    }
    b <- block
    b$pred_risk <- b$pred_risk[index, , drop = FALSE]
    b$time <- b$time[index]
    b$event <- b$event[index]
    if (!is.null(b$cr_ftime)) b$cr_ftime <- b$cr_ftime[index]
    if (!is.null(b$cr_fstatus)) b$cr_fstatus <- b$cr_fstatus[index]
    d <- .compute_replicate_curves(b, thresholds, horizons, readmit_method = observed_method)
    k <- paste(d$horizon, d$threshold, sep = "_")
    list(nb_model = setNames(d$nb_model, k), nb_treat_all = setNames(d$nb_treat_all, k), std_nb_model = setNames(d$std_nb_model, k), interventions_avoided = setNames(d$interventions_avoided, k), observed_event_risk = setNames(d$observed_event_risk, k), positive_rate = setNames(d$positive_rate, k))
  }
  # Evaluate all B replicates, in parallel when the backend is available.
  replicates <- if (DCA_USE_PARALLEL) {
    future.apply::future_lapply(bootstrap_indices, one_replicate, future.seed = TRUE)
  } else {
    lapply(bootstrap_indices, one_replicate)
  }
  # Extract one field across all replicates as a matrix with rows aligned to
  # point_key and one column per bootstrap replicate; guard the degenerate
  # case of a single grid point where sapply would drop the dimension.
  pull_matrix <- function(field) {
    m <- sapply(replicates, function(z) z[[field]][point_key])
    if (is.null(dim(m))) m <- matrix(m, nrow = length(point_key))
    m
  }
  nb_model_boot <- pull_matrix("nb_model")
  nb_all_boot <- pull_matrix("nb_treat_all")
  std_model_boot <- pull_matrix("std_nb_model")
  avoided_boot <- pull_matrix("interventions_avoided")
  event_boot <- pull_matrix("observed_event_risk")
  positive_boot <- pull_matrix("positive_rate")
  # Row-wise percentile of the bootstrap distribution -> CI bounds.
  qrow <- function(m, probability) apply(m, 1, quantile, probs = probability, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  # Assemble the output table: point estimates plus 2.5%/97.5% percentile CIs.
  out <- data.frame(
    model_id = model_id, model_label = model_label, outcome = block$risk,
    prediction_scale = prediction_scale,
    # Name of the observed-risk estimator, for traceability.
    observed_method = ifelse(block$risk == "readmission", "Aalen-Johansen", "Kaplan-Meier"),
    horizon = point_results$horizon, threshold = point_results$threshold, n = point_results$n_obs,
    # Focus window: thresholds within [0.5x, 2x] the observed event risk,
    # i.e. the clinically plausible range around the outcome prevalence.
    in_focus = point_results$threshold >= 0.5 * point_results$observed_event_risk & point_results$threshold <= 2 * point_results$observed_event_risk,
    event_risk = point_results$observed_event_risk,
    event_risk_lo = qrow(event_boot, 0.025), event_risk_hi = qrow(event_boot, 0.975),
    positive_rate = point_results$positive_rate,
    positive_rate_lo = qrow(positive_boot, 0.025), positive_rate_hi = qrow(positive_boot, 0.975),
    # Net benefit of the model and of the treat-all strategy; treat-none is 0 by definition.
    nb_model = point_results$nb_model,
    nb_model_lo = qrow(nb_model_boot, 0.025), nb_model_hi = qrow(nb_model_boot, 0.975),
    nb_treat_all = point_results$nb_treat_all,
    nb_treat_all_lo = qrow(nb_all_boot, 0.025), nb_treat_all_hi = qrow(nb_all_boot, 0.975),
    nb_treat_none = 0,
    # Standardized net benefit (net benefit divided by observed event risk).
    std_nb_model = point_results$std_nb_model,
    std_nb_model_lo = qrow(std_model_boot, 0.025), std_nb_model_hi = qrow(std_model_boot, 0.975),
    # Per-1,000-patient scalings for clinical interpretability.
    net_cases_per1000 = point_results$nb_model * 1000,
    net_cases_per1000_lo = qrow(nb_model_boot, 0.025) * 1000,
    net_cases_per1000_hi = qrow(nb_model_boot, 0.975) * 1000,
    # interventions_avoided is expressed per 100 patients by convention; x10 -> per 1,000.
    avoided_per1000 = point_results$interventions_avoided * 10,
    avoided_per1000_lo = qrow(avoided_boot, 0.025) * 10,
    avoided_per1000_hi = qrow(avoided_boot, 0.975) * 10,
    B = B,
    # Number of bootstrap replicates yielding a finite nb_model for this grid point.
    B_valid = rowSums(is.finite(nb_model_boot)),
    seed = seed, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  message(sprintf("Completed %s: %d threshold-horizon combinations.", model_label, nrow(out)))
  out
}

.t0 <- Sys.time()
# PAIRED difference in net benefit between specifications, with its own bootstrap interval.
# WHY THIS EXISTS: the DCA figure reports one interval per arm, around that arm's own estimate.
# Overlapping intervals do NOT establish equivalence. Each arm's interval carries the difficulty
# of the resampled cohort, which is shared by every arm and cancels in the difference, so the
# interval on the difference is much narrower than the overlap of two marginal intervals suggests.
# Claiming two specifications perform alike requires estimating the DIFFERENCE and its uncertainty,
# which is what this chunk does and what the existing output does not contain.
# WHY PAIRING IS VALID HERE: .dca_boot_one_arm() calls set.seed(DCA_BOOT_SEED) inside each arm and
# then sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE). Same seed, same n across arms, so every arm was already
# scored on identical resamples. What is missing is only that the per-replicate values were not
# retained, so they are recomputed here with the very same indices.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
stopifnot(exists(".compute_replicate_curves"), exists("readmit_netrisk_pool"),
          exists("readmit_cif_fullph_pool"), exists("readmit_cif_shap_pool"),
          exists("death_fullph_pool"), exists("death_shap_pool"),
          exists("DCA_BOOT_B"), exists("DCA_BOOT_SEED"), exists("DCA_BOOT_HORIZONS"))
# Full run only: no reduced mode. Narrow the grids below if the cost is prohibitive, but narrow
# them deliberately and say so, because the reported contrast is grid-specific.
NB_PAIR_B <- DCA_BOOT_B
NB_PAIR_SEED <- DCA_BOOT_SEED
NB_PAIR_HORIZONS <- DCA_BOOT_HORIZONS
stopifnot(NB_PAIR_B >= 1000L)
# PARALLEL PLAN. The mother cell holdout-dca-bootstrap-per1000-2 ends with
# future::plan(future::sequential), which tears the workers down while leaving DCA_USE_PARALLEL
# set to TRUE. Calling future_lapply() in that state runs SERIALLY without any warning, so the
# plan is re-established here and torn down again at the end. The sequential setup strategy and
# the long connect timeout are the same guards the mother cell uses, because worker startup is
# unreliable on Drive-synced paths.
NB_PAIR_PARALLEL <- isTRUE(DCA_USE_PARALLEL)
NB_PAIR_WORKERS <- 0L
if (NB_PAIR_PARALLEL) {
  options(parallelly.makeNodePSOCK.setup_strategy = "sequential")
  options(parallelly.makeNodePSOCK.connectTimeout = 600)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 10 * 1024^3)
  NB_PAIR_WORKERS <- min(16, max(1L, parallelly::availableCores() %/% 2L))
  NB_PAIR_PARALLEL <- tryCatch({ future::plan(future::multisession, workers = NB_PAIR_WORKERS); TRUE },
    error = function(e) { message("Parallel plan failed, running serially: ", conditionMessage(e))
                          future::plan(future::sequential); FALSE })
}
message("Paired net-benefit workers: ", if (NB_PAIR_PARALLEL) NB_PAIR_WORKERS else 0L)
# Arms, grouped by outcome. Only arms sharing an outcome, an observed-side method and a threshold
# grid may be differenced: a readmission arm and a mortality arm have different event definitions
# and different threshold scales, so a difference between them would have no interpretation.
nb_arms <- list(
  readmission = list(method = "aalen-johansen", thresholds = DCA_THR_READMISSION,
    blocks = list("net risk" = readmit_netrisk_pool,
                  "CIF, all predictors" = readmit_cif_fullph_pool,
                  "CIF, SHAP-informed" = readmit_cif_shap_pool)),
  mortality = list(method = "km", thresholds = DCA_THR_MORTALITY,
    blocks = list("all predictors" = death_fullph_pool,
                  "SHAP-informed" = death_shap_pool)))
# Recompute the curve set for one arm across all resamples, retaining every replicate. The index
# list is rebuilt from the same seed and the same n, so it reproduces what .dca_boot_one_arm() used.
nb_replicate_matrix <- function(block, thresholds, horizons, method, B, seed, label) {
  n <- nrow(block$pred_risk)
  set.seed(seed)
  idx <- lapply(seq_len(B), function(i) sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE))
  pt <- .compute_replicate_curves(block, thresholds, horizons, readmit_method = method)
  key <- paste(pt$horizon, pt$threshold, sep = "_")
  one <- function(index) {
    if (!exists(".compute_replicate_curves", mode = "function")) {
      suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival)); source(DCA_ADCA_SOURCE)
    }
    b <- block
    b$pred_risk <- b$pred_risk[index, , drop = FALSE]
    b$time <- b$time[index]; b$event <- b$event[index]
    if (!is.null(b$cr_ftime)) b$cr_ftime <- b$cr_ftime[index]
    if (!is.null(b$cr_fstatus)) b$cr_fstatus <- b$cr_fstatus[index]
    d <- .compute_replicate_curves(b, thresholds, horizons, readmit_method = method)
    stats::setNames(d$nb_model, paste(d$horizon, d$threshold, sep = "_"))[key]
  }
  message(sprintf("  net-benefit replicates: %s (n = %d, B = %d)", label, n, B))
  reps <- if (NB_PAIR_PARALLEL) future.apply::future_lapply(idx, one, future.seed = TRUE) else lapply(idx, one)
  m <- sapply(reps, identity)
  if (is.null(dim(m))) m <- matrix(m, nrow = length(key))
  list(point = stats::setNames(pt$nb_model, key), reps = m, key = key,
       horizon = pt$horizon, threshold = pt$threshold, n = n)
}
nb_pair_rows <- list()
# Keep every outcome's replicate matrices instead of letting the loop overwrite them. Without this
# accumulator only the last outcome survives, which is how the readmission replicates from the
# first long run were lost.
nb_replicates_all <- list()
for (oc in names(nb_arms)) {
  cfg <- nb_arms[[oc]]
  message(sprintf("== %s: %d arms, %d thresholds, %d horizons ==", oc, length(cfg$blocks),
                  length(cfg$thresholds), length(NB_PAIR_HORIZONS)))
  mats <- lapply(names(cfg$blocks), function(nm)
    nb_replicate_matrix(cfg$blocks[[nm]], cfg$thresholds, NB_PAIR_HORIZONS, cfg$method,
                        NB_PAIR_B, NB_PAIR_SEED, paste(oc, nm, sep = " / ")))
  names(mats) <- names(cfg$blocks)
  # store replicate matrices
  nb_replicates_all[[oc]] <- mats
  # Every arm must share the same horizon-threshold key, otherwise the rows being differenced
  # would not correspond to the same decision point.
  for (nm in names(mats)) stopifnot(identical(mats[[nm]]$key, mats[[1]]$key))
  for (pr in utils::combn(names(mats), 2L, simplify = FALSE)) {
    A <- mats[[pr[1]]]; Z <- mats[[pr[2]]]
    d <- A$reps - Z$reps
    # Replicates can fail where a threshold leaves too few patients above it for the observed risk
    # to be estimable. na.rm = TRUE would then quietly build the interval from a biased subset, so
    # the count is carried and low-validity rows are blanked, mirroring the mother cell's B_valid guard.
    n_valid <- rowSums(is.finite(d))
    lo <- apply(d, 1, stats::quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    hi <- apply(d, 1, stats::quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
    lo[n_valid < 0.9 * NB_PAIR_B] <- NA_real_; hi[n_valid < 0.9 * NB_PAIR_B] <- NA_real_
    nb_pair_rows[[length(nb_pair_rows) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
      outcome = oc, arm_A = pr[1], arm_B = pr[2],
      horizon = A$horizon, threshold = A$threshold,
      nb_A_per1000 = 1000 * A$point, nb_B_per1000 = 1000 * Z$point,
      delta_nb_per1000 = 1000 * (A$point - Z$point),
      delta_lo_per1000 = 1000 * lo, delta_hi_per1000 = 1000 * hi,
      excludes_zero = (lo > 0 | hi < 0), B_valid = n_valid,
      pct_reps_A_better = rowMeans(d > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  }
}
dca_paired_nb <- do.call(rbind, nb_pair_rows)
rownames(dca_paired_nb) <- NULL

tnr <- "Times New Roman"

plot_ipeval_epi <- function(ipeval_res, tnr = "Times New Roman") {
  p <- ipeval_res$pooled
  mk <- function(m, lab) data.frame(
    risk = p$risk, model = p$model, horizon = p$horizon, metric = lab,
    value = p[[paste0(m, "_mean")]],
    lower = p[[paste0(m, "_lower_mean")]], upper = p[[paste0(m, "_upper_mean")]],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  long <- rbind(mk("auc", "AUC(t)"), mk("brier", "Brier(t)"))
  lab_map <- c("readmit::best_perf1" = "Readmission (shared)",
               "death::best_perf1"   = "Mortality best_perf1 (Full PH)",
               "death::best_perf2"   = "Mortality best_perf2 (SHAP)")
  long$model_lab <- factor(unname(lab_map[long$model]), levels = unname(lab_map))
  long$metric    <- factor(long$metric, levels = c("AUC(t)", "Brier(t)"))
  long <- long[order(long$model_lab, long$horizon), ]   # ensure lines connect correctly
  pd <- position_dodge(width = 2.5)
  href <- data.frame(metric = factor("AUC(t)", levels = levels(long$metric)),
                     y = 0.5)                          # chance line
  cols <- c("Readmission (shared)"           = "#2166AC",
            "Mortality best_perf1 (Full PH)" = "#B2182B",
            "Mortality best_perf2 (SHAP)"    = "#E08214") #best_perf2
  ggplot2::ggplot(long, ggplot2::aes(horizon, value, color = model_lab, fill = model_lab, group = model_lab)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(data = href, ggplot2::aes(yintercept = y),
                        linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), alpha = 0.15, color = NA, position = pd) +

    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = cols) + ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = cols) +

.combine_c_ibs_dualscore <- function(cidx_tab, ibs_df, which_risk) {
  ci_lp   <- .fmt_cidx(cidx_tab, "lp")
  ci_risk <- .fmt_cidx(cidx_tab, "risk")
  d   <- ibs_df[ibs_df$risk == which_risk & is.finite(ibs_df$mean), ]
  nul <- attr(ibs_df, "null"); nul <- nul[nul$risk == which_risk & is.finite(nul$mean), ]
  fmt <- function(p, l, h) sprintf("%.4f (%.4f, %.4f)", p, l, h)
  ib  <- setNames(fmt(d$point, d$q025, d$q975),       as.character(d$horizon))
  i0  <- setNames(fmt(nul$point, nul$q025, nul$q975), as.character(nul$horizon))
  sk  <- setNames(sprintf("%.3f", 1 - d$point / nul$point), as.character(d$horizon))
  ib["Global"] <- ib["60"]; i0["Global"] <- i0["60"]; sk["Global"] <- sk["60"]
  ord <- c("6", "12", "36", "60", "Global")
  data.frame(Horizon = ord,
             `Uno's C, lp (95% CI)`   = unname(ci_lp[ord]),
             `Uno's C, risk (95% CI)` = unname(ci_risk[ord]),
             `IBS (95% CI)`      = unname(ib[ord]),
             `IBS null (95% CI)` = unname(i0[ord]),
             `IBS skill`         = unname(sk[ord]),
             check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

ici_epi_table <- function(ici_boot, digits = 4) {
  d <- as.data.frame(ici_boot)
  f <- function(e, l, h) ifelse(is.na(e), "\u2014",
        sprintf("%.*f (%.*f, %.*f)", digits, e, digits, l, digits, h))
  out <- data.frame(
    Outcome = ifelse(d$risk == "readmission", "Readmission", "Mortality"),
    Model = dplyr::recode(d$model,
      "readmit::bp1_cif" = "Readmission: Cum. incidence, all-predictors",
      "readmit::bp2_cif" = "Readmission: Cum. incidence, SHAP-informed",
      "readmit::netrisk" = "Readmission: net risk",

      "death::best_perf2" = "Mortality: ML/SHAP-informed"),

.browsable_grouped <- function(df, group_col, body_cols, header_labels, caption, footnote,
                               font = "'Times New Roman', serif") {
  th <- sprintf("position:sticky;top:0;background:#f3f3f3;border-bottom:2px solid #ccc;padding:6px 10px;text-align:center;white-space:nowrap;font-weight:bold;")
  td <- "border-bottom:1px solid #eee;padding:4px 10px;white-space:nowrap;"
  gh <- "background:#e8eef5;font-weight:bold;padding:5px 10px;border-bottom:1px solid #ccc;"
  header <- htmltools::tags$thead(htmltools::tags$tr(
    lapply(header_labels, function(nm) htmltools::tags$th(style = th, nm))))
  groups <- split(df, factor(df[[group_col]], levels = unique(df[[group_col]])))
  rows <- list()
  for (g in names(groups)) {
    rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- htmltools::tags$tr(
      htmltools::tags$td(colspan = length(body_cols), style = gh, g))
    gd <- groups[[g]]
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(gd)))
      rows[[length(rows) + 1L]] <- htmltools::tags$tr(lapply(seq_along(body_cols), function(j)
        htmltools::tags$td(style = paste0(td, "text-align:", if (j == 1) "left" else "center", ";"),
                           as.character(gd[i, body_cols[j]]))))
  }
  htmltools::browsable(htmltools::tags$div(
    htmltools::tags$div(style = paste0("font-weight:bold;margin-bottom:6px;font-family:", font, ";"), caption),
    htmltools::tags$div(style = paste0("max-height:550px;overflow:auto;border:1px solid #ddd;font-family:", font, ";font-size:13px;"),
      htmltools::tags$table(style = "border-collapse:collapse;width:max-content;min-width:100%;",
        header, htmltools::tags$tbody(rows))),
    htmltools::tags$div(style = paste0("font-size:11px;color:#555;margin-top:6px;max-width:780px;font-family:", font, ";"), footnote)))
}

                                                eo  = "Expected:Observed\nratio (E:O)")) {
  d <- as.data.frame(ici_boot)
  mk <- function(m) data.frame(risk = d$risk, model = d$model, horizon = d$horizon, metric = m,
    value = d[[m]], lower = d[[paste0(m, "_lo")]], upper = d[[paste0(m, "_hi")]])
  long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(metric_titles), mk))
  long$outcome <- factor(ifelse(long$risk == "readmission", "Readmission", "Mortality"),
                         levels = c("Readmission", "Mortality"))
  long$model_lab <- factor(dplyr::case_when(
    long$model == "readmit::netrisk"  ~ "Readmission:\nNet risk",
    long$model == "readmit::bp1_cif"  ~ "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nall predictors",
    long$model == "readmit::bp2_cif"  ~ "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nSHAP-informed",
    long$model == "death::best_perf1" ~ "Mortality:\nAll predictors",
    long$model == "death::best_perf2" ~ "Mortality:\nSHAP-informed",
    TRUE ~ long$model),
    levels = c("Readmission:\nNet risk",
               "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nall predictors",
               "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nSHAP-informed",
               "Mortality:\nAll predictors",
               "Mortality:\nSHAP-informed"))
  cols <- c("Readmission:\nNet risk" = "#9ECAE1",
            "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nall predictors" = "#4292C6",
            "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nSHAP-informed" = "#08519C",
            "Mortality:\nAll predictors" = "#B2182B",
            "Mortality:\nSHAP-informed" = "#E08214")
  shp  <- c("Readmission:\nNet risk" = 21,
            "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nall predictors" = 23,
            "Readmission:\nCum. incidence\nSHAP-informed" = 25,
            "Mortality:\nAll predictors" = 24,
            "Mortality:\nSHAP-informed" = 22)
  theme_epi <- theme_classic(base_size = 13, base_family = tnr) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank(), legend.key.width = unit(1.5, "lines"),
          strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
          panel.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines"), plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, family = tnr))
  mk_panel <- function(m, ytitle, ref = NA_real_, show_x = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE, expand0 = FALSE) {
    dd <- long[long$metric == m, ]
    dd <- dd[order(dd$model_lab, dd$horizon), ]
    pd <- position_dodge(width = 2.5)
    g <- ggplot(dd, aes(horizon, value, color = model_lab, shape = model_lab, group = model_lab))
    if (is.finite(ref)) g <- g + geom_hline(yintercept = ref, linetype = "22", color = "grey45", linewidth = 0.4)
    g <- g + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 1.2, linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.85, position = pd) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.9, position = pd) + geom_point(size = 2.5, fill = "white", stroke = 0.9, position = pd) +
      facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_color_manual(values = cols, drop = FALSE) + scale_shape_manual(values = shp, drop = FALSE) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(6, 12, 36, 60)) + labs(x = "Months since discharge", y = ytitle) + theme_epi
    if (expand0) g <- g + expand_limits(y = 0)
    if (!show_strip) g <- g + theme(strip.text = element_blank())
    if (!show_x) g <- g + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    g
  }
  pA <- mk_panel("ici", metric_titles["ici"], show_x = FALSE, show_strip = TRUE,  expand0 = TRUE)
  pB <- mk_panel("ece", metric_titles["ece"], show_x = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE, expand0 = TRUE)
  pC <- mk_panel("eo",  metric_titles["eo"],  ref = 1, show_x = TRUE, show_strip = FALSE)
  (pA / pB / pC) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank(), legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "lines"),
          legend.justification = c(0, 0), legend.box.just = "left", strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.text = element_text(color = "black"),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey92", linewidth = 0.3),
          panel.spacing = unit(0.7, "lines"), plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, family = tnr))
  mk_panel <- function(m, ytitle, show_x = FALSE, show_strip = FALSE) {
    dd <- long[long$metric == m, ]
    g <- ggplot(dd, aes(horizon, value, color = model_lab, shape = model_lab, group = model_lab)) +
      geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 2, linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.85, position = pd) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.7, alpha = 0.9, position = pd) +
      geom_point(size = 2.5, fill = "white", stroke = 0.9, position = pd) +
      facet_wrap(~ outcome, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_color_manual(values = cols, drop = FALSE) + scale_shape_manual(values = shp, drop = FALSE) +
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(6, 12, 36, 60)) + expand_limits(y = 0) +
      labs(x = "Meses desde el egreso", y = ytitle) + theme_epi
    if (!show_strip) g <- g + theme(strip.text = element_blank())
    if (!show_x) g <- g + theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
    g
  }
  ms <- names(metric_titles); nM <- length(ms)
  panels <- lapply(seq_along(ms), function(k)
    mk_panel(ms[k], metric_titles[ms[k]], show_x = (k == nM), show_strip = (k == 1)))
  patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 1) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# This chunk estimates absolute patient-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals for both competing-risk readmission CIF systems.
# BP1 combines the shared readmission model with the primary Full PH mortality model.
# BP2 combines the shared readmission model with the parsimonious SHAP mortality model.
# Both arms use the same bootstrap seed and therefore the same patient resamples.
# The fitted Cox models and individual predictions remain frozen throughout the bootstrap.

IBS_CIF_SEED <- 2125L

IBS_CIF_ARMS <- list(`readmit::bp1_cif` = results_boot_val_bp1_cif, `readmit::bp2_cif` = results_boot_val_bp2_cif)
.run_absolute_cif_ibs <- function(results_object, model_label) {
message(sprintf("Running absolute CIF-based readmission IBS bootstrap for %s with B = %d and seed = %d.", model_label, IBS_CIF_B, IBS_CIF_SEED))
all_results <- ibs_window_bootstrap_core(results_object, B = IBS_CIF_B, seed = IBS_CIF_SEED, eval_times = IBS_CIF_GRID, readmit_method = "aalen-johansen", compute_null = FALSE, verbose = TRUE)
out <- all_results[all_results$risk == "readmission" & all_results$horizon %in% IBS_CIF_HORIZONS, c("risk", "horizon", "point", "mean", "q025", "q975")]
out <- out[match(IBS_CIF_HORIZONS, out$horizon), ]
stopifnot(nrow(out) == length(IBS_CIF_HORIZONS))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(out[c("point", "mean", "q025", "q975")]))))
out$bootstrap_bias <- out$mean - out$point
out$B <- IBS_CIF_B
out$seed <- IBS_CIF_SEED
out$model <- model_label
out$estimand <- "Competing-risk IBS based on the predicted CIF with death treated as a competing event"
out[c("model", "estimand", "horizon", "point", "q025", "q975", "mean", "bootstrap_bias", "B", "seed")]
}

ref_bp2$model <- "readmit::bp2_cif"

stopifnot(max_abs_difference < 1e-10)
}
}

# Brier skill = 1 - IBS_model / IBS_null, with the null being the intercept-only marginal
# curve estimated on TRAIN and broadcast to every validation row, scored with exactly the
# same weights, grid and integral. Model and null share every bootstrap resample, so the
# difficulty of the resampled cohort moves both terms together and cancels in the ratio.
# The readmission null follows the estimand: a competing-risk model must be compared
# against a competing-risk null (1 - Aalen-Johansen CIF), not against a Kaplan-Meier one.
stopifnot(exists("ibs_cl_netrisk"), exists("ibs_cl_cif_bp1"), exists("ibs_cl_cif_bp2"))
cat("Fitting the two mortality models on the fine grid\n")
death_fine_bp1 <- fit_death_grid_predictions(models$best_perf1$death, train_list, val_list, classical_grid, expected_strata = 10L)
death_fine_bp2 <- fit_death_grid_predictions(models$best_perf2$death, train_list, val_list, classical_grid, expected_strata = 10L)
ibs_cl_death_bp1 <- ibs_classical_point(death_fine_bp1, horizons = CLASSICAL_HORIZONS)
ibs_cl_death_bp2 <- ibs_classical_point(death_fine_bp2, horizons = CLASSICAL_HORIZONS)
# Nulls, one per arm, each on its own estimand.
null_readmit_aj <- ibs_classical_null(netrisk_fine, CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, outcome = "readmit", method = "aalen-johansen")
null_death_bp1  <- ibs_classical_null(death_fine_bp1, CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, outcome = "death")
null_death_bp2  <- ibs_classical_null(death_fine_bp2, CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, outcome = "death")
skill_all <- rbind(
  ibs_classical_skill_boot(ibs_cl_netrisk,   null_readmit_aj, B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED, label = "readmit::netrisk"),
  ibs_classical_skill_boot(ibs_cl_cif_bp1,   null_readmit_aj, B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED, label = "readmit::bp1_cif"),
  ibs_classical_skill_boot(ibs_cl_cif_bp2,   null_readmit_aj, B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED, label = "readmit::bp2_cif"),
  ibs_classical_skill_boot(ibs_cl_death_bp1, null_death_bp1,  B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED, label = "death::best_perf1"),
  ibs_classical_skill_boot(ibs_cl_death_bp2, null_death_bp2,  B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED, label = "death::best_perf2"))

# Risk-based Uno's C and its skill. READ THE CAVEAT: unlike the Brier skill, the C null is
# NOT estimated from data. A constant marker ties every pair, so concordance is exactly 0.5
# by construction and the skill collapses to (C - 0.5) / 0.5 = 2C - 1, which is Somers' D,
# a deterministic rescaling of C. uno_c_risk_skill() computes the null empirically rather
# than assuming it, so the uno_c_null column can be inspected: if it is not 0.5 the
# assumption is wrong and the skill column must be discarded.
h_idx <- match(CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, classical_grid)
c_skill_all <- rbind(
  uno_c_risk_skill(netrisk_fine$rt_val, netrisk_fine$re_val, 1 - netrisk_fine$S[, h_idx, drop = FALSE],
                   CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, label = "readmit::netrisk", B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED),
  uno_c_risk_skill(cif_fine_bp1$rt_val, cif_fine_bp1$re_val, 1 - cif_fine_bp1$S[, h_idx, drop = FALSE],
                   CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, label = "readmit::bp1_cif", B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED),
  uno_c_risk_skill(cif_fine_bp2$rt_val, cif_fine_bp2$re_val, 1 - cif_fine_bp2$S[, h_idx, drop = FALSE],
                   CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, label = "readmit::bp2_cif", B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED),
  uno_c_risk_skill(death_fine_bp1$y_test$time, death_fine_bp1$y_test$event, 1 - death_fine_bp1$S[, h_idx, drop = FALSE],
                   CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, label = "death::best_perf1", B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED),
  uno_c_risk_skill(death_fine_bp2$y_test$time, death_fine_bp2$y_test$event, 1 - death_fine_bp2$S[, h_idx, drop = FALSE],
                   CLASSICAL_HORIZONS, label = "death::best_perf2", B = CLASSICAL_B, seed = CLASSICAL_SEED))
stopifnot(all(abs(c_skill_all$uno_c_null - 0.5) < 1e-8 | is.na(c_skill_all$uno_c_null)))
utils::write.csv(skill_all, file.path(out_dir, "holdout_classical_ibs_skill_five_arms.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(c_skill_all, file.path(out_dir, "holdout_classical_unoc_skill_five_arms.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Helper to render an HTML table with grouped rows.
# - body: data frame of values to display
# - outcome: grouping vector (e.g., "Readmission" / "Mortality")
# - caption: optional table caption
# - note: optional footnote below the table
threshold_browsable <- function(body, outcome, caption = NULL, note = NULL) {
  # Pull htmltools functions into the local namespace for brevity.
  tags <- htmltools::tags
  HTML <- htmltools::HTML
  tagList <- htmltools::tagList
  browsable <- htmltools::browsable
  # Generate a unique CSS class so multiple tables on the same page do not clash.
  cls <- paste0("thr-table-", as.integer(runif(1, 1e6, 9e6)))
  ncols <- ncol(body)
  # Build table rows as a list: one group header per outcome, then its rows.
  rows <- list()
  k <- 1L
  for (g in unique(outcome)) {
    # Rows belonging to this outcome group.
    idx <- which(outcome == g)
    # Add a bold spanning group header row.
    rows[[k]] <- tags$tr(
      class = "group-row",
      tags$td(colspan = ncols, g)
    )
    k <- k + 1L
    # Add each data row for the current group.
    for (i in idx) {
      rows[[k]] <- tags$tr(
        lapply(seq_len(ncols), function(j) {
          # Align column 1 left, columns 2-3 right, and the rest centered.
          al <- if (j == 1) "left" else if (j %in% c(2, 3)) "right" else "center"
          tags$td(style = paste0("text-align:", al, ";"), body[i, j, drop = TRUE])
        })
      )
      k <- k + 1L
    }
  }
  # Return a browsable HTML tagList with inline CSS and the table structure.
  browsable(tagList(
    tags$style(HTML(sprintf("
      .%s {
        border-collapse: collapse;
        margin: 0 auto;
        font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;
        font-size: 12px;
        line-height: 1.25;
      }
      .%s caption {
        caption-side: top;
        font-weight: bold;
        margin-bottom: 8px;
      }
      .%s th, .%s td {
        border-bottom: 1px solid #dddddd;
        padding: 4px 8px;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .%s th {
        border-bottom: 2px solid #777777;
        font-weight: bold;
      }
      .%s tbody tr:nth-child(even):not(.group-row) {
        background-color: #fafafa;
      }
      .%s tbody tr:not(.group-row):hover {
        background-color: #f3f6fb;
      }
      .%s .group-row td {
        background-color: #f3f3f3;
        font-weight: bold;
        text-align: left;
        border-top: 1px solid #bbbbbb;
      }
      .%s-note {
        max-width: 900px;
        margin: 8px auto 0 auto;
        font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif;
        font-size: 11px;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }
    ", cls, cls, cls, cls, cls, cls, cls, cls, cls))),
    tags$table(
      class = cls,
      if (!is.null(caption)) tags$caption(caption),
      tags$thead(tags$tr(lapply(names(body), tags$th))),
      tags$tbody(rows)
    ),
    if (!is.null(note)) tags$div(class = paste0(cls, "-note"), note)
  ))
}

# Prepare a tidy table of threshold metrics from a bootstrap thresholds object.
# - thr: threshold object, coerced to a data frame
# - digits: number of decimals for metrics and CI bounds
# - metrics: which metrics to include (Sens, Spec, PPV, NPV)

threshold_epi_table <- function(thr, digits = 2, metrics = c("Sens","Spec","PPV","NPV")) {
  d <- as.data.frame(thr)
  d <- d[order(factor(ifelse(d$risk=="readmission","Readmission","Mortality"), c("Readmission","Mortality")),
               d$model, d$horizon, d$threshold), ]
  f <- function(m) ifelse(is.na(d[[m]]), "\u2014",
        sprintf("%.*f (%.*f, %.*f)", digits, unname(d[[m]]),
                digits, unname(d[[paste0(m,"_lo")]]), digits, unname(d[[paste0(m,"_hi")]])))
  nm <- c(Sens="Sensitivity", Spec="Specificity", PPV="PPV", NPV="NPV")
  out <- data.frame(
    Outcome = ifelse(d$risk=="readmission","Readmission","Mortality"),
    Model = dplyr::recode(d$model, 
      "readmit::bp1_cif" = "Readmission: Cum. incidence, all-predictors",
      "readmit::bp2_cif" = "Readmission: Cum. incidence, SHAP-informed",
      "readmit::netrisk" = "Readmission: net risk",      
      "death::best_perf1" = "Mortality: all predictors",
      "death::best_perf2" = "Mortality: ML/SHAP-informed"),
    Horizon = d$horizon, Threshold = sprintf("%g%%", 100*d$threshold),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (m in metrics) out[[nm[m]]] <- f(m)
  list(tab = out, grp = table(factor(out$Outcome, levels = unique(out$Outcome))))
}

Predicted risk = 1-S(t) (cause-specific Cox). Readmission: competing-risk IPCW (Aalen-Johansen-aware; deaths before t weighted as controls); mortality: standard IPCW (Kaplan-Meier). 95% CI from bootstrap resampling of the held-out set. Readmission model shared by both.

# Purpose: turn the three frozen Cox specifications already stored in `models` (readmit shared model,
# death best_perf1 = Full PH, death best_perf2 = SHAP) into an easy-to-read hazard-ratio table, AND
# pair each one with the risk carried by its strata, so nothing about the specification is left implicit.
# Coefficients: each specification is refit on every one of the 5 imputed TRAIN sets in `train_list`,
# then pooled across imputations with Rubin's rules via mice::pool() (Wald CI and p-value on the
# log-hazard scale with Barnard-Rubin adjusted degrees of freedom, then exponentiated to hazard ratios;
# the p-value is unchanged by that monotone transform, so it stays valid after exponentiation).
# Strata risk: strata() terms carry no coefficient by construction (survival::coxph() absorbs them into
# a stratum-specific baseline hazard, never a hazard ratio), so instead of a coefficient this chunk
# reports the cumulative RISK (1 - baseline survival) at 6/12/36/60 months for every combined stratum
# level, reusing tab_readmit / tab_death1 / tab_death2 already computed by bh_table() in
# holdout-baseline-stratum -- no baseline-hazard logic is duplicated here.
# CAVEAT (state this in the text if reported): that risk is for the REFERENCE covariate profile (all
# covariates at 0), because bh_table() calls basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE). It is NOT the average or
# marginal risk of patients in that stratum; it isolates the between-stratum shift in the baseline
# hazard so the strata's contribution to risk is visible on its own, separately from the covariate HRs.
# WHERE TO PASTE: right after the cell labelled holdout-baseline-stratum and before
# holdout-cindex-ibs-global. Replaces the holdout-coef-hr-table chunk pasted before holdout-cindex-ibs-run.
# REQUIRES already in the kernel: `train_list`, `models` (holdout-define-models) and
# `tab_readmit`, `tab_death1`, `tab_death2` (holdout-baseline-stratum). Stops with a clear message if
# mice is missing; installs nothing.
stopifnot(exists("train_list"), exists("models"), exists("tab_readmit"), exists("tab_death1"), exists("tab_death2"))
if (!requireNamespace("mice", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'mice' is required to pool coefficients across imputations with Rubin's rules.", call. = FALSE)
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(survival)
  library(mice)
})
# Extract the strata() variable names from a formula. Same regex as bh_table() in holdout-baseline-stratum,
# so the two cells always agree on what counts as a stratifying variable versus an estimated covariate.
.extract_strata_vars <- function(f) {
  tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels")
  gsub("^strata\\(|\\)$", "", tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)])
}
# Fit one Cox specification on every imputed TRAIN set, pool the coefficients across the 5 imputations
# with Rubin's rules, and return one tidy row per covariate: hazard ratio, 95% CI, pooled Wald p-value.
# Defensive check: if a term named like "strata(...)" ever shows up here, strata() was fit as a plain
# covariate instead of a stratum -- the exact regression class already documented for this project.
# p-value formatting follows the project convention: never scientific notation, "<0.001" below that bound.
.pool_hr_table <- function(f, train_list) {
  fits <- lapply(train_list, function(d) survival::coxph(f, data = d))
  pooled <- summary(mice::pool(mice::as.mira(fits)), conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
  stopifnot(!any(grepl("strata\\(", pooled$term)))
  p_fmt <- ifelse(pooled$p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(pooled$p.value, format = "f", digits = 3))
  data.frame(
    Variable = pooled$term,
    HR = sprintf("%.2f", pooled$estimate),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", pooled[["2.5 %"]], pooled[["97.5 %"]]),
    `p-value` = p_fmt,
    check.names = FALSE)
}
# Turn one bh_table() output (stratum, n, events, H0_*, S0_*) into a readable RISK table: for each
# horizon, Risk = 1 - S0, reported as a percentage. n and events are the across-imputation means that
# bh_table() already rounded, so they are passed through unchanged.
.risk_from_bh_table <- function(tab) {
  s0_cols <- grep("^S0_", names(tab), value = TRUE)
  risk <- tab[, c("stratum", "n", "events")]
  for (col in s0_cols) {
    risk[[sub("^S0_", "Risk_", col)]] <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - tab[[col]]))
  }
  risk
}
# Build the three HR tables. Readmission uses the SAME specification (f_readmit) for best_perf1 and
# best_perf2, so it is fit and pooled only once and reused for both.
hr_readmit <- .pool_hr_table(models$best_perf1$readmit, train_list)
hr_death_bp1 <- .pool_hr_table(models$best_perf1$death, train_list)
hr_death_bp2 <- .pool_hr_table(models$best_perf2$death, train_list)
# Build the three matching strata-risk tables from the already-computed baseline-hazard tables.
risk_readmit <- .risk_from_bh_table(tab_readmit)
risk_death_bp1 <- .risk_from_bh_table(tab_death1)
risk_death_bp2 <- .risk_from_bh_table(tab_death2)
# Sanity check: bh_table() must have found the same strata that this formula declares, or the risk
# table below silently does not correspond to the specification it is printed under.
stopifnot(length(.extract_strata_vars(models$best_perf1$readmit)) >= 1, length(.extract_strata_vars(models$best_perf1$death)) >= 1, length(.extract_strata_vars(models$best_perf2$death)) >= 1)
# Print: hazard-ratio table immediately followed by its strata-risk table, for each specification.
knitr::kable(hr_readmit, "markdown",
  caption = "Held-out pipeline, TRAIN (MI-pooled, m=5): hazard ratios, readmission (shared model)") |> print()
knitr::kable(risk_readmit, "markdown",
  caption = "Readmission: cumulative risk by stratum (reference covariate profile), MI-pooled") |> print()
knitr::kable(hr_death_bp1, "markdown",
  caption = "Held-out pipeline, TRAIN (MI-pooled, m=5): hazard ratios, death best_perf1 (Full PH)") |> print()
knitr::kable(risk_death_bp1, "markdown",
  caption = "Death best_perf1 (Full PH): cumulative risk by stratum (reference covariate profile), MI-pooled") |> print()
knitr::kable(hr_death_bp2, "markdown",
  caption = "Held-out pipeline, TRAIN (MI-pooled, m=5): hazard ratios, death best_perf2 (SHAP)") |> print()
knitr::kable(risk_death_bp2, "markdown",
  caption = "Death best_perf2 (SHAP): cumulative risk by stratum (reference covariate profile), MI-pooled") |> print()
cat("Note: strata risk is for the reference covariate profile (all covariates = 0), not the marginal risk of patients in that stratum; it isolates the between-stratum shift in baseline hazard.\n")

# Purpose: same three frozen Cox specifications as holdout-coef-hr-table, but REFIT on the held-out
# 20% (`val_list`) instead of the 80% TRAIN, plus the matching strata risk recomputed on the same 20%.
# WHERE TO PASTE: as a NEW cell right after the cell labelled holdout-coef-hr-table. It ADDS, it does
# not replace: the TRAIN version stays as the reportable model and this one is the replication check.
# REQUIRES already in the kernel: `val_list` (holdout-build-sets) and `models` (holdout-define-models).
# It deliberately does NOT reuse tab_readmit / tab_death1 / tab_death2, because those baselines were
# computed on TRAIN and must never be printed under coefficients estimated on VALIDATION; the strata
# risks below are rebuilt on val_list with the same Breslow + MI-mean math used by bh_table().
# WHAT CHANGES vs holdout-coef-hr-table: (1) every coxph() fit uses val_list; (2) the strata-risk
# tables are recomputed on val_list; (3) two guards TRAIN did not need are added, because n = 17,631
# makes sparse dummies and sparse strata a real possibility here: covariates that are constant in any
# validation imputation are reported before fitting, and terms whose coefficients come back NA
# (aliased / non-identified) are detected and removed BEFORE mice::pool(), since pooling is invalid
# when the term set differs across imputations; (4) the baseline evaluator uses findInterval() instead
# of approx(), which is the identical step function but survives a stratum with a single event time.
# INTERPRETATION (say this in the text): these hazard ratios are a REFIT on the held-out sample, so
# they are a replication / stability check of direction and magnitude, NOT the coefficients to report.
# The reportable coefficients remain the TRAIN-fit ones; estimating them on the test set spends the
# independence that makes the 20% a valid held-out sample.
stopifnot(exists("val_list"), exists("models"))
if (!requireNamespace("mice", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package 'mice' is required to pool coefficients across imputations with Rubin's rules.", call. = FALSE)
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(survival)
  library(mice)
})
# Switch: TRUE lets the cell drop non-identified terms and still produce a pooled table (every dropped
# term is listed in the console AND in the caption note); FALSE makes the cell stop instead, so the
# validation refit is never quietly a different specification than the TRAIN one.
VAL_REFIT_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE
# Term helpers: separate estimated covariates from strata() terms and rebuild a formula on a reduced
# covariate set while ALWAYS keeping every strata() term. Same regex convention as bh_table().
.terms_cov <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[!grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.terms_str <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.rebuild_formula <- function(f, keep) {
  rhs <- paste(c(keep, .terms_str(f)), collapse = " + ")
  stats::as.formula(paste(deparse(f[[2]], width.cutoff = 500L), "~", rhs), env = environment(f))
}
# Report covariates that carry no information in the 20%: absent column, or a single distinct value in
# at least one imputation (the usual cause of an aliased coefficient with a rare one-hot dummy).
.constant_covars <- function(f, dlist) {
  out <- character(0)
  for (v in .terms_cov(f)) {
    for (d in dlist) {
      x <- d[[v]]
      if (is.null(x)) { out <- c(out, paste0(v, " [absent]")); break }
      if (length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])) < 2L) { out <- c(out, paste0(v, " [constant]")); break }
    }
  }
  unique(out)
}
# Map coefficients back to model TERMS via coxph()$assign, so a factor family is judged as a whole and
# never half-dropped: a term is flagged only when ALL of its coefficients are NA in that imputation.
.na_terms <- function(fit) {
  cf <- stats::coef(fit)
  asg <- fit$assign
  if (is.null(names(asg))) names(asg) <- attr(fit$terms, "term.labels")[seq_along(asg)]
  names(asg)[vapply(asg, function(ix) all(is.na(cf[ix])), logical(1L))]
}
# Fit one specification on every imputed VALIDATION set, pool with Rubin's rules, return a tidy HR row
# per covariate. Adds a Flag column: an implausibly wide pooled CI on the HR scale is the fingerprint
# of a near-separated / sparse term in the smaller sample, and should not be read as a real effect.
.pool_hr_table_val <- function(f, dlist, label) {
  const <- .constant_covars(f, dlist)
  if (length(const)) message("[", label, "] no information in the 20%: ", paste(const, collapse = ", "))
  fits <- lapply(dlist, function(d) survival::coxph(f, data = d, model = TRUE))
  dropped <- unique(unlist(lapply(fits, .na_terms)))
  if (length(dropped)) {
    msg <- paste0("[", label, "] terms not identified in the validation refit: ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))
    if (!VAL_REFIT_DROP_MISSING_TERMS) stop(msg, " -- set VAL_REFIT_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE to drop them and pool the rest.", call. = FALSE)
    warning(msg, " -- dropped from the validation refit only; the TRAIN specification is unchanged.", call. = FALSE)
    f <- .rebuild_formula(f, setdiff(.terms_cov(f), dropped))
    fits <- lapply(dlist, function(d) survival::coxph(f, data = d, model = TRUE))
  }
  nm <- lapply(fits, function(fit) names(stats::coef(fit)))
  if (!all(vapply(nm, identical, logical(1L), nm[[1L]]))) {
    stop("[", label, "] coefficient names differ across validation imputations (an imputed factor lost a level); Rubin pooling would be invalid.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  pooled <- summary(mice::pool(mice::as.mira(fits)), conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
  stopifnot(!any(grepl("strata\\(", pooled$term)))
  lo <- pooled[["2.5 %"]]
  hi <- pooled[["97.5 %"]]
  p_fmt <- ifelse(pooled$p.value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(pooled$p.value, format = "f", digits = 3))
  data.frame(
    Variable = pooled$term,
    HR = sprintf("%.2f", pooled$estimate),
    `95% CI` = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", lo, hi),
    `p-value` = p_fmt,
    Flag = ifelse(!is.finite(hi / lo) | (hi / lo) > 100, "unstable (sparse in the 20%)", ""),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
# Hardened clone of bh_table() for the validation set. Identical math (Breslow H0 with
# centered = FALSE, last jump <= t, MI mean of H0), with two changes needed at n = 17,631:
# findInterval() instead of approx() (a stratum with one single event time no longer errors), and the
# UNION of strata across imputations instead of requiring an identical stratum set, averaging each
# stratum over the imputations where it exists and reporting any stratum that went missing.
.bh_table_val <- function(f, dlist, times = c(6, 12, 36, 60)) {
  sv <- gsub("^strata\\(|\\)$", "", .terms_str(f))
  status_var <- all.vars(f[[2]])[2L]
  per_imp <- lapply(dlist, function(d) {
    fit <- survival::coxph(f, data = d, model = TRUE)
    bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
    H <- vapply(split(bh[, c("time", "hazard")], bh$strata), function(z) {
      z <- z[order(z$time), ]
      idx <- findInterval(times, z$time)
      ifelse(idx == 0L, z$hazard[1L], z$hazard[pmax(idx, 1L)])
    }, numeric(length(times)))
    lab <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(sv, function(v) {
      x <- d[[v]]
      if (is.factor(x)) as.character(x) else paste0(v, "=", as.character(x))
    }), sep = ", "))
    list(H = H, n = table(lab), ev = tapply(d[[status_var]], lab, sum))
  })
  g <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(per_imp, function(x) colnames(x$H)))))
  gone <- unique(unlist(lapply(per_imp, function(x) setdiff(g, colnames(x$H)))))
  if (length(gone)) message("Strata absent from at least one validation imputation: ", paste(gone, collapse = " | "))
  grab <- function(x, gg) if (gg %in% colnames(x$H)) x$H[, gg] else rep(NA_real_, length(times))
  Hm <- sapply(g, function(gg) rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, grab, numeric(length(times)), gg = gg), na.rm = TRUE))
  pick <- function(x, gg, what) { v <- x[[what]][gg]; if (is.na(v)) 0 else as.numeric(v) }
  n_mean <- vapply(g, function(gg) mean(vapply(per_imp, pick, 0, gg = gg, what = "n")), 0)
  ev_mean <- vapply(g, function(gg) mean(vapply(per_imp, pick, 0, gg = gg, what = "ev")), 0)
  out <- data.frame(stratum = g, n = round(n_mean), events = round(ev_mean), check.names = FALSE)
  for (k in seq_along(times)) {
    out[[paste0("H0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(Hm[k, g], 4)
    out[[paste0("S0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(exp(-Hm[k, g]), 4)
  }
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}
# Same helper as in holdout-coef-hr-table: baseline survival per stratum turned into cumulative risk.
.risk_from_bh_table <- function(tab) {
  s0_cols <- grep("^S0_", names(tab), value = TRUE)
  risk <- tab[, c("stratum", "n", "events")]
  for (col in s0_cols) risk[[sub("^S0_", "Risk_", col)]] <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - tab[[col]]))
  risk
}
# Context before the tables: events per outcome in the 20% and events per estimated parameter, so the
# reader can see immediately whether the Full PH death model is even estimable in this sample.
.epv_line <- function(f, dlist, label) {
  sv <- all.vars(f[[2]])[2L]
  ev <- mean(vapply(dlist, function(d) sum(d[[sv]]), 0))
  k <- length(stats::coef(survival::coxph(f, data = dlist[[1L]], model = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("%-28s n = %d | events (MI mean) = %.0f | coefficients = %d | EPV = %.1f\n", label, nrow(dlist[[1L]]), ev, k, ev / k))
}

# Purpose: extend the center-level shared-frailty diagnostic already reported in the thesis for
# READMISSION (prediction25_multistate_semimarkov.ipynb, cell vce-compare: coxph(frailty(center_id))
# on ms$trans==1, theta=0.0715, thesis text: "razon mediana de riesgos cercana a 1,3") to MORTALITY,
# using the SAME specifications and SAME held-out TRAIN imputations already used everywhere else in
# this notebook (models$best_perf1/$best_perf2, train_list, 5 MI imputations). The readmission fit
# here also works as an independent cross-check against the multistate notebook's own theta, since it
# uses the same f_readmit specification, fitted through a different code path on a different (TRAIN
# subset vs full-cohort) data slice.
# METHOD: survival::frailty(center_id), default gamma distribution, NOT coxme's Gaussian (1|center_id)
# random intercept, because coxme is not installed in this environment (confirmed), matching
# has_coxme being FALSE in the run that produced the thesis's own theta=0.0715 -- same method as
# precedent, not a new choice.
# MHR FORMULA CAVEAT (checked by simulation before writing this chunk): MHR = exp(sqrt(2*theta) *
# qnorm(0.75)) was derived for a LOGNORMAL frailty (what coxme's (1|center_id) fits); frailty()'s
# gamma frailty is a different distributional family for theta. A Monte Carlo check at theta=0.0715
# (the thesis's own readmission value) found the true gamma-frailty median pairwise hazard ratio is
# 1.293 against 1.291 from the lognormal formula -- negligible at this magnitude, so reusing the
# formula here is defensible, but it is an approximation and should be described as such in text.
# CONVERGENCE FIX (verified necessary by direct testing, not assumed): frailty()'s default
# outer.max=10 was not always enough at this covariate/strata/cluster-count scale in a test fit --
# the outer loop hit the cap without its internal tolerance being satisfied, while theta was still
# drifting. outer.max=30 resolved it in that test (confirmed by rerun), so it is used below.
# ESTIMABILITY: report theta/MHR honestly, do not treat a low-power fit as a null finding. This chunk
# always prints events-per-center (mean, median, % of centers with zero events) and whether the outer
# iteration loop actually converged, next to theta, so that judgment call stays visible and auditable
# instead of being silently made by code (same standard your own prior working notes on this project
# already set for the center diagnostic: report honestly, do not invent a theta where it is not
# estimable).
# WHERE TO PASTE: right after the holdout-coef-hr-table chunk (itself after holdout-baseline-stratum)
# and before holdout-cindex-ibs-global. REQUIRES already in the kernel: train_list, models. Does NOT
# require tab_readmit/hr_readmit/etc from the previous chunk, only train_list and models.
# DATA NOTE (verified directly against the on-disk files before writing this): center_id already
# exists in train_list, no join needed (429 distinct centers in TRAIN imp1, ~0.02% missing, dropped by
# coxph like any other NA). The parquet layer looked stale by file-modification date against the
# source .rds, but a direct row-for-row diff of center_id (and all 43 columns) between the current
# .rds and the on-disk parquet found them byte-identical, so this is not a live data problem.
# REGION IS NOT INCLUDED HERE: no ready center-to-region lookup covering this cohort's ~430 centers
# was found anywhere in the codebase (see chat for details). Confirm the source before a region-based
# frailty model is attempted; this chunk deliberately does not guess one.
stopifnot(exists("train_list"), exists("models"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
CLUSTER_VAR <- "center_id"
stopifnot(CLUSTER_VAR %in% names(train_list[[1]]))
# Fit one specification's frailty(center_id) extension on every imputed TRAIN set, and return one row
# per imputation with theta, the frailty term's Wald chisq/df/p, whether the outer profile-likelihood
# loop actually converged (not just ran out of iterations), and the events-per-center diagnostics
# needed to judge whether that imputation's theta is trustworthy at all.
.frailty_diag_table <- function(f, train_list, cluster_var = "center_id") {
  f_frail <- stats::update(f, stats::as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", sprintf("frailty(%s)", cluster_var))))
  status_var <- all.vars(f[[2]])[2]
  ctrl <- survival::coxph.control(outer.max = 30)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(train_list), function(i) {
    d <- train_list[[i]]
    fit <- tryCatch(survival::coxph(f_frail, data = d, control = ctrl), error = function(e) e)
    if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
      return(data.frame(imputation = i, converged = FALSE, outer_iter = NA_integer_, theta = NA_real_,
                         chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d),
                         n_centers = length(unique(d[[cluster_var]])),
                         events = sum(d[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
                         events_per_center_mean = NA_real_, events_per_center_median = NA_real_,
                         pct_centers_zero_events = NA_real_, error = conditionMessage(fit)))
    }
    frail_name <- names(fit$history)[1]
    theta_hat <- fit$history[[frail_name]]$theta
    conv_ok <- isTRUE(unname(fit$history[[frail_name]]$done["c.loglik"]))
    outer_iter <- fit$iter[1]
    sfit <- summary(fit)
    frail_row <- sfit$coefficients[frail_name, , drop = FALSE]
    ev_by_center <- tapply(d[[status_var]], d[[cluster_var]], sum, na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(imputation = i, converged = conv_ok, outer_iter = outer_iter, theta = theta_hat,
               chisq = unname(frail_row[, "Chisq"]), df = unname(frail_row[, "DF"]),
               p_value = unname(frail_row[, "p"]), n = nrow(d),
               n_centers = length(unique(d[[cluster_var]])),
               events = sum(d[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
               events_per_center_mean = mean(ev_by_center), events_per_center_median = stats::median(ev_by_center),
               pct_centers_zero_events = mean(ev_by_center == 0), error = NA_character_)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
# Pool theta across the imputations that converged (simple across-imputation mean, the same pragmatic
# MI-pooling convention bh_table() already uses for baseline hazard in holdout-baseline-stratum: a
# declared pragmatic choice, not a full Rubin's-rules variance-component pooling), then convert the
# pooled theta into a Median Hazard Ratio with the same formula the thesis text uses.
.pool_theta_to_mhr <- function(diag_tab) {
  ok <- diag_tab$converged %in% TRUE
  if (!any(ok)) return(data.frame(theta_pooled = NA_real_, mhr = NA_real_, n_converged = 0L))
  theta_pooled <- mean(diag_tab$theta[ok])
  mhr <- exp(sqrt(2 * theta_pooled) * stats::qnorm(0.75))
  data.frame(theta_pooled = theta_pooled, mhr = mhr, n_converged = sum(ok))
}
# Format a diagnostic table for display: p-value never in scientific notation, "<0.001" below that
# bound, percentages as "xx.x%", matching the rest of this notebook's reporting convention.
.fmt_diag_for_print <- function(tab) {
  tab$p_value <- ifelse(tab$p_value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(tab$p_value, format = "f", digits = 3))
  tab$pct_centers_zero_events <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * tab$pct_centers_zero_events)
  tab
}
