# Purpose: exact counterpart of holdout-center-frailty-mhr, run on the held-out 20% (`val_list`)
# instead of the 80% TRAIN. Same specifications (models$best_perf1 / $best_perf2), same 5 MI
# imputations, same survival::frailty(center_id) gamma frailty, same outer.max = 30 convergence fix,
# same lognormal MHR = exp(sqrt(2*theta) * qnorm(0.75)) approximation and the same caveat about it
# (gamma vs lognormal families differ; the Monte Carlo check at theta = 0.0715 gave 1.293 vs 1.291,
# negligible at this magnitude but still an approximation, so describe it as such in text).
# WHERE TO PASTE: as a NEW cell right after the cell labelled holdout-center-frailty-mhr. It ADDS, it
# does not replace: the TRAIN diagnostic stays as the reportable one, this is the held-out counterpart.
# REQUIRES already in the kernel: `val_list` (holdout-build-sets) and `models` (holdout-define-models).
# If holdout-center-frailty-mhr was run first, this cell also prints a TRAIN vs VALIDATION side-by-side
# table by reusing pool_readmit / pool_death_bp1 / pool_death_bp2; if not, it simply skips that table.
# WHAT CHANGES vs the TRAIN version, and why each change is needed only in the 20%:
# (1) EMPTY FACTOR LEVELS -- tapply(status, center_id, sum) returns NA for every center level that has
# no rows. In TRAIN essentially all ~429 centers are present so this never fired; in the 20% many
# centers are absent, which turns events_per_center_mean and pct_centers_zero_events into NA and
# silently destroys the estimability diagnostic. Levels with no rows are dropped here and n_centers
# counts only centers actually observed in that imputation.
# (2) NON-IDENTIFIED TERMS -- at n = 17,631 rare one-hot dummies of the Full PH death model can be
# aliased (coef = NA). They are detected on a plain coxph() fit and removed before the frailty fit,
# because leaving them in perturbs the profile likelihood that estimates theta. Every removed term is
# named in a warning and the reduced term count is printed, so the specification change is auditable.
# (3) DIAGNOSTICS BEFORE THE FIT -- events per center are computed before coxph() runs, so a failed or
# non-converged fit still reports why it failed instead of a row of NAs.
# INTERPRETATION (state this in the text): a frailty variance estimated on the 20% is a diagnostic of
# center clustering IN THAT SAMPLE, not a validation of the TRAIN theta. With few events per center,
# theta is strongly shrunk toward zero, so theta close to 0 and MHR close to 1 here mean "not
# estimable at this event density", NOT "no center-level clustering". Read them next to the printed
# events-per-center columns, never on their own.
stopifnot(exists("val_list"), exists("models"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
CLUSTER_VAR <- "center_id"
stopifnot(CLUSTER_VAR %in% names(val_list[[1]]))
# Switch: TRUE removes aliased terms and fits anyway (each one named in a warning); FALSE stops, so
# the validation frailty fit is never quietly a different specification than the TRAIN one.
VAL_FRAILTY_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE
# Term helpers, identical convention to bh_table() and to holdout-coef-hr-table-val: strata() terms
# are never touched and are always carried into any rebuilt formula.
.terms_cov <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[!grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.terms_str <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.rebuild_formula <- function(f, keep) {
  rhs <- paste(c(keep, .terms_str(f)), collapse = " + ")
  stats::as.formula(paste(deparse(f[[2]], width.cutoff = 500L), "~", rhs), env = environment(f))
}
# Map coefficients back to model TERMS through coxph()$assign, so a factor family is judged whole and
# never half-dropped: a term is flagged only when ALL of its coefficients are NA in that imputation.
.na_terms <- function(fit) {
  cf <- stats::coef(fit)
  asg <- fit$assign
  if (is.null(names(asg))) names(asg) <- attr(fit$terms, "term.labels")[seq_along(asg)]
  names(asg)[vapply(asg, function(ix) all(is.na(cf[ix])), logical(1L))]
}
# Fit the plain (no frailty) specification on every validation imputation, collect the union of terms
# that came back aliased, and return either the original formula or a reduced one.
.identifiable_formula_val <- function(f, dlist, label) {
  fits <- lapply(dlist, function(d) survival::coxph(f, data = d))
  dropped <- unique(unlist(lapply(fits, .na_terms)))
  if (!length(dropped)) return(f)
  msg <- paste0("[", label, "] terms not identified in the 20%: ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))
  if (!VAL_FRAILTY_DROP_MISSING_TERMS) stop(msg, " -- set VAL_FRAILTY_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE to drop them and fit the rest.", call. = FALSE)
  warning(msg, " -- dropped from the validation frailty fit only; the TRAIN specification is unchanged.", call. = FALSE)
  .rebuild_formula(f, setdiff(.terms_cov(f), dropped))
}
# Events-per-center diagnostics, computed before any fit and immune to empty factor levels: centers
# with a missing id are excluded, and centers with no rows in this imputation are not counted as
# zero-event centers (they are simply not in the 20%), which is the distinction that matters here.
.center_diag <- function(d, status_var, cluster_var) {
  cl <- d[[cluster_var]]
  keep <- !is.na(cl)
  ev <- tapply(d[[status_var]][keep], droplevels(as.factor(cl[keep])), sum, na.rm = TRUE)
  ev <- ev[!is.na(ev)]
  list(n_centers = length(ev), events = sum(d[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
       mean_ev = if (length(ev)) mean(ev) else NA_real_,
       median_ev = if (length(ev)) stats::median(ev) else NA_real_,
       pct_zero = if (length(ev)) mean(ev == 0) else NA_real_,
       n_missing_cluster = sum(!keep))
}
# Fit one specification's frailty(center_id) extension on every imputed VALIDATION set and return one
# row per imputation: theta, the frailty term's Wald chisq/df/p, whether the outer profile-likelihood
# loop truly converged (not merely stopped), and the estimability diagnostics next to it.
.frailty_diag_table_val <- function(f, dlist, cluster_var = "center_id", label = "") {
  f_use <- .identifiable_formula_val(f, dlist, label)
  f_frail <- stats::update(f_use, stats::as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", sprintf("frailty(%s)", cluster_var))))
  status_var <- all.vars(f_use[[2]])[2]
  ctrl <- survival::coxph.control(outer.max = 30)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(dlist), function(i) {
    d <- dlist[[i]]
    cd <- .center_diag(d, status_var, cluster_var)
    row <- data.frame(imputation = i, converged = FALSE, outer_iter = NA_integer_, theta = NA_real_,
                      chisq = NA_real_, df = NA_real_, p_value = NA_real_, n = nrow(d),
                      n_centers = cd$n_centers, events = cd$events,
                      events_per_center_mean = cd$mean_ev, events_per_center_median = cd$median_ev,
                      pct_centers_zero_events = cd$pct_zero, error = NA_character_,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    fit <- tryCatch(survival::coxph(f_frail, data = d, control = ctrl), error = function(e) e)
    if (inherits(fit, "error")) { row$error <- conditionMessage(fit); return(row) }
    frail_name <- names(fit$history)[1]
    row$theta <- fit$history[[frail_name]]$theta
    row$converged <- isTRUE(unname(fit$history[[frail_name]]$done["c.loglik"]))
    row$outer_iter <- fit$iter[1]
    frail_row <- summary(fit)$coefficients[frail_name, , drop = FALSE]
    row$chisq <- unname(frail_row[, "Chisq"])
    row$df <- unname(frail_row[, "DF"])
    row$p_value <- unname(frail_row[, "p"])
    row
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  attr(out, "n_terms") <- length(.terms_cov(f_use))
  attr(out, "n_terms_original") <- length(.terms_cov(f))
  out
}
# Pool theta across converged imputations with the same pragmatic across-imputation mean used by
# bh_table() for the baseline hazard (a declared convention, not full Rubin's rules for a variance
# component), then convert to the Median Hazard Ratio with the formula the thesis text uses.
.pool_theta_to_mhr <- function(diag_tab) {
  ok <- diag_tab$converged %in% TRUE
  if (!any(ok)) return(data.frame(theta_pooled = NA_real_, mhr = NA_real_, n_converged = 0L))
  theta_pooled <- mean(diag_tab$theta[ok])
  data.frame(theta_pooled = theta_pooled, mhr = exp(sqrt(2 * theta_pooled) * stats::qnorm(0.75)), n_converged = sum(ok))
}
# Display formatting: p never in scientific notation, "<0.001" below that bound, percentages as xx.x%,
# and NA tolerated everywhere because a non-converged validation fit is a legitimate result to print.
.fmt_diag_for_print <- function(tab) {
  tab$p_value <- ifelse(is.na(tab$p_value), NA_character_, ifelse(tab$p_value < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(tab$p_value, format = "f", digits = 3)))
  tab$pct_centers_zero_events <- ifelse(is.na(tab$pct_centers_zero_events), NA_character_, sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * tab$pct_centers_zero_events))
  tab
}
# One-line summary that keeps theta and its estimability visible together, never theta alone.
.report_pool <- function(pool, diag_tab, label) {
  cat(sprintf("%s, pooled across %d/%d converged imputations: theta = %.4f, MHR = %.2f | terms kept %d/%d | events/center median = %.1f | centers with zero events = %.1f%%\n",
              label, pool$n_converged, nrow(diag_tab), pool$theta_pooled, pool$mhr,
              attr(diag_tab, "n_terms"), attr(diag_tab, "n_terms_original"),
              stats::median(diag_tab$events_per_center_median, na.rm = TRUE),
              100 * mean(diag_tab$pct_centers_zero_events, na.rm = TRUE)))
}

# Purpose: baseline hazard/survival per stratum for the SAME three cluster-robust specifications used
# in holdout-coef-hr-table-robust-centerid (readmit shared model, death best_perf1, death best_perf2),
# pooled across the 5 TRAIN imputations, mirroring bh_table() from holdout-baseline-stratum.
# WHY A SEPARATE FUNCTION INSTEAD OF REUSING bh_table(): bh_table() hardcodes a plain coxph() call
# with no cluster()/robust argument, and holdout-baseline-stratum is a different, already-established
# cell that this task did not ask to modify. This chunk defines its own small variant instead of
# editing that one, keeping the two cells independent.
# THE NUMBERS SHOULD MATCH holdout-baseline-stratum's tab_readmit/tab_death1/tab_death2 EXACTLY
# (verified end-to-end on simulated data mirroring the real strata/cluster structure before writing
# this: adding cluster(center_id) + robust=TRUE to a coxph() call does not change the fitted
# coefficients or the Breslow baseline hazard at all, only how the standard error is computed; every
# H0/S0 column matched to zero difference against a naive fit of the same formula). Computing it again
# here, directly from the robust fit objects, is about keeping this table self-contained next to the
# robust HR table, not because the values are expected to differ.
# WHERE TO PASTE: right after holdout-coef-hr-table-robust-centerid.
# REQUIRES already in the kernel: train_list, models.
stopifnot(exists("train_list"), exists("models"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
CLUSTER_VAR <- "center_id"
stopifnot(CLUSTER_VAR %in% names(train_list[[1]]))
# Same logic as bh_table() in holdout-baseline-stratum, with cluster(center_id) added to the formula
# and robust = TRUE at the fit step. strata() detection is unaffected by the extra cluster() term
# (verified: term.labels lists "cluster(center_id)" as its own separate term, never matched by the
# "^strata\\(" regex below, so it never gets mistaken for a stratifying variable).
.bh_table_robust <- function(f, train_list, cluster_var = "center_id", times = c(6, 12, 36, 60)) {
  f_robust <- stats::update(f, stats::as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", sprintf("cluster(%s)", cluster_var))))
  tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels")
  sv <- gsub("^strata\\(|\\)$", "", tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)])
  status_var <- all.vars(f[[2]])[2]
  per_imp <- lapply(train_list, function(d) {
    fit <- survival::coxph(f_robust, data = d, model = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
    bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
    H <- sapply(split(bh[, c("time", "hazard")], bh$strata), function(z)
      stats::approx(z$time, z$hazard, xout = times, method = "constant", f = 0, rule = 2)$y)
    # coxph's combined strata label uses the bare level for a FACTOR strata variable, but prefixes
    # "var=value" for a non-factor (numeric/logical) strata variable -- verified empirically against
    # survival::basehaz() (same behavior confirmed again here with cluster()+robust=TRUE active).
    lab <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(sv, function(v) {
      x <- d[[v]]
      if (is.factor(x)) as.character(x) else paste0(v, "=", as.character(x))
    }), sep = ", "))
    if (!setequal(colnames(H), unique(lab)))
      stop("Stratum labels from basehaz() do not match the data; inspect the strata variables.")
    list(H = H, n = table(lab), ev = tapply(d[[status_var]], lab, sum))
  })
  g <- sort(colnames(per_imp[[1]]$H))
  if (!all(vapply(per_imp, function(x) setequal(colnames(x$H), g), logical(1))))
    stop("Stratum set differs across imputations; inspect imputed strata variables before pooling.")
  Hm <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(per_imp, function(x) x$H[, g, drop = FALSE])) / length(per_imp)
  n_mean <- rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, function(x) as.numeric(x$n[g]), numeric(length(g))))
  ev_mean <- rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, function(x) as.numeric(x$ev[g]), numeric(length(g))))
  out <- data.frame(stratum = g, n = round(n_mean), events = round(ev_mean), check.names = FALSE)
  for (k in seq_along(times)) {
    out[[paste0("H0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(Hm[k, g], 4)
    out[[paste0("S0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(exp(-Hm[k, g]), 4)
  }
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

# Purpose: exact counterpart of holdout-baseline-stratum-robust-centerid, computed on the held-out 20%
# (`val_list`) instead of the 80% TRAIN: baseline hazard/survival per stratum for the same three
# cluster-robust specifications (readmit shared model, death best_perf1, death best_perf2), pooled
# across the 5 validation imputations.
# WHERE TO PASTE: as a NEW cell right after the cell labelled holdout-coef-hr-table-robust-centerid-3.
# It ADDS, it does not replace. If you want to keep the same 3-cell split as the TRAIN version, cut it
# at the two knitr::kable() calls for death bp1 and death bp2; the objects are all built up front.
# REQUIRES already in the kernel: `val_list` (holdout-build-sets) and `models` (holdout-define-models).
# WHAT SHOULD MATCH WHAT: adding cluster(center_id) + robust = TRUE changes only the standard errors,
# never the coefficients nor the Breslow baseline hazard, so these tables should reproduce the
# validation baselines from holdout-coef-hr-table-val -- WITH ONE EXCEPTION documented below. This
# cell checks that automatically against risk_readmit_val / risk_death_bp1_val / risk_death_bp2_val
# when those objects exist, instead of leaving the claim to the reader.
# THE EXCEPTION (also true of the TRAIN version, worth stating there too): cluster(center_id) makes
# center_id part of the model frame, so rows with a missing center_id are dropped by na.action in the
# robust fit but kept in the non-robust one. The match is therefore exact only when no center_id is
# missing. The number of rows dropped for that reason is printed per specification below, so a small
# discrepancy can be attributed to it rather than mistaken for a fitting problem.
# WHAT CHANGES vs the TRAIN version, and why each is needed only in the 20%:
# (1) approx() -> findInterval(): mathematically the identical step function (last jump <= t, flat
# tail, rule = 2 below the first event time), but approx() errors when a stratum contributes a single
# event time, which is possible at n = 17,631 in a sparse stratum and never happened in TRAIN.
# (2) UNION of strata across imputations instead of stop(): a stratum can be absent from one imputed
# validation set. It is averaged over the imputations where it exists and reported by name, rather
# than aborting the whole table.
# (3) NON-IDENTIFIED TERMS: rare one-hot dummies can be aliased (coef = NA) in the 20%, and
# survfit()/basehaz() do not tolerate NA coefficients. They are detected on a plain coxph() fit and
# removed before the robust fit, with every removed term named in a warning.
# INTERPRETATION: these baselines are estimated ON the held-out sample, so they belong to the
# validation refit, not to the frozen TRAIN model. Do not print them under TRAIN coefficients.
stopifnot(exists("val_list"), exists("models"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
CLUSTER_VAR <- "center_id"
stopifnot(CLUSTER_VAR %in% names(val_list[[1]]))
# Switch: TRUE removes aliased terms and fits anyway (each one named in a warning); FALSE stops, so
# the validation robust fit is never quietly a different specification than the TRAIN one.
VAL_ROBUST_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE
# Term helpers, same convention as bh_table(): the "^strata\\(" regex never matches cluster(), which
# terms() lists as its own separate term label, so a cluster term can never be mistaken for a stratum.
.terms_cov <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[!grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.terms_str <- function(f) { tl <- attr(stats::terms(f), "term.labels"); tl[grepl("^strata\\(", tl)] }
.rebuild_formula <- function(f, keep) {
  rhs <- paste(c(keep, .terms_str(f)), collapse = " + ")
  stats::as.formula(paste(deparse(f[[2]], width.cutoff = 500L), "~", rhs), env = environment(f))
}
.na_terms <- function(fit) {
  cf <- stats::coef(fit)
  asg <- fit$assign
  if (is.null(names(asg))) names(asg) <- attr(fit$terms, "term.labels")[seq_along(asg)]
  names(asg)[vapply(asg, function(ix) all(is.na(cf[ix])), logical(1L))]
}
.identifiable_formula_val <- function(f, dlist, label) {
  fits <- lapply(dlist, function(d) survival::coxph(f, data = d))
  dropped <- unique(unlist(lapply(fits, .na_terms)))
  if (!length(dropped)) return(f)
  msg <- paste0("[", label, "] terms not identified in the 20%: ", paste(dropped, collapse = ", "))
  if (!VAL_ROBUST_DROP_MISSING_TERMS) stop(msg, " -- set VAL_ROBUST_DROP_MISSING_TERMS <- TRUE to drop them and fit the rest.", call. = FALSE)
  warning(msg, " -- dropped from the validation robust fit only; the TRAIN specification is unchanged.", call. = FALSE)
  .rebuild_formula(f, setdiff(.terms_cov(f), dropped))
}
# Same logic as .bh_table_robust() in holdout-baseline-stratum-robust-centerid, hardened for the 20%.
.bh_table_robust_val <- function(f, dlist, cluster_var = "center_id", times = c(6, 12, 36, 60), label = "") {
  f_use <- .identifiable_formula_val(f, dlist, label)
  f_robust <- stats::update(f_use, stats::as.formula(paste(". ~ . +", sprintf("cluster(%s)", cluster_var))))
  sv <- gsub("^strata\\(|\\)$", "", .terms_str(f_use))
  status_var <- all.vars(f_use[[2]])[2]
  n_dropped_cluster <- vapply(dlist, function(d) sum(is.na(d[[cluster_var]])), 0L)
  per_imp <- lapply(dlist, function(d) {
    fit <- survival::coxph(f_robust, data = d, model = TRUE, robust = TRUE)
    bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
    # Step evaluation without approx(): findInterval() gives the count of jump times <= t, so index 0
    # means below the first event time (rule = 2 convention: carry the first value) and any index >= 1
    # is the last jump at or before t. Identical output to approx(method = "constant", f = 0, rule = 2)
    # and, unlike it, well defined when a stratum has a single event time.
    H <- vapply(split(bh[, c("time", "hazard")], bh$strata), function(z) {
      z <- z[order(z$time), ]
      idx <- findInterval(times, z$time)
      ifelse(idx == 0L, z$hazard[1L], z$hazard[pmax(idx, 1L)])
    }, numeric(length(times)))
    # coxph's combined strata label uses the bare level for a FACTOR strata variable and prefixes
    # "var=value" for a non-factor one; rows dropped for a missing cluster id must be dropped from the
    # label vector too, otherwise n/events would be counted on a different row set than the fit used.
    keep <- !is.na(d[[cluster_var]])
    dk <- d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    lab <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(sv, function(v) {
      x <- dk[[v]]
      if (is.factor(x)) as.character(x) else paste0(v, "=", as.character(x))
    }), sep = ", "))
    if (!all(colnames(H) %in% unique(lab)))
      stop("Stratum labels from basehaz() are not present in the data; inspect the strata variables.")
    list(H = H, n = table(lab), ev = tapply(dk[[status_var]], lab, sum))
  })
  g <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(per_imp, function(x) colnames(x$H)))))
  gone <- unique(unlist(lapply(per_imp, function(x) setdiff(g, colnames(x$H)))))
  if (length(gone)) message("[", label, "] strata absent from at least one validation imputation: ", paste(gone, collapse = " | "))
  grab <- function(x, gg) if (gg %in% colnames(x$H)) x$H[, gg] else rep(NA_real_, length(times))
  Hm <- sapply(g, function(gg) rowMeans(vapply(per_imp, grab, numeric(length(times)), gg = gg), na.rm = TRUE))
  pick <- function(x, gg, what) { v <- x[[what]][gg]; if (is.na(v)) 0 else as.numeric(v) }
  n_mean <- vapply(g, function(gg) mean(vapply(per_imp, pick, 0, gg = gg, what = "n")), 0)
  ev_mean <- vapply(g, function(gg) mean(vapply(per_imp, pick, 0, gg = gg, what = "ev")), 0)
  out <- data.frame(stratum = g, n = round(n_mean), events = round(ev_mean), check.names = FALSE)
  for (k in seq_along(times)) {
    out[[paste0("H0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(Hm[k, g], 4)
    out[[paste0("S0_", times[k], "m")]] <- round(exp(-Hm[k, g]), 4)
  }
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  attr(out, "n_dropped_cluster") <- mean(n_dropped_cluster)
  attr(out, "n_terms") <- length(.terms_cov(f_use))
  attr(out, "n_terms_original") <- length(.terms_cov(f))
  out
}
# Turn an H0/S0 table into the same Risk_* representation used by holdout-coef-hr-table-val, so the
# two cells can be compared column by column rather than by eye.
.risk_from_bh_table <- function(tab) {
  s0_cols <- grep("^S0_", names(tab), value = TRUE)
  risk <- tab[, c("stratum", "n", "events")]
  for (col in s0_cols) risk[[sub("^S0_", "Risk_", col)]] <- sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * (1 - tab[[col]]))
  risk
}
# Automatic equality check against the non-robust validation baselines, when they are in the kernel.
# Only the Risk_* columns are compared: n and events legitimately differ by the rows that cluster()
# dropped for a missing center_id, which is exactly the exception documented at the top of this cell.
.compare_risk_val <- function(tab_robust, ref_name, label) {
  if (!exists(ref_name, inherits = TRUE)) {
    cat(sprintf("%-28s comparison skipped (%s not in the kernel; run holdout-coef-hr-table-val first)\n", label, ref_name))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  ref <- get(ref_name, inherits = TRUE)
  a <- .risk_from_bh_table(tab_robust)
  cols <- intersect(grep("^Risk_", names(a), value = TRUE), names(ref))
  common <- intersect(a$stratum, ref$stratum)
  bad <- sum(a[match(common, a$stratum), cols] != ref[match(common, ref$stratum), cols])
  cat(sprintf("%-28s strata compared = %d/%d | mismatching risk cells = %d | rows dropped for missing %s (MI mean) = %.1f | terms kept %d/%d\n",
              label, length(common), nrow(a), bad, CLUSTER_VAR,
              attr(tab_robust, "n_dropped_cluster"), attr(tab_robust, "n_terms"), attr(tab_robust, "n_terms_original")))
}

title: SENDA Convenio 1 2010-2022 - Multistate semi-Markov nomogram (step 2.6, best_perf2)
text:
States (illness-death, semi-competing): 1 = Discharge (alive without readmission), 2 = Readmission (readmitted alive), 3 = Death (absorbing).









Transition
Intensity
Clock
Model




1->2 readmission
lambda12
forward (from discharge)
f_readmit (best_perf2)


1->3 death without readm.
lambda13
forward (from discharge)
formula_shap_death_rule2 (best_perf2)


2->3 death after readm.
lambda23
reset (sojourn from readmission)
death covariables



Implementation trick (handoff): in long format mstate, time = Tstop - Tstart (gap). For 1->2 and 1->3, Tstart = 0 => gap = time since discharge (clock-forward). For 2->3, gap = sojourn (clock-reset). Fitting everything on the gap delivers the correct semi-Markov without “choosing clock” by hand. Clock-reset on 2->3 is used as primary model only if Titman-Putter rejects Markov on that transition (section 7).
Decisions in this version (answer your three questions):

Markov: the transition to test is 2->3, with the general test by Titman & Putter (mstate::MarkovTest), not just the entry-time covariate shortcut.
vce(center_id): compare naive vs center-robust vs center frailty to see if modeling clustering improves fit (not just inflates SE).
Whole-sample: transition probabilities for population-level reporting are applied to the entire cohort (>80k) and averaged (population-averaged); the profile-specific calculation is the particular case for the nomogram. You were not wrong.


Variable names, outcomes (readmit_event, death_event) and times (*_time_from_disch_m) are not changed. Blocks with explicit assumptions.

make_synthetic <- function(N = 88000, n_centers = 220, seed = 2125) {
  set.seed(seed)
  cid <- sample.int(n_centers, N, replace = TRUE)
  fr  <- rnorm(n_centers, 0, 0.5)[cid]                  # frailty real de centro
  age <- sample(0:2, N, TRUE); alc <- rbinom(N,1,.35); unemp <- rbinom(N,1,.4)
  dit <- rgamma(N, 2, 1/2); plan <- sample(0:2, N, TRUE); phys <- rbinom(N,1,.3)
  lp_r <- .15*age + .30*alc + .10*unemp - .05*dit + fr
  lp_d0<- .45*age + .50*alc + .40*unemp + fr
  lp_d1<- .40*age + .45*alc + .35*unemp + .6 + fr
  tr  <- rexp(N, .02*exp(lp_r)); td0 <- rexp(N, .004*exp(lp_d0)); adm <- 120
  sjd <- rexp(N, .010*exp(lp_d1)) * (1 + .02*tr)         # sojourn depende de entrada => NO-Markov
  re_t <- numeric(N); re_e <- integer(N); de_t <- numeric(N); de_e <- integer(N)
  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    if (min(tr[i], td0[i]) > adm) { re_t[i]<-adm; de_t[i]<-adm }
    else if (td0[i] < tr[i])      { re_t[i]<-td0[i]; de_t[i]<-td0[i]; de_e[i]<-1L }
    else { re_t[i]<-tr[i]; re_e[i]<-1L; td<-tr[i]+sjd[i]
           if (td>adm){de_t[i]<-adm} else {de_t[i]<-td; de_e[i]<-1L} }
  }
  data.frame(readmit_time_from_disch_m = re_t, readmit_event = re_e,
             death_time_from_disch_m = de_t, death_event = de_e,
             adm_age_rec3 = age, primary_sub_mod_alcohol = alc,
             occupation_condition_corr24_unemployed = unemp, dit_m = dit,
             plan_type_strata = factor(plan), any_phys_dx = factor(phys),
             tr_outcome_adm_discharge_rule_violation_undet = factor(sample(0:1,N,TRUE)),
             center_id = factor(cid))
}

bad <- with(dat_ms, readmit_event==1 & death_event==1 &
              death_time_from_disch_m < readmit_time_from_disch_m)

                dat_ms$readmit_time_from_disch_m[bad] <- dat_ms$death_time_from_disch_m[bad] }

d3$tstart0  <- 0

# Formulas base (SIN cluster) y version con cluster(center_id) embebido en la formula.
mk <- function(covs, strata_vars, lhs) as.formula(paste(lhs, "~",
        paste(c(covs, sprintf("strata(%s)", strata_vars)), collapse = " + ")))
add_cluster <- function(f) update(f, as.formula(paste(". ~ . + cluster(", CLUSTER_VAR, ")")))

f1 <- mk(covs_readmit, strata_readmit, "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
f2 <- mk(covs_death,   strata_death,   "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
f3 <- mk(covs_death,   strata_death,   "Surv(tstart0, sojourn, status)")

m_tr1 <- coxph(add_cluster(f1), data = d1, robust = TRUE, x = TRUE)
m_tr2 <- coxph(add_cluster(f2), data = d2, robust = TRUE, x = TRUE)

Robust variance change SEs. To answer “does it improve the model” compare, on the transition with most clustering (1->2):

naive (independence),
robust (sandwich clustered by center),
center frailty (random effect frailty(center_id) / coxme), which does change the fit: if AIC drops / penalized likelihood rises and frailty variance (theta) is non-trivial, clustering by center contributes and should be modeled.



Code
co1 <- coxph(f1, data = d1, robust = FALSE)                       # naive
se_cmp <- data.frame(term = rownames(summary(m_tr1)$coefficients),
  se_naive  = summary(co1)$coefficients[,"se(coef)"],
  se_robust = summary(m_tr1)$coefficients[,"robust se"])
se_cmp$ratio <- se_cmp$se_robust / se_cmp$se_naive
cat("Robust SE/naive (1->2):\n"); print(round(se_cmp[,-1],4))

# Frailty by center: if coxme is present; if not, frailty().
frail_fit <- NULL
if (has_coxme) {
  ff <- as.formula(paste("Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status) ~",
        paste(c(covs_readmit, sprintf("strata(%s)",strata_readmit)), collapse=" + "),
        "+ (1|", CLUSTER_VAR, ")"))
  frail_fit <- tryCatch(coxme::coxme(ff, data = d1), error = function(e) {message(e); NULL})
  if (!is.null(frail_fit)) { cat("\n[coxme] varianza del frailty de centro (theta):\n")
    print(frail_fit$vcoef); cat("AIC frailty:", AIC(frail_fit), "| AIC naive:", AIC(co1), "\n") }
} else {
  ff <- mk(c(covs_readmit, sprintf("frailty(%s)", CLUSTER_VAR)), strata_readmit, "Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status)")
  frail_fit <- tryCatch(coxph(ff, data = d1), error = function(e){message(e); NULL})
  if (!is.null(frail_fit)) print(frail_fit)
}
cat("\nReading: if the center frailty reduces AIC and theta > 0 in a non‑trivial way => modeling the center improves the fit;",
    "\nif only the SEs change (robust vs. naive) without improving fit => robust variance is sufficient.\n")

The transition to test is 2->3. General test by Titman & Putter (2022), mstate::MarkovTest: log-rank-type statistics that test whether the intensity of 2->3 depends on the state occupied at previous times (i.e., entry time / sojourn). Complemented with a robust shortcut (entry-time covariate on clock-forward, Wald) in case the installed version of MarkovTest differs.

qsel <- as.numeric(quantile(d3$Tstop[d3$status==1], c(.2,.35,.5,.65,.8), na.rm = TRUE))
markov_TP <- tryCatch(
  mstate::MarkovTest(ms, id = "id", transition = 3, grid = qsel, B = 2000),  # singular!
  error = function(e) { message("MarkovTest failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
p_TP <- if (!is.null(markov_TP)) markov_TP$p_stat_wb[1] else NA_real_
if (!is.null(markov_TP))
  cat(sprintf("[MarkovTest 2->3] p_stat_wb=%.3g | p_ch_stat_wb=%.3g\n",
              p_TP, markov_TP$p_ch_stat_wb))

# (b) Robust shortcut: entry time as covariate in 2->3 clock-forward (robust Wald)
d3$t_entry <- d3$Tstart
fmk <- mk(c(covs_death, "t_entry"), strata_death, "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
m_mk <- coxph(add_cluster(fmk), data = d3, robust = TRUE)
p_entry <- summary(m_mk)$coefficients["t_entry","Pr(>|z|)"]
cat(sprintf("\n[2->3] coef(t_entry)=%.4f  p=%.3g\n",
            summary(m_mk)$coefficients["t_entry","coef"], p_entry))

# (c) Cross-check log-rank by entry time tertiles (clock-reset)
d3$entry_tertile <- cut(d3$t_entry, quantile(d3$t_entry, c(0,1/3,2/3,1)),
                        include.lowest = TRUE, labels = c("early","medium","late"))
print(survdiff(Surv(sojourn, status) ~ entry_tertile, data = d3))

p_lr <- 1 - pchisq(survdiff(Surv(sojourn, status) ~ entry_tertile, data = d3)$chisq, df = 2)
SEMI_MARKOV <- (!is.na(p_TP) && p_TP < 0.05) || (p_entry < 0.05)
cat(sprintf("[2->3 Markov] Titman-Putter p=%.3g | entry-time Wald p=%.3g | log-rank p=%.2g\n",
            p_TP, p_entry, p_lr))
cat(if (SEMI_MARKOV)
  "=> Markov rejected in 2->3: clock-reset (semi-Markov) is primary.\n" else

For a given covariate profile, trajectories are simulated with clock-reset and state occupancy is reported at 6/12/36/60 months. Primary engine for the app: flexsurv (pmatrix.simfs, with CIs via MVN resampling of coefficients); here a semi-parametric version is included with mstate::mssample on the Cox best_perf2 as reference/validation. Both yield the same quantity: P(state | profile, t).


Code
M_SIM <- 1e5
.haz_for_profile <- function(model, newdata, trans_id) {
  sf <- survfit(model, newdata = newdata)
  hz <- if (!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv),1e-12))
  data.frame(time = sf$time, Haz = hz, trans = trans_id)
}
predict_profile <- function(profile, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), M = M_SIM,
                            models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3), trans = tmat, seed = 2125) {
  set.seed(seed)
  Haz <- rbind(.haz_for_profile(models[[1]], profile, 1L),
               .haz_for_profile(models[[2]], profile, 2L),
               .haz_for_profile(models[[3]], profile, 3L))
  Haz <- Haz[order(Haz$trans, Haz$time),]
  s <- mssample(Haz = Haz, trans = trans, clock = "reset",
                history = list(state = 1, time = 0, tstate = NULL),
                tvec = tvec, M = M, output = "state")
  data.frame(month = tvec,
             p_alive_no_readm = s[["Discharge"]] %||% s[,2],
             p_readmitted     = s[["Readmission"]] %||% s[,3],
             p_dead           = s[["Death"]] %||% s[,4])
}

ref_profile <- function(data, vars) {
  vars <- vars[vars %in% names(data)]
  as.data.frame(setNames(lapply(vars, function(v){
    x <- data[[v]]; if (is.numeric(x)) median(x, na.rm=TRUE)
    else factor(names(sort(table(x),decreasing=TRUE))[1], levels=levels(factor(x)))}), vars))
}

# the 2->3 transition is refit clock-forward (time from discharge, not sojourn).
m_tr3_fwd <- coxph(add_cluster(f2), data = d3, robust = TRUE, x = TRUE)   # f2 = Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status) ~ covs_death + strata_death

# Build a profile-specific msfit on a common time grid (step carry-forward).
.msfit_profile_fwd <- function(profile, models, trans) {
  raw <- lapply(models, function(m) {
    sf <- survfit(m, newdata = profile)
    ch <- if (!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv), 1e-12))
    data.frame(time = sf$time, Haz = ch)
  })
  ut <- sort(unique(c(0, unlist(lapply(raw, `[[`, "time")))))
  Haz <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(raw), function(k) {
    df <- raw[[k]]; idx <- findInterval(ut, df$time)
    data.frame(time = ut, Haz = ifelse(idx == 0, 0, df$Haz[pmax(idx, 1)]), trans = k)
  }))
  structure(list(Haz = Haz, trans = trans), class = "msfit")
}
predict_profile_markov <- function(profile, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS),
                                   models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd), trans = tmat) {
  pt <- probtrans(.msfit_profile_fwd(profile, models, trans), predt = 0, variance = FALSE)[[1]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(tvec, function(h) {
    i <- which.min(abs(pt$time - h))
    data.frame(month = h, p_alive_no_readm = pt$pstate1[i],
               p_readmitted = pt$pstate2[i], p_dead = pt$pstate3[i])
  }))
}

# Fast apples-to-apples band: MVN draws of Cox coefs (cluster-robust vcov) -> scale each
# transition's cumulative hazard -> probtrans (exact, clock-forward). ~9 s/profile.
# Coefficient-only band (per-stratum baseline held fixed -> mild lower bound).
stopifnot(exists("m_tr3_fwd"))
.z_exact <- function(model, newdata){
  p <- length(coef(model)); if(!p) return(numeric(0)); base <- model; z <- numeric(p)
  for(j in seq_len(p)){ bj<-numeric(p); bj[j]<-1; base$coefficients<-bj
    z[j] <- as.numeric(predict(base, newdata=newdata, type="lp")) }
  setNames(z, names(coef(model)))
}
.mvn0 <- function(V, B){ p<-nrow(V); if(!p) return(matrix(0,B,0))
  matrix(rnorm(B*p), B, p) %*% chol((V + t(V))/2) }

predict_profile_ci_mvn <- function(profile, models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd),
                                   trans = tmat, tvec = HORIZONS, B = 500,
                                   n_grid = 200, cl = 0.95, seed = 2125){
  set.seed(seed); K <- length(models); grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, max(tvec), length.out=n_grid), tvec)))
  base_grid <- sapply(seq_len(K), function(k){              # base cumhaz per transition on thinned grid
    sf <- survfit(models[[k]], newdata = profile)
    ch <- if(!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv),1e-12))
    idx <- findInterval(grid, sf$time); ifelse(idx==0, 0, ch[pmax(idx,1)]) })
  z <- lapply(models, .z_exact, newdata = profile); Del <- lapply(models, function(m) .mvn0(vcov(m), B))
  hidx <- match(tvec, grid)
  run_pt <- function(sc){
    Hb <- data.frame(time=rep(grid,K), Haz=as.numeric(sweep(base_grid,2,sc,`*`)),
                     trans=rep(seq_len(K), each=length(grid)))
    probtrans(structure(list(Haz=Hb, trans=trans), class="msfit"), predt=0, variance=FALSE)[[1]] }
  pt0 <- run_pt(rep(1,K)); occ <- array(NA_real_, c(B, length(tvec), 3))
  for(b in seq_len(B)){
    sc <- vapply(seq_len(K), function(k) if(length(z[[k]])) exp(sum(z[[k]]*Del[[k]][b,])) else 1, numeric(1))
    pt <- run_pt(sc); occ[b,,1]<-pt$pstate1[hidx]; occ[b,,2]<-pt$pstate2[hidx]; occ[b,,3]<-pt$pstate3[hidx]
  }
  a <- (1-cl)/2
  out <- data.frame(month=tvec, alive=pt0$pstate1[hidx], readm=pt0$pstate2[hidx], dead=pt0$pstate3[hidx])
  for(s in 1:3){ nm<-c("alive","readm","dead")[s]; qq<-apply(occ[,,s],2,quantile,c(a,1-a),na.rm=TRUE)
    out[[paste0(nm,"_lo")]]<-qq[1,]; out[[paste0(nm,"_hi")]]<-qq[2,] }
  out
}

The Markov assumption for the readmission→death transition was not rejected (Titman–Putter test p = 0.57; entry-time Wald p = 0.57; log-rank by entry tertile p = 0.10). Consistent with this, state occupancy under clock-forward vs clock-reset specifications differed by ≤ 1.5 pp, within the 95% parameter-uncertainty interval at all horizons. We therefore adopt the Markov clock-forward specification as primary, with the semi-Markov specification as sensitivity.
Across risk-spanning profiles, the clock specification (Markov vs semi-Markov) shifted state occupancy by ≤ 1.5 percentage points (worst case: highest-risk profile, 36 months), well within the 95% parameter-uncertainty interval (half-width 1.9–5.1 pp) at every horizon. The clock choice is therefore immaterial relative to estimation uncertainty; we adopt the Markov clock-forward specification as primary and report the semi-Markov specification as a sensitivity analysis.

marginal_averaged <- function(data, n_sub = 2000, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), seed = 2125,
                              models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd)) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sub <- data[sample.int(nrow(data), min(n_sub, nrow(data))), , drop = FALSE]   # only the subset travels to the workers
  preds <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i) {

    as.matrix(s[, c("p_alive_no_readm","p_readmitted","p_dead")])
  }, future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival","mstate"))
  acc <- Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)
  data.frame(month = tvec, p_alive_no_readm = acc[,1], p_readmitted = acc[,2], p_dead = acc[,3])
}

This is a sensitivity analysis, not the nomogram’s engine. Flexible parametric models (flexsurvspline, Royston–Parmar) are fit per transition on gap time (so this run is semi-Markov) without strata() and without cluster-robust variance. It therefore diverges from the primary specification on clock, strata, and center clustering — by design. Its value: if a fully parametric, differently-specified family yields similar state occupancy to the primary Cox + probtrans (Markov) engine, that is robustness to the modelling family. The nomogram’s online engine and CIs come from the serialized Cox transition models + probtrans (Markov clock-forward) + the cluster-robust MVN band, not from pmatrix.simfs.

fit_ms_one <- function(d){

  if (any(bad)){ d$readmit_event[bad]<-0; d$readmit_time_from_disch_m[bad]<-d$death_time_from_disch_m[bad] }
  tie <- with(d, readmit_event==1 & death_event==1 & death_time_from_disch_m==readmit_time_from_disch_m)
  if (any(tie)) d$death_time_from_disch_m[tie] <- d$death_time_from_disch_m[tie] + eps
  keep <- unique(c(covs_readmit, covs_death, strata_readmit, strata_death, CLUSTER_VAR))

                 status = c(NA,"readmit_event","death_event"), data = d, trans = tmat, keep = keep)
  list(m1 = coxph(add_cluster(f1),        data = ms_i[ms_i$trans==1,], robust = TRUE, x = TRUE),  # 1->2

predict_profile_markov_pooled <- function(profile, tvec = HORIZONS, fits = ms_fits){

# 4. (optional) POOLED CI band by Rubin: within = mean MVN variance; between = variance of the 5 points
predict_profile_ci_mvn_pooled <- function(profile, tvec = HORIZONS, B = 500, fits = ms_fits, cl = 0.95){
  z <- qnorm(1-(1-cl)/2); m <- length(fits)
  per <- lapply(fits, function(f) predict_profile_ci_mvn(profile, models = list(f$m1,f$m2,f$m3),
                                                         tvec = tvec, B = B))
  out <- data.frame(month = tvec)
  for (s in c("alive","readm","dead")){
    pts <- sapply(per, function(p) p[[s]])
    hw  <- sapply(per, function(p) (p[[paste0(s,"_hi")]] - p[[paste0(s,"_lo")]])/2)
    qbar <- rowMeans(pts); within <- rowMeans((hw/z)^2); between <- apply(pts, 1, var)
    total <- within + (1 + 1/m)*between                              # Rubin total variance
    out[[s]] <- qbar; out[[paste0(s,"_lo")]] <- qbar - z*sqrt(total); out[[paste0(s,"_hi")]] <- qbar + z*sqrt(total)
  }
  out
}

ms_full <- msprep(time = c(NA,"readmit_time_from_disch_m","death_time_from_disch_m"),
                  status = c(NA,"readmit_event","death_event"),
                  data = .clean_ms(full_imp[[1]]), trans = tmat)
pt0 <- probtrans(msfit(coxph(Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status) ~ strata(trans), data = ms_full), trans = tmat),
                 predt = 0)[[1]]
aj_full <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(3, HORIZONS), function(h){
  i <- pmax(findInterval(h, pt0$time), 1L)
  data.frame(month = h, alive_obs = pt0$pstate1[i], readm_obs = pt0$pstate2[i], dead_obs = pt0$pstate3[i]) }))

# ---- 2. PREDICHO: marginal pooled (mismos pacientes en las 5 imput.; cada una con SUS covariables+modelos) ----
marginal_averaged_pool <- function(imp_list = full_imp, fits = ms_fits, n_sub = 1000,
                                   tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), seed = 2125){
  set.seed(seed); idx <- sample.int(nrow(imp_list[[1]]), min(n_sub, nrow(imp_list[[1]])))
  per_imp <- lapply(seq_along(fits), function(m){
    sub  <- imp_list[[m]][idx, , drop = FALSE]
    mods <- list(fits[[m]]$m1, fits[[m]]$m2, fits[[m]]$m3)
    preds <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i)
      as.matrix(predict_profile_markov(sub[i, , drop = FALSE], tvec = tvec, models = mods)[
                , c("p_alive_no_readm","p_readmitted","p_dead")]),
      future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival","mstate"))
    Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)                       # marginal de la imputacion m
  })
  acc <- Reduce(`+`, per_imp) / length(per_imp)              # Rubin Q-barra sobre imputaciones
  data.frame(month = tvec, alive_pred = acc[,1], readm_pred = acc[,2], dead_pred = acc[,3])
}
t0 <- Sys.time()
marg_pool <- marginal_averaged_pool(n_sub = 1000)
cat(sprintf("marginal_averaged_pool (5 imput x n_sub=1000, paralelo): %.1f min\n",
            as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))

# ---- 3. COMPARACION: pooled full-sample vs AJ observado (abs + rel) ----
cmp <- merge(aj_full, marg_pool, by = "month")
for (s in c("alive","readm","dead")){
  cmp[[paste0(s,"_abs")]] <- cmp[[paste0(s,"_pred")]] - cmp[[paste0(s,"_obs")]]
  cmp[[paste0(s,"_rel")]] <- 100 * cmp[[paste0(s,"_abs")]] / pmax(cmp[[paste0(s,"_obs")]], 1e-6)
}
cmp$max_abs <- pmax(abs(cmp$alive_abs), abs(cmp$readm_abs), abs(cmp$dead_abs))
cat(sprintf("In-the-large POOLED calibration  full-sample vs AJ — max |pred-obs|: %.4f\n", max(cmp$max_abs)))
knitr::kable(cmp[, c("month","alive_obs","alive_pred","alive_rel","readm_obs","readm_pred","readm_rel",
                     "dead_obs","dead_pred","dead_rel","max_abs")],

Markov: the formal test is Titman & Putter on 2->3 (MarkovTest); the entry-time shortcut is the robust backup. If Markov is rejected, clock-reset is primary.
vce(center_id): robust inflates/adjusts SE without changing coefficients; the center frailty tells if modeling the cluster improves fit (AIC/theta). Report both.
Whole-sample: marginal probabilities are computed over the entire cohort (non-parametric Aalen-Johansen and/or average of individual predictions). The nomogram uses the profile-specific calculation.
flexsurv fits offline and predicts online (MVN CIs), avoiding refitting per click and filtering test. USE_SYNTHETIC<-FALSE plugs in real data.
PRE-CHECK 2->3: if <~50 deaths after readmission, use Martinez-Camblor fallback.

In synthetic mode an illness-death cohort with the same structure is generated to validate the workflow.

make_synthetic <- function(N = 88000, n_centers = 220, seed = 2125) {
  set.seed(seed)
  cid <- sample.int(n_centers, N, replace = TRUE)
  fr  <- rnorm(n_centers, 0, 0.5)[cid]                  # frailty real de centro
  age <- sample(0:2, N, TRUE); alc <- rbinom(N,1,.35); unemp <- rbinom(N,1,.4)
  dit <- rgamma(N, 2, 1/2); plan <- sample(0:2, N, TRUE); phys <- rbinom(N,1,.3)
  lp_r <- .15*age + .30*alc + .10*unemp - .05*dit + fr
  lp_d0<- .45*age + .50*alc + .40*unemp + fr
  lp_d1<- .40*age + .45*alc + .35*unemp + .6 + fr
  tr  <- rexp(N, .02*exp(lp_r)); td0 <- rexp(N, .004*exp(lp_d0)); adm <- 120
  sjd <- rexp(N, .010*exp(lp_d1)) * (1 + .02*tr)         # sojourn depende de entrada => NO-Markov
  re_t <- numeric(N); re_e <- integer(N); de_t <- numeric(N); de_e <- integer(N)
  for (i in seq_len(N)) {
    if (min(tr[i], td0[i]) > adm) { re_t[i]<-adm; de_t[i]<-adm }
    else if (td0[i] < tr[i])      { re_t[i]<-td0[i]; de_t[i]<-td0[i]; de_e[i]<-1L }
    else { re_t[i]<-tr[i]; re_e[i]<-1L; td<-tr[i]+sjd[i]
           if (td>adm){de_t[i]<-adm} else {de_t[i]<-td; de_e[i]<-1L} }
  }
  data.frame(readmit_time_from_disch_m = re_t, readmit_event = re_e,
             death_time_from_disch_m = de_t, death_event = de_e,
             adm_age_rec3 = age, primary_sub_mod_alcohol = alc,
             occupation_condition_corr24_unemployed = unemp, dit_m = dit,
             plan_type_strata = factor(plan), any_phys_dx = factor(phys),
             tr_outcome_adm_discharge_rule_violation_undet = factor(sample(0:1,N,TRUE)),
             center_id = factor(cid))
}

}

text:
Three transition-specific Cox models (each transition preserves its best_perf2 strata). Clock-reset on 2->3 (sojourn). Robust variance cluster(center_id).


Code
d1 <- ms[ms$trans==1,]; d2 <- ms[ms$trans==2,]; d3 <- ms[ms$trans==3,]
d3$tstart0  <- 0
d3$sojourn  <- pmax(d3$Tstop - d3$Tstart, eps)        # reloj reset (sojourn desde la readmision)

# Formulas base (SIN cluster) y version con cluster(center_id) embebido en la formula.
mk <- function(covs, strata_vars, lhs) as.formula(paste(lhs, "~",
        paste(c(covs, sprintf("strata(%s)", strata_vars)), collapse = " + ")))
add_cluster <- function(f) update(f, as.formula(paste(". ~ . + cluster(", CLUSTER_VAR, ")")))

f1 <- mk(covs_readmit, strata_readmit, "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
f2 <- mk(covs_death,   strata_death,   "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
f3 <- mk(covs_death,   strata_death,   "Surv(tstart0, sojourn, status)")

title: SENDA Convenio 1 2010-2022 - Multistate semi-Markov nomogram (step 2.6, best_perf2)
text:
Robust variance change SEs. To answer “does it improve the model” compare, on the transition with most clustering (1->2):

naive (independence),
robust (sandwich clustered by center),
center frailty (random effect frailty(center_id) / coxme), which does change the fit: if AIC drops / penalized likelihood rises and frailty variance (theta) is non-trivial, clustering by center contributes and should be modeled.



Code
co1 <- coxph(f1, data = d1, robust = FALSE)                       # naive
se_cmp <- data.frame(term = rownames(summary(m_tr1)$coefficients),
  se_naive  = summary(co1)$coefficients[,"se(coef)"],
  se_robust = summary(m_tr1)$coefficients[,"robust se"])
se_cmp$ratio <- se_cmp$se_robust / se_cmp$se_naive
cat("Robust SE/naive (1->2):\n"); print(round(se_cmp[,-1],4))

# Frailty by center: if coxme is present; if not, frailty().
frail_fit <- NULL
if (has_coxme) {
  ff <- as.formula(paste("Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status) ~",
        paste(c(covs_readmit, sprintf("strata(%s)",strata_readmit)), collapse=" + "),
        "+ (1|", CLUSTER_VAR, ")"))
  frail_fit <- tryCatch(coxme::coxme(ff, data = d1), error = function(e) {message(e); NULL})
  if (!is.null(frail_fit)) { cat("\n[coxme] varianza del frailty de centro (theta):\n")
    print(frail_fit$vcoef); cat("AIC frailty:", AIC(frail_fit), "| AIC naive:", AIC(co1), "\n") }
} else {
  ff <- mk(c(covs_readmit, sprintf("frailty(%s)", CLUSTER_VAR)), strata_readmit, "Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status)")
  frail_fit <- tryCatch(coxph(ff, data = d1), error = function(e){message(e); NULL})
  if (!is.null(frail_fit)) print(frail_fit)
}
cat("\nReading: if the center frailty reduces AIC and theta > 0 in a non‑trivial way => modeling the center improves the fit;",
    "\nif only the SEs change (robust vs. naive) without improving fit => robust variance is sufficient.\n")

title: SENDA Convenio 1 2010-2022 - Multistate semi-Markov nomogram (step 2.6, best_perf2)
text:
The transition to test is 2->3. General test by Titman & Putter (2022), mstate::MarkovTest: log-rank-type statistics that test whether the intensity of 2->3 depends on the state occupied at previous times (i.e., entry time / sojourn). Complemented with a robust shortcut (entry-time covariate on clock-forward, Wald) in case the installed version of MarkovTest differs.


Code
# (a) Titman & Putter general test on transition 2->3
qsel <- as.numeric(quantile(d3$Tstop[d3$status==1], c(.2,.35,.5,.65,.8), na.rm = TRUE))
markov_TP <- tryCatch(
  mstate::MarkovTest(ms, id = "id", transition = 3, grid = qsel, B = 2000),  # singular!
  error = function(e) { message("MarkovTest failed: ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })
p_TP <- if (!is.null(markov_TP)) markov_TP$p_stat_wb[1] else NA_real_
if (!is.null(markov_TP))
  cat(sprintf("[MarkovTest 2->3] p_stat_wb=%.3g | p_ch_stat_wb=%.3g\n",
              p_TP, markov_TP$p_ch_stat_wb))

# (b) Robust shortcut: entry time as covariate in 2->3 clock-forward (robust Wald)
d3$t_entry <- d3$Tstart
fmk <- mk(c(covs_death, "t_entry"), strata_death, "Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status)")
m_mk <- coxph(add_cluster(fmk), data = d3, robust = TRUE)
p_entry <- summary(m_mk)$coefficients["t_entry","Pr(>|z|)"]
cat(sprintf("\n[2->3] coef(t_entry)=%.4f  p=%.3g\n",
            summary(m_mk)$coefficients["t_entry","coef"], p_entry))

# (c) Cross-check log-rank by entry time tertiles (clock-reset)
d3$entry_tertile <- cut(d3$t_entry, quantile(d3$t_entry, c(0,1/3,2/3,1)),
                        include.lowest = TRUE, labels = c("early","medium","late"))
print(survdiff(Surv(sojourn, status) ~ entry_tertile, data = d3))

p_lr <- 1 - pchisq(survdiff(Surv(sojourn, status) ~ entry_tertile, data = d3)$chisq, df = 2)
SEMI_MARKOV <- (!is.na(p_TP) && p_TP < 0.05) || (p_entry < 0.05)
cat(sprintf("[2->3 Markov] Titman-Putter p=%.3g | entry-time Wald p=%.3g | log-rank p=%.2g\n",
            p_TP, p_entry, p_lr))
cat(if (SEMI_MARKOV)
  "=> Markov rejected in 2->3: clock-reset (semi-Markov) is primary.\n" else
  "=> No evidence against Markov in 2->3: clock-forward (Markov) primary; semi-Markov reported as sensitivity.\n")

title: SENDA Convenio 1 2010-2022 - Multistate semi-Markov nomogram (step 2.6, best_perf2)
text:
For a given covariate profile, trajectories are simulated with clock-reset and state occupancy is reported at 6/12/36/60 months. Primary engine for the app: flexsurv (pmatrix.simfs, with CIs via MVN resampling of coefficients); here a semi-parametric version is included with mstate::mssample on the Cox best_perf2 as reference/validation. Both yield the same quantity: P(state | profile, t).


Code
M_SIM <- 1e5
.haz_for_profile <- function(model, newdata, trans_id) {
  sf <- survfit(model, newdata = newdata)
  hz <- if (!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv),1e-12))
  data.frame(time = sf$time, Haz = hz, trans = trans_id)
}
predict_profile <- function(profile, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), M = M_SIM,
                            models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3), trans = tmat, seed = 2125) {
  set.seed(seed)
  Haz <- rbind(.haz_for_profile(models[[1]], profile, 1L),
               .haz_for_profile(models[[2]], profile, 2L),
               .haz_for_profile(models[[3]], profile, 3L))
  Haz <- Haz[order(Haz$trans, Haz$time),]
  s <- mssample(Haz = Haz, trans = trans, clock = "reset",
                history = list(state = 1, time = 0, tstate = NULL),
                tvec = tvec, M = M, output = "state")
  data.frame(month = tvec,
             p_alive_no_readm = s[["Discharge"]] %||% s[,2],
             p_readmitted     = s[["Readmission"]] %||% s[,3],
             p_dead           = s[["Death"]] %||% s[,4])
}

ref_profile <- function(data, vars) {
  vars <- vars[vars %in% names(data)]
  as.data.frame(setNames(lapply(vars, function(v){
    x <- data[[v]]; if (is.numeric(x)) median(x, na.rm=TRUE)
    else factor(names(sort(table(x),decreasing=TRUE))[1], levels=levels(factor(x)))}), vars))
}
profile_ref <- ref_profile(dat_ms, unique(c(covs_readmit,covs_death,strata_readmit,strata_death)))
probs_ref <- predict_profile(profile_ref)

# Markov / clock-FORWARD occupancy via msfit + probtrans (exact AJ-type, no simulation).
# Reuses m_tr1, m_tr2 (cluster-robust point estimates are unaffected by survfit); only
# the 2->3 transition is refit clock-forward (time from discharge, not sojourn).
m_tr3_fwd <- coxph(add_cluster(f2), data = d3, robust = TRUE, x = TRUE)   # f2 = Surv(Tstart,Tstop,status) ~ covs_death + strata_death

# Build a profile-specific msfit on a common time grid (step carry-forward).
.msfit_profile_fwd <- function(profile, models, trans) {
  raw <- lapply(models, function(m) {
    sf <- survfit(m, newdata = profile)
    ch <- if (!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv), 1e-12))
    data.frame(time = sf$time, Haz = ch)
  })
  ut <- sort(unique(c(0, unlist(lapply(raw, `[[`, "time")))))
  Haz <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(raw), function(k) {
    df <- raw[[k]]; idx <- findInterval(ut, df$time)
    data.frame(time = ut, Haz = ifelse(idx == 0, 0, df$Haz[pmax(idx, 1)]), trans = k)
  }))
  structure(list(Haz = Haz, trans = trans), class = "msfit")
}
predict_profile_markov <- function(profile, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS),
                                   models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd), trans = tmat) {
  pt <- probtrans(.msfit_profile_fwd(profile, models, trans), predt = 0, variance = FALSE)[[1]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(tvec, function(h) {
    i <- which.min(abs(pt$time - h))
    data.frame(month = h, p_alive_no_readm = pt$pstate1[i],
               p_readmitted = pt$pstate2[i], p_dead = pt$pstate3[i])
  }))
}

# Robustness of occupancy to the clock assumption across real risk-spanning profiles.
# Verdict = gap vs the prediction's own Monte-Carlo resolution, not fixed thresholds.
stopifnot(exists("predict_profile"), exists("predict_profile_markov"))  # m_tr3_fwd must exist

# 1. Cheap risk axis from linear predictors (no simulation)
eta_r <- as.numeric(predict(m_tr1, newdata = dat_ms, type = "lp"))
eta_d <- as.numeric(predict(m_tr2, newdata = dat_ms, type = "lp"))
risk  <- as.numeric(scale(eta_r) + scale(eta_d))               # overall "leaves state 1" risk
qp    <- c(.05,.20,.40,.50,.60,.80,.95)
idx   <- vapply(quantile(risk, qp, na.rm=TRUE), function(q) which.min(abs(risk-q)), integer(1))
idx   <- unique(c(which.min(risk), idx, which.max(risk)))      # + the two extremes

# 2. Compare engines at horizons; raise M so MC SE << the differences we care about
M_HI <- 10000L
scan <- do.call(rbind, lapply(idx, function(i){
  prof <- dat_ms[i,,drop=FALSE]
  sm <- predict_profile(prof, tvec=HORIZONS, M=M_HI)           # semi-Markov (mssample)
  mk <- predict_profile_markov(prof, tvec=HORIZONS)            # Markov (probtrans, exact)
  se <- function(p) sqrt(pmax(p*(1-p),0)/M_HI)
  data.frame(profile=i, risk=round(risk[i],2), month=HORIZONS,
    d_alive = mk$p_alive_no_readm - sm$p_alive_no_readm,
    d_readm = mk$p_readmitted     - sm$p_readmitted,
    d_dead  = mk$p_dead           - sm$p_dead,
    mc_floor = 2*pmax(se(sm$p_readmitted), se(sm$p_dead), se(sm$p_alive_no_readm)))
}))
scan$max_abs   <- pmax(abs(scan$d_alive), abs(scan$d_readm), abs(scan$d_dead))
scan$beyond_mc <- scan$max_abs > scan$mc_floor                 # resolvable above sim noise?

# 3. Verdict
cat(sprintf("Max |Δ| over all profiles/states/horizons : %.4f\n", max(scan$max_abs)))
cat(sprintf("Cells where |Δ| exceeds 2·MC-SE          : %d / %d\n", sum(scan$beyond_mc), nrow(scan)))

cat(sprintf("Spearman(risk, max|Δ|)                   : %.3f  (~0 => gap doesn't grow with risk)\n",
            suppressWarnings(cor(scan$risk, scan$max_abs, method="spearman"))))

# Fast apples-to-apples band: MVN draws of Cox coefs (cluster-robust vcov) -> scale each
# transition's cumulative hazard -> probtrans (exact, clock-forward). ~9 s/profile.
# Coefficient-only band (per-stratum baseline held fixed -> mild lower bound).
stopifnot(exists("m_tr3_fwd"))
.z_exact <- function(model, newdata){
  p <- length(coef(model)); if(!p) return(numeric(0)); base <- model; z <- numeric(p)
  for(j in seq_len(p)){ bj<-numeric(p); bj[j]<-1; base$coefficients<-bj
    z[j] <- as.numeric(predict(base, newdata=newdata, type="lp")) }
  setNames(z, names(coef(model)))
}
.mvn0 <- function(V, B){ p<-nrow(V); if(!p) return(matrix(0,B,0))
  matrix(rnorm(B*p), B, p) %*% chol((V + t(V))/2) }

predict_profile_ci_mvn <- function(profile, models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd),
                                   trans = tmat, tvec = HORIZONS, B = 500,
                                   n_grid = 200, cl = 0.95, seed = 2125){
  set.seed(seed); K <- length(models); grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, max(tvec), length.out=n_grid), tvec)))
  base_grid <- sapply(seq_len(K), function(k){              # base cumhaz per transition on thinned grid
    sf <- survfit(models[[k]], newdata = profile)
    ch <- if(!is.null(sf$cumhaz)) as.numeric(sf$cumhaz) else -log(pmax(as.numeric(sf$surv),1e-12))
    idx <- findInterval(grid, sf$time); ifelse(idx==0, 0, ch[pmax(idx,1)]) })
  z <- lapply(models, .z_exact, newdata = profile); Del <- lapply(models, function(m) .mvn0(vcov(m), B))
  hidx <- match(tvec, grid)
  run_pt <- function(sc){
    Hb <- data.frame(time=rep(grid,K), Haz=as.numeric(sweep(base_grid,2,sc,`*`)),
                     trans=rep(seq_len(K), each=length(grid)))
    probtrans(structure(list(Haz=Hb, trans=trans), class="msfit"), predt=0, variance=FALSE)[[1]] }
  pt0 <- run_pt(rep(1,K)); occ <- array(NA_real_, c(B, length(tvec), 3))
  for(b in seq_len(B)){
    sc <- vapply(seq_len(K), function(k) if(length(z[[k]])) exp(sum(z[[k]]*Del[[k]][b,])) else 1, numeric(1))
    pt <- run_pt(sc); occ[b,,1]<-pt$pstate1[hidx]; occ[b,,2]<-pt$pstate2[hidx]; occ[b,,3]<-pt$pstate3[hidx]
  }
  a <- (1-cl)/2
  out <- data.frame(month=tvec, alive=pt0$pstate1[hidx], readm=pt0$pstate2[hidx], dead=pt0$pstate3[hidx])
  for(s in 1:3){ nm<-c("alive","readm","dead")[s]; qq<-apply(occ[,,s],2,quantile,c(a,1-a),na.rm=TRUE)
    out[[paste0(nm,"_lo")]]<-qq[1,]; out[[paste0(nm,"_hi")]]<-qq[2,] }
  out
}

for (pid in c(58565, 55639)) {
  ci <- predict_profile_ci_mvn(dat_ms[pid,,drop=FALSE], B = 500)
  ci$dead_hw <- (ci$dead_hi-ci$dead_lo)/2; ci$readm_hw <- (ci$readm_hi-ci$readm_lo)/2
  gap <- scan[scan$profile==pid, c("month","d_readm","d_dead")]
  tab <- merge(ci[,c("month","dead","dead_hw","readm","readm_hw")], gap, by="month")
  tab$dead_ok <- abs(tab$d_dead) < tab$dead_hw; tab$readm_ok <- abs(tab$d_readm) < tab$readm_hw
  cat(sprintf("\n=== profile %d (risk %.2f) ===\n", pid, scan$risk[scan$profile==pid][1]))
  print(knitr::kable(tab, digits=4))
}

The Markov assumption for the readmission→death transition was not rejected (Titman–Putter test p = 0.57; entry-time Wald p = 0.57; log-rank by entry tertile p = 0.10). Consistent with this, state occupancy under clock-forward vs clock-reset specifications differed by ≤ 1.5 pp, within the 95% parameter-uncertainty interval at all horizons. We therefore adopt the Markov clock-forward specification as primary, with the semi-Markov specification as sensitivity.
Across risk-spanning profiles, the clock specification (Markov vs semi-Markov) shifted state occupancy by ≤ 1.5 percentage points (worst case: highest-risk profile, 36 months), well within the 95% parameter-uncertainty interval (half-width 1.9–5.1 pp) at every horizon. The clock choice is therefore immaterial relative to estimation uncertainty; we adopt the Markov clock-forward specification as primary and report the semi-Markov specification as a sensitivity analysis.

# Marginal occupancy = average of EXACT Markov predictions by profile (no precompute -> no bias).
# Speedups vs original: (a) n_sub=1000 (the average is already stable; ~3x faster),
# (b) parallel with future.apply -> ON WINDOWS mclapply does NOT fork (falls back to serial); future does.
# Same numeric result as the serial version.
if (!requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("future.apply", repos = "https://cran.dcc.uchile.cl/")
library(future.apply)
plan(multisession, workers = min(6L, future::availableCores()))   # multiple cores; cap by memory

marginal_averaged <- function(data, n_sub = 2000, tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), seed = 2125,
                              models = list(m_tr1, m_tr2, m_tr3_fwd)) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sub <- data[sample.int(nrow(data), min(n_sub, nrow(data))), , drop = FALSE]   # only the subset travels to the workers
  preds <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i) {
    s <- predict_profile_markov(sub[i, , drop = FALSE], tvec = tvec, models = models)  # exact, event grid
    as.matrix(s[, c("p_alive_no_readm","p_readmitted","p_dead")])
  }, future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival","mstate"))
  acc <- Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)
  data.frame(month = tvec, p_alive_no_readm = acc[,1], p_readmitted = acc[,2], p_dead = acc[,3])
}

text:
This is a sensitivity analysis, not the nomogram’s engine. Flexible parametric models (flexsurvspline, Royston–Parmar) are fit per transition on gap time (so this run is semi-Markov) without strata() and without cluster-robust variance. It therefore diverges from the primary specification on clock, strata, and center clustering — by design. Its value: if a fully parametric, differently-specified family yields similar state occupancy to the primary Cox + probtrans (Markov) engine, that is robustness to the modelling family. The nomogram’s online engine and CIs come from the serialized Cox transition models + probtrans (Markov clock-forward) + the cluster-robust MVN band, not from pmatrix.simfs.

# Gap-time por transicion (Tstart=0 en 1->2 y 1->3 => clock-forward; sojourn en 2->3 => reset).
ms$gap <- pmax(ms$Tstop - ms$Tstart, eps)
rhs_fs <- function(covs) paste(covs, collapse = " + ")
fs_fit <- function(tr, covs, k = 2) {
  dd <- ms[ms$trans == tr, ]
  f  <- as.formula(paste("Surv(gap, status) ~", rhs_fs(covs)))
  flexsurvspline(f, data = dd, k = k, scale = "hazard")   # k nodos internos
}
fs12 <- tryCatch(fs_fit(1, covs_readmit), error = function(e){message("fs12: ",conditionMessage(e)); NULL})
fs13 <- tryCatch(fs_fit(2, covs_death),   error = function(e){message("fs13: ",conditionMessage(e)); NULL})
fs23 <- tryCatch(fs_fit(3, covs_death),   error = function(e){message("fs23: ",conditionMessage(e)); NULL})

fmsm_obj <- NULL
if (!any(sapply(list(fs12,fs13,fs23), is.null))) {
  fmsm_obj <- fmsm(fs12, fs13, fs23, trans = tmat)
  cat("fmsm with 3 transitions using flexsurvspline.\n")
} else message("A flexsurv transition did not converged; check covariates or use mssample instead.")

predict_profile_fs <- function(profile, fmsm_obj, tvec = HORIZONS, M = 10000, B = 200, cl = 0.95) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(tvec, function(h){
    P  <- flexsurv::pmatrix.simfs(fmsm_obj, trans = tmat, t = h, newdata = profile,
                                  M = M, ci = TRUE, B = B, cl = cl)      # <- ci=TRUE + B pasado
    lo <- attr(P, "lower"); hi <- attr(P, "upper")
    data.frame(month = h,
      alive = P[1,1], alive_lo = lo[1,1], alive_hi = hi[1,1],
      readm = P[1,2], readm_lo = lo[1,2], readm_hi = hi[1,2],
      dead  = P[1,3], dead_lo  = lo[1,3], dead_hi  = hi[1,3])
  }))
}

# (88,152) and POOLED across the 5 imputations. The rest of the notebook can keep using imp1;

f3_simple <- as.formula(paste("Surv(Tstart, Tstop, status) ~",
              paste(c(covs_death, "any_phys_dx"), collapse = " + "), "+ strata(plan_type_strata)"))

# 1. Full sample, 5 imputations (rbind train+test reconstructs the 88,152 WITH derived columns)

fit_ms_one <- function(d){
  bad <- with(d, readmit_event==1 & death_event==1 & death_time_from_disch_m < readmit_time_from_disch_m)
  if (any(bad)){ d$readmit_event[bad]<-0; d$readmit_time_from_disch_m[bad]<-d$death_time_from_disch_m[bad] }
  tie <- with(d, readmit_event==1 & death_event==1 & death_time_from_disch_m==readmit_time_from_disch_m)
  if (any(tie)) d$death_time_from_disch_m[tie] <- d$death_time_from_disch_m[tie] + eps
  keep <- unique(c(covs_readmit, covs_death, strata_readmit, strata_death, CLUSTER_VAR))
  keep <- keep[keep %in% names(d)]
  ms_i <- msprep(time = c(NA,"readmit_time_from_disch_m","death_time_from_disch_m"),
                 status = c(NA,"readmit_event","death_event"), data = d, trans = tmat, keep = keep)
  list(m1 = coxph(add_cluster(f1),        data = ms_i[ms_i$trans==1,], robust = TRUE, x = TRUE),  # 1->2
       m2 = coxph(add_cluster(f2),        data = ms_i[ms_i$trans==2,], robust = TRUE, x = TRUE),  # 1->3 (audit d2 pending)
     m3 = coxph(add_cluster(f3_simple), data = ms_i[ms_i$trans==3,], robust = TRUE, x = TRUE))  # 2->3 simplified
}
ms_fits <- lapply(full_imp, fit_ms_one)        # 5 sets {m1,m2,m3}; save with saveRDS for the artifact

# 3. probtrans POOLED: predict per imputation and average (Rubin's Q-bar)
predict_profile_markov_pooled <- function(profile, tvec = HORIZONS, fits = ms_fits){
  preds <- lapply(fits, function(f)
    as.matrix(predict_profile_markov(profile, tvec = tvec,
              models = list(f$m1, f$m2, f$m3))[,c("p_alive_no_readm","p_readmitted","p_dead")]))
  acc <- Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)
  data.frame(month = tvec, p_alive_no_readm = acc[,1], p_readmitted = acc[,2], p_dead = acc[,3])
}

# 4. (optional) POOLED CI band by Rubin: within = mean MVN variance; between = variance of the 5 points
predict_profile_ci_mvn_pooled <- function(profile, tvec = HORIZONS, B = 500, fits = ms_fits, cl = 0.95){
  z <- qnorm(1-(1-cl)/2); m <- length(fits)
  per <- lapply(fits, function(f) predict_profile_ci_mvn(profile, models = list(f$m1,f$m2,f$m3),
                                                         tvec = tvec, B = B))
  out <- data.frame(month = tvec)
  for (s in c("alive","readm","dead")){
    pts <- sapply(per, function(p) p[[s]])
    hw  <- sapply(per, function(p) (p[[paste0(s,"_hi")]] - p[[paste0(s,"_lo")]])/2)
    qbar <- rowMeans(pts); within <- rowMeans((hw/z)^2); between <- apply(pts, 1, var)
    total <- within + (1 + 1/m)*between                              # Rubin total variance
    out[[s]] <- qbar; out[[paste0(s,"_lo")]] <- qbar - z*sqrt(total); out[[paste0(s,"_hi")]] <- qbar + z*sqrt(total)
  }
  out
}

marginal_averaged_pool <- function(imp_list = full_imp, fits = ms_fits, n_sub = 1000,
                                   tvec = c(3, HORIZONS), seed = 2125){
  set.seed(seed); idx <- sample.int(nrow(imp_list[[1]]), min(n_sub, nrow(imp_list[[1]])))
  per_imp <- lapply(seq_along(fits), function(m){
    sub  <- imp_list[[m]][idx, , drop = FALSE]
    mods <- list(fits[[m]]$m1, fits[[m]]$m2, fits[[m]]$m3)
    preds <- future_lapply(seq_len(nrow(sub)), function(i)
      as.matrix(predict_profile_markov(sub[i, , drop = FALSE], tvec = tvec, models = mods)[
                , c("p_alive_no_readm","p_readmitted","p_dead")]),
      future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival","mstate"))
    Reduce(`+`, preds) / length(preds)                       # marginal de la imputacion m
  })
  acc <- Reduce(`+`, per_imp) / length(per_imp)              # Rubin Q-barra sobre imputaciones
  data.frame(month = tvec, alive_pred = acc[,1], readm_pred = acc[,2], dead_pred = acc[,3])
}

Markov: the formal test is Titman & Putter on 2->3 (MarkovTest); the entry-time shortcut is the robust backup. If Markov is rejected, clock-reset is primary.
vce(center_id): robust inflates/adjusts SE without changing coefficients; the center frailty tells if modeling the cluster improves fit (AIC/theta). Report both.
Whole-sample: marginal probabilities are computed over the entire cohort (non-parametric Aalen-Johansen and/or average of individual predictions). The nomogram uses the profile-specific calculation.
flexsurv fits offline and predicts online (MVN CIs), avoiding refitting per click and filtering test. USE_SYNTHETIC<-FALSE plugs in real data.

text:
The four delta chunks are consumers: they read dual_fits[[nm]]$raw_predictions and extract per-subject predictions; they never re-fit Cox. That makes paired bootstrap cheap.
It is separate from the scattered evaluate_dual_cox_python_style() calls for three reasons: 1. Common grid. GRID <- c(3,6,12,36,60) is applied to all specs at once. ÃŽâ€IBS is only valid when both objects integrate over the same grid. 2. Intact predictions. Saved objects elsewhere are stripped via .strip_raw() to keep RDS small. Cell 72 leaves predictions intact, which is required for OOF reconstruction. 3. Valid pairing. All five models are fit in one loop over the same py_corrected_datasets_boot and k_folds = 5. This guarantees the paired delta chunks compare identical folds, imputations, and subjects.
Why run it first: Cell 72 now validates and loads the intact common-grid OOF predictions from pred22_ndp_2026_07_13__dualfits.rds by default. These predictions already contain the fixed-strata fits and are unaffected by the IBS lookup error. Cox models are refit only if DELTAC_IBS_REFIT <- TRUE; a formula or grid mismatch stops rather than silently reusing stale fits. For the IBS repair, run cells 8, 9, 72, 76, 77 and 89.

clean_strata <- function(f) stats::as.formula(gsub("strat\\(","strata(",paste(deparse(f),collapse=" ")))
.formula_key <- function(f) {
  txt <- if (is.character(f)) paste(f,collapse=" ") else paste(deparse(f),collapse=" ")
  gsub("[[:space:]]+","",txt)
}

if (!DELTAC_IBS_REFIT && file.exists(DELTAC_IBS_CACHE)) {
  .cached <- readRDS(DELTAC_IBS_CACHE)

    expected_d <- .formula_key(clean_strata(specs[[nm]][[2]]))

        !identical(.formula_key(fit$config$formula_death),expected_d))
      stop("Cached common-grid formulas differ from the current specs; set DELTAC_IBS_REFIT <- TRUE.")
  }
  cat("Loaded validated common-grid raw predictions; Cox refitting was skipped.\n")
  rm(.cached)
} else {
  dual_fits <- list()
  for (nm in names(specs)) {
    fr <- specs[[nm]][[1]]; fd <- specs[[nm]][[2]]
    if (is.null(fr) || is.null(fd)) { message("skip ", nm); next }

      formula_readmit = clean_strata(fr), formula_death = clean_strata(fd),

# Build or reuse a DS-only common-grid cache without changing the validated primary p225 object.

= FALSE)

if (!exists(".p225_input_manifest", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) stop("The canonical input manifest is unavailable. Rerun
load-data.", call. = FALSE)
if (!is.list(py_corrected_datasets_boot) || length(py_corrected_datasets_boot) != 5L) stop("Expected exactly five canonical
imputations.", call. = FALSE)
DS_GRID <- c(3, 6, 12, 36, 60)
DS_FOLDS <- 5L
DS_SEED <- 2125L
DS_OUT_DIR <- file.path(project_root, "data", "20241015_out")

# Select the newest complete p24 DS sidecar set and reject incomplete or mixed stems.
ds_suffixes <- c("dual_shap_ds_py", "dual_shap_ds_upd_py", "dual_shap_ds_int_py")
ds_pattern <- paste0("^pred24.*__(", paste(ds_suffixes, collapse = "|"), ")\\.rds$")
ds_sidecar_files <- list.files(DS_OUT_DIR, pattern = ds_pattern, full.names = TRUE)
if (length(ds_sidecar_files) == 0L) stop("No p24 DS sidecars were found in: ", DS_OUT_DIR, call. = FALSE)
ds_sidecar_names <- basename(ds_sidecar_files)
ds_sidecar_stems <- sub(paste0("__(?:", paste(ds_suffixes, collapse = "|"), ")\\.rds$"), "", ds_sidecar_names, perl = TRUE)
ds_complete_stems <- unique(ds_sidecar_stems[vapply(unique(ds_sidecar_stems), function(stem) {
  expected <- file.path(DS_OUT_DIR, paste0(stem, "__", ds_suffixes, ".rds"))
  all(file.exists(expected))
}, logical(1))])
if (length(ds_complete_stems) == 0L) stop("No complete p24 DS sidecar triplet was found.", call. = FALSE)
ds_stem_mtime <- vapply(ds_complete_stems, function(stem) {
  expected <- file.path(DS_OUT_DIR, paste0(stem, "__", ds_suffixes, ".rds"))
  max(file.info(expected)$mtime)
}, as.POSIXct("1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"))
DS_SIDECAR_STEM <- ds_complete_stems[which.max(ds_stem_mtime)]
DS_SIDECAR_PATHS <- stats::setNames(file.path(DS_OUT_DIR, paste0(DS_SIDECAR_STEM, "__", ds_suffixes, ".rds")), c("base", "nph",
"interact"))
DS_CACHE <- file.path(DS_OUT_DIR, paste0("pred225_ds_common_grid__", DS_SIDECAR_STEM, "__v1.rds"))
DS_REFIT <- !file.exists(DS_CACHE)
# Parse character formulas stored by p24 sidecars and validate their required variables before fitting.
.ds_formula_key <- function(formula_object) {
  formula_object <- .ds_parse_formula(formula_object, "DS formula comparison")
  gsub("[[:space:]]+", "", paste(deparse(formula_object), collapse = " "))
}
.ds_parse_formula <- function(formula_value, label) {
  formula_object <- if (inherits(formula_value, "formula")) {
    formula_value
  } else if (is.character(formula_value) && length(formula_value) == 1L && nzchar(formula_value)) {
    stats::as.formula(formula_value, env = .GlobalEnv)
  } else {
    stop("Invalid DS formula in ", label, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!inherits(formula_object, "formula")) stop("Could not parse DS formula in ", label, ".", call. = FALSE)
  formula_object
}
.ds_extract_sidecar_formulas <- function(path, label) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing DS sidecar: ", path, call. = FALSE)
  sidecar <- readRDS(path)
  if (!is.list(sidecar) || !is.list(sidecar$results) || !is.list(sidecar$results$risk) || !is.list(sidecar$results$risk$config)) {
    stop("DS sidecar has no risk configuration: ", basename(path), call. = FALSE)
  }
  config <- sidecar$results$risk$config
  if (!identical(as.numeric(config$eval_times), DS_GRID)) {
    stop("DS sidecar grid differs from the required common grid in ", basename(path), ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  out <- list(
    formula_readmit = .ds_parse_formula(config$formula_readmit, paste(label, "readmission")),
    formula_death = .ds_parse_formula(config$formula_death, paste(label, "death"))
  )
  rm(sidecar, config)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  out
}
ds_formula_sets <- lapply(names(DS_SIDECAR_PATHS), function(label) {
  .ds_extract_sidecar_formulas(DS_SIDECAR_PATHS[[label]], label)
})
names(ds_formula_sets) <- names(DS_SIDECAR_PATHS)
ds_common_columns <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(py_corrected_datasets_boot, names))
ds_outcome_columns <- c("readmit_time_from_disch_m", "readmit_event", "death_time_from_disch_m", "death_event")
for (model_name in names(ds_formula_sets)) {
  for (outcome_name in c("readmission", "death")) {
    formula_name <- if (outcome_name == "readmission") "formula_readmit" else "formula_death"
    required_predictors <- setdiff(all.vars(ds_formula_sets[[model_name]][[formula_name]]), ds_outcome_columns)
    missing_predictors <- setdiff(required_predictors, ds_common_columns)
    if (length(missing_predictors) > 0L) {
      stop("DS ", model_name, " ", outcome_name, " formula requires missing predictor(s): ", paste(missing_predictors, collapse = ", "),
      call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
# Define outcome-specific candidates so only the target outcome changes in each comparison.
ds_specs <- list(
  ds_base = list(formula_readmit = ds_formula_sets$base$formula_readmit, formula_death = ds_formula_sets$base$formula_death),
  ds_nph_readmit = list(formula_readmit = ds_formula_sets$nph$formula_readmit, formula_death = ds_formula_sets$base$formula_death),
  ds_interact_readmit = list(formula_readmit = ds_formula_sets$interact$formula_readmit, formula_death =
  ds_formula_sets$base$formula_death),
  ds_nph_death = list(formula_readmit = ds_formula_sets$base$formula_readmit, formula_death = ds_formula_sets$nph$formula_death),
  ds_interact_death = list(formula_readmit = ds_formula_sets$base$formula_readmit, formula_death =
  ds_formula_sets$interact$formula_death)
)
.ds_specs_signature <- lapply(ds_specs, function(specification) {
  c(readmission = .ds_formula_key(specification$formula_readmit), death = .ds_formula_key(specification$formula_death))
})
# Verify that the current canonical input has the same observed outcomes and row order as the primary OOF cache.
.ds_extract_raw_outcomes <- function(fit, outcome, imputation_index) {
  raw_predictions <- fit$raw_predictions
  blocks <- Filter(function(block) identical(as.integer(block$imp_idx), as.integer(imputation_index)), raw_predictions)
  if (length(blocks) != DS_FOLDS) stop("Primary cache has an unexpected number of OOF blocks for imputation ", imputation_index, ".",
  call. = FALSE)
  n_rows <- max(vapply(blocks, function(block) max(block$original_val_idx), integer(1)))
  time <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
  event <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
  for (block in blocks) {
    outcome_block <- block[[outcome]]
    if (is.null(outcome_block) || !is.null(outcome_block$error) || is.null(outcome_block$y_val)) stop("Primary cache has incomplete ",
    outcome, " OOF predictions.", call. = FALSE)
    index <- as.integer(block$original_val_idx)
    y_val <- as.matrix(outcome_block$y_val)
    time[index] <- as.numeric(y_val[, 1L])
    event[index] <- as.numeric(y_val[, 2L])
  }
  list(time = time, event = event)
}
if (exists("dual_fits", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE) && is.list(dual_fits) && !is.null(dual_fits$base$raw_predictions)) {

    stop("Canonical input outcomes do not match the validated primary OOF cache for imputation ", imputation_index, ".", call. = FALSE)

}
.ds_validate_cached_fit <- function(fit, specification, model_name) {
  if (is.null(fit$raw_predictions) || length(fit$raw_predictions) != length(py_corrected_datasets_boot) * DS_FOLDS) {
    stop("Cached DS fit has incomplete raw predictions: ", model_name, call. = FALSE)

    stop("Cached DS formulas differ for ", model_name, ". Delete only the DS cache after confirming the intended new specification.",
    call. = FALSE)

    stop("Cached DS folds differ from the validated primary OOF folds for ", model_name, ".", call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
.ds_evaluate_sequentially <- function(specification, model_name) {
  old_options <- options(dualcox.concordance_score = "lp", dualcox.concordance_within_strata = FALSE)
