# ===========================================================================
# ANNEX 2 of 4. NULL MODEL AND IPA. Runs after p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev.
# Nothing is refitted: it reuses the four scored objects that chunk left in the
# session, so it costs seconds. It ADDS a table, ibs_dev_ipa_table; it does not
# modify ibs_dev_table.
# WHY. A raw IBS is a level, not a skill. Two levels computed on different
# cohorts cannot be compared, because the difficulty of the cohort sits inside
# them: a cohort with fewer events gets a lower Brier score whatever the model
# does. The null is the intercept-only marginal curve, estimated on the same data
# and scored with the SAME weights, grid and integral as the model, and IPA, the
# index of prediction accuracy, is 1 - IBS_model / IBS_null. That ratio is what
# makes development, held-out and external results comparable.
# The interval is PAIRED: model and null share every resample, so the difficulty
# of the resampled cohort moves both terms together and largely cancels.
# The readmission null follows the estimand, as it must. A competing-risk model is
# compared against an Aalen-Johansen null and a cause-specific model against a
# Kaplan-Meier null; crossing them would make the skill meaningless.
# EXPECT SMALL IPA FOR MORTALITY. With about 4 percent of subjects dying, the
# marginal curve already scores well on the Brier scale, so the achievable skill
# is small by construction. That is a property of a rare outcome, not evidence of
# a poor model, and the manuscript should say so before a reviewer reads it the
# other way.
# ===========================================================================
.t0 <- proc.time()
stopifnot(exists("ibs_dev_readmit_cs"), exists("ibs_dev_readmit_aj"),
          exists("ibs_dev_death_full"), exists("ibs_dev_death_shap"),
          exists("ANNEXD_GRID"), exists("ANNEXD_HORIZONS"), exists("ANNEXD_B"),
          exists("ANNEXD_SEED"), exists(".N_dev"),
          exists(".rt"), exists(".re"), exists(".dt"), exists(".de"))
# The competing-risk marginal curves live in ibs_window_bootstrap_holdout.R, which
# ibs_classical_holdout.R otherwise resolves lazily through project_root and fails
# to find when the working directory is the cons folder.
if (!exists(".ibsb_marg_aj_surv") || !exists(".ibsb_marg_km")) {
  .r <- if (exists("project_root", inherits = TRUE) &&
            dir.exists(file.path(project_root, "cons", "_alt_scripts"))) project_root else
    { .cw <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
      if (grepl("/cons$", .cw)) dirname(.cw) else .cw }
  source(file.path(.r, "cons", "_alt_scripts", "ibs_window_bootstrap_holdout.R"))
}
stopifnot(exists("ibs_classical_null"), exists("ibs_classical_skill_boot"),
          exists(".ibsb_marg_km"), exists(".ibsb_marg_aj_surv"))
# ---- 1. Prediction shells ------------------------------------------------------
# ibs_classical_null only reads nrow(pred$S) to know how many rows to broadcast
# the marginal curve over, and takes the grid from pred$grid, so a one-column
# shell is enough and no second n x grid matrix is allocated here.
.shell <- matrix(0, .N_dev, 1L)
.shell_death <- list(S = .shell, grid = ANNEXD_GRID,
  y_test = data.frame(time = .dt, event = .de),
  y_train = data.frame(time = .dt, event = .de))
.shell_readmit <- list(S = .shell, grid = ANNEXD_GRID,
  rt_val = .rt, re_val = .re, dt_val = .dt, de_val = .de,
  rt_tr = .rt, re_tr = .re, dt_tr = .dt, de_tr = .de)
# ---- 2. Nulls -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mortality: one Kaplan-Meier null serves both specifications, because the null
# depends on the outcome and the cohort, not on the covariates of either model.
ibs_dev_null_death <- ibs_classical_null(.shell_death,
  horizons = ANNEXD_HORIZONS, outcome = "death")
ibs_dev_null_readmit_cs <- ibs_classical_null(.shell_readmit,
  horizons = ANNEXD_HORIZONS, outcome = "readmit", method = "ipcw")
ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj <- ibs_classical_null(.shell_readmit,
  horizons = ANNEXD_HORIZONS, outcome = "readmit", method = "aalen-johansen")
rm(.shell, .shell_death, .shell_readmit); invisible(gc())
# The null must be scored on the same rows as the model, otherwise the ratio is
# not a skill. Assert it rather than trust it.
stopifnot(nrow(ibs_dev_null_death$contrib_trapezoid) == nrow(ibs_dev_death_full$contrib_trapezoid),
          nrow(ibs_dev_null_readmit_cs$contrib_trapezoid) == nrow(ibs_dev_readmit_cs$contrib_trapezoid),
          nrow(ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj$contrib_trapezoid) == nrow(ibs_dev_readmit_aj$contrib_trapezoid))
# A model that cannot beat its own marginal curve has no skill at that horizon.
# Say it out loud instead of leaving a negative IPA to be noticed in a table.
for (.p in list(list("readmission cause-specific", ibs_dev_readmit_cs, ibs_dev_null_readmit_cs),
                list("readmission competing-risk", ibs_dev_readmit_aj, ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj),
                list("death-full", ibs_dev_death_full, ibs_dev_null_death),
                list("death-shap", ibs_dev_death_shap, ibs_dev_null_death))) {
  .bad <- which(.p[[2]]$ibs$ibs >= .p[[3]]$ibs$ibs)
  if (length(.bad))
    warning(sprintf("%s: IBS is at or above its null at horizon(s) %s, so IPA is not positive there.",
                    .p[[1]], paste(ANNEXD_HORIZONS[.bad], collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE)
}
# ---- 3. IPA with a paired bootstrap ---------------------------------------------
# Arm keys are the same four strings the other annex chunks join on.
.skill_row <- function(pt, pt_null, arm, estimand) {
  s <- ibs_classical_skill_boot(pt, pt_null, B = ANNEXD_B, seed = ANNEXD_SEED,
                                label = arm, verbose = FALSE)
  data.frame(arm = arm, estimand = estimand, horizon_months = s$horizon_months,
             ibs_oof = s$ibs, ibs_null = s$ibs_null,
             ipa = s$ibs_skill, ipa_lo95 = s$skill_lo, ipa_hi95 = s$skill_hi,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}
ibs_dev_ipa_table <- rbind(
  .skill_row(ibs_dev_readmit_cs, ibs_dev_null_readmit_cs, "readmission-cs",
             "death as censoring (cause-specific), Kaplan-Meier null"),
  .skill_row(ibs_dev_readmit_aj, ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj, "readmission-aj",
             "death as definitive non-event (competing risk), Aalen-Johansen null"),
  .skill_row(ibs_dev_death_full, ibs_dev_null_death, "death-full",
             "all-cause mortality, Kaplan-Meier null"),
  .skill_row(ibs_dev_death_shap, ibs_dev_null_death, "death-shap",
             "all-cause mortality, Kaplan-Meier null"))
# The IBS column here must be the same number the previous chunk reported. If it
# is not, the two tables are describing different objects and neither can be read.
if (exists("ibs_dev_table")) {
  .j <- merge(ibs_dev_ipa_table[, c("arm", "horizon_months", "ibs_oof")],
              ibs_dev_table[, c("arm", "horizon_months", "ibs_oof")],
              by = c("arm", "horizon_months"), suffixes = c("_ipa", "_dev"))
  if (nrow(.j) != nrow(ibs_dev_ipa_table))
    stop("Arm or horizon keys do not line up with ibs_dev_table; re-run p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev.", call. = FALSE)
  .d <- max(abs(.j$ibs_oof_ipa - .j$ibs_oof_dev), na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("Consistency with the preceding table: max |difference| in IBS = %.3e\n", .d))
  if (!is.finite(.d) || .d > 1e-12)
    stop("The IBS in this table does not match the preceding one; the point objects changed between chunks.", call. = FALSE)
}
# ---- 4. Export -------------------------------------------------------------------
if (exists(".annex_out_dir") && dir.exists(.annex_out_dir))
  utils::write.csv(ibs_dev_ipa_table,
    file.path(.annex_out_dir, "pred225_annex_ibs_null_ipa_oof_development.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
.elapsed <- proc.time() - .t0
cat(sprintf("\n[chunk: %s] %.1f sec\n", "p225-annex-ibs-null-ipa", .elapsed["elapsed"]))
print(knitr::kable(ibs_dev_ipa_table, "markdown", digits = 6, caption = sprintf(
  "Annex. Intercept-only null integrated Brier score and index of prediction accuracy (IPA = 1 - IBS/IBS null), out of fold on the development cohort (n = %s, the 80 percent training split), on the same classical integral, grid, weights and fold partition as the preceding table. The null is the marginal curve estimated on the same data and scored identically, so the comparison isolates what the covariates add. IPA intervals are paired bootstrap percentiles, model and null sharing every resample, which is what makes cohort difficulty cancel. Raw IBS levels are not comparable across cohorts; IPA is the quantity to carry into any comparison with held-out or external results. The readmission null follows the estimand of its arm: Kaplan-Meier for the cause-specific arm, Aalen-Johansen for the competing-risk arm. Mortality IPA is small by construction because roughly 4 percent of the cohort dies, so the marginal curve is already accurate on the Brier scale; that is a property of a rare outcome, not a deficiency of the model. Abbreviations: IBS, integrated Brier score; IPA, index of prediction accuracy; OOF, out of fold.",
  format(.N_dev, big.mark = ","))))
# ---- 5. All-arm IPA extension matching the comprehensive paired sweep -------
.t_ipa_all <- proc.time()
stopifnot(exists("ibs_dev_pairwise_points"), exists("ibs_dev_pairwise_arm_metadata"), exists(".annexp_bootstrap_points", mode = "function"), exists("ANNEXP_B"), exists("ANNEXP_SEED"), exists("ANNEXP_WORKERS"), identical(ANNEXP_HORIZONS, c(6, 12, 36, 60)))
.annexp_null_shell <- matrix(0, .N_dev, 1L)
.annexp_null_readmit_pred <- list(S = .annexp_null_shell, grid = ANNEXD_GRID, n_imp = length(.dev), rt_val = .rt, re_val = .re, dt_val = .dt, de_val = .de, rt_tr = .rt, re_tr = .re, dt_tr = .dt, de_tr = .de)
.annexp_null_death_pred <- list(S = .annexp_null_shell, grid = ANNEXD_GRID, n_imp = length(.dev), y_test = data.frame(time = .dt, event = .de), y_train = data.frame(time = .dt, event = .de))
ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj_all <- ibs_classical_null(.annexp_null_readmit_pred, horizons = ANNEXP_HORIZONS, outcome = "readmit", method = "aalen-johansen"); ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj_all$method <- "readmission-aj"
ibs_dev_null_death_all <- ibs_classical_null(.annexp_null_death_pred, horizons = ANNEXP_HORIZONS, outcome = "death"); ibs_dev_null_death_all$method <- "death"
rm(.annexp_null_shell, .annexp_null_readmit_pred, .annexp_null_death_pred); invisible(gc())
.annexp_skill_points <- c(ibs_dev_pairwise_points, list(`null::readmission-aj` = ibs_dev_null_readmit_aj_all, `null::death` = ibs_dev_null_death_all))
cat(sprintf("Running one shared, parallel model-null bootstrap for %d model arms and two nulls, B = %d.\n", length(ibs_dev_pairwise_points), ANNEXP_B)); flush.console()
ibs_dev_ipa_all_boot_replicates <- .annexp_bootstrap_points(.annexp_skill_points, ANNEXP_B, ANNEXP_SEED + 100000L, ANNEXP_WORKERS)
.annexp_skill_quantile <- function(values, probability) apply(values, 1L, function(x) { finite <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(finite) < 20L) NA_real_ else stats::quantile(finite, probs = probability, names = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) })
.annexp_skill_rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ibs_dev_pairwise_arm_metadata)), function(metadata_index) {
  metadata <- ibs_dev_pairwise_arm_metadata[metadata_index, , drop = FALSE]; arm <- metadata$arm; null_arm <- if (metadata$outcome == "readmission") "null::readmission-aj" else "null::death"
  model_point <- ibs_dev_pairwise_points[[arm]]$ibs$ibs; null_point <- .annexp_skill_points[[null_arm]]$ibs$ibs
  model_boot <- ibs_dev_ipa_all_boot_replicates[arm, , , drop = TRUE]; null_boot <- ibs_dev_ipa_all_boot_replicates[null_arm, , , drop = TRUE]; skill_boot <- 1 - model_boot / null_boot
  data.frame(outcome = metadata$outcome, model = metadata$model, prediction_definition = metadata$prediction_definition, arm = arm, horizon_months = ANNEXP_HORIZONS, ibs_oof = model_point, ibs_lo95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(model_boot, 0.025), ibs_hi95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(model_boot, 0.975), ibs_null = null_point, ibs_null_lo95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(null_boot, 0.025), ibs_null_hi95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(null_boot, 0.975), ipa = 1 - model_point / null_point, ipa_lo95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(skill_boot, 0.025), ipa_hi95 = .annexp_skill_quantile(skill_boot, 0.975), bootstrap_requested = ANNEXP_B, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
})
ibs_dev_ipa_all_table <- do.call(rbind, .annexp_skill_rows)
ibs_dev_ipa_all_table <- ibs_dev_ipa_all_table[order(ibs_dev_ipa_all_table$outcome, ibs_dev_ipa_all_table$model, ibs_dev_ipa_all_table$prediction_definition, ibs_dev_ipa_all_table$horizon_months), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(ibs_dev_ipa_all_table) <- NULL
stopifnot(nrow(ibs_dev_ipa_all_table) == 56L, all(ibs_dev_ipa_all_table$bootstrap_requested == ANNEXP_B))
.annexp_point_control <- merge(ibs_dev_ipa_all_table[, c("arm", "horizon_months", "ibs_oof")], do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ibs_dev_pairwise_points), function(arm) data.frame(arm = arm, horizon_months = ibs_dev_pairwise_points[[arm]]$ibs$horizon_months, ibs_pairwise = ibs_dev_pairwise_points[[arm]]$ibs$ibs, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))), by = c("arm", "horizon_months"), all = FALSE)

# ===========================================================================
# ANNEX 3 of 4. SENSITIVITY ON THE INTERVAL, NOT ON THE ESTIMATE.
# The annex bootstrap holds the censoring distribution G fixed at its pooled
# development estimate and resamples only the precomputed per-subject
# contributions. That is what makes B = 1000 on a 240-node grid affordable, and it
# keeps the PAIRED comparisons exact, because every arm in a replicate is then
# weighted identically. What it does not do is propagate the uncertainty of having
# ESTIMATED G, so the marginal interval of each IBS is narrower than it should be
# by an unknown amount. This chunk re-estimates G inside every replicate and
# prints both widths side by side.
# NO POINT ESTIMATE MOVES. IBS, null IBS and IPA are full-sample quantities and
# are not recomputed here. Only the interval width changes.
# WHY FIXED G IS STILL RIGHT WHERE IT IS USED. For the paired difference between
# the two mortality specifications, and for IPA, both terms share whatever G the
# replicate has, so the contrast isolates the model and not the weights. Fixed G
# is wrong only for the marginal interval of a single IBS. The two designs
# complement each other; neither replaces the other.
# EVERY ARM KEEPS ITS OWN G, ALWAYS. The four arms are scored on the same subjects
# but on different observed sides, so their censoring distributions are genuinely
# different objects: the mortality arms censor on death, the cause-specific
# readmission arm censors on readmission, and the competing-risk arm censors
# administratively on the first event. Forcing a common G across them would not be
# a harmonisation, it would misweight three of the four.
# WHY THE SURVIVAL MATRICES ARE NEEDED. Re-weighting requires the per-subject
# survival curves; contrib_trapezoid is already G-weighted and trapezoided and
# cannot be re-weighted. The preceding chunk keeps them as S_oof_* when
# ANNEXD_KEEP_S is TRUE. If they are absent, for instance after a cache hit, they
# are refitted here on the same fold partition, which is the slow branch.
# HOW IT IS AFFORDABLE AT n = 70,521. The weight factorises: subjects still at
# risk at a node share the single factor 1/G(t0), and subjects past their own
# event carry 1/G(their time). Writing the contribution as
#   c_j = (1/G(t0_j)) * sum_i A_ij + sum_i B_ij / G(t_i-)
# with A and B free of G, every replicate becomes two matrix-vector products and
# the n x grid matrix is never rebuilt inside the loop. The identity is asserted
# against the engine's own contributions on the first replicates.
# ===========================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
.t0 <- proc.time()
stopifnot(exists("ibs_dev_readmit_cs"), exists("ibs_dev_readmit_aj"),
          exists("ibs_dev_death_full"), exists("ibs_dev_death_shap"),
          exists("ANNEXD_GRID"), exists("ANNEXD_HORIZONS"), exists("ANNEXD_B"),
          exists("ANNEXD_SEED"), exists(".N_dev"),
          exists(".rt"), exists(".re"), exists(".dt"), exists(".de"),
          exists(".ibc_trap_weights"), exists(".ibsb_cr"), exists("ibs_classical_boot_ci"))
GSENS_B    <- ANNEXD_B
GSENS_SEED <- ANNEXD_SEED
GSENS_GMIN <- 0.05
GSENS_EPS  <- 1e-8
# ---- 1. Fast and slow censoring lookups -----------------------------------------
# The engine evaluates G with summary(survfit, times =, extend = TRUE), which is
# correct but far too slow to call once per replicate. The fast version returns
# the same step function through findInterval. The equality is ASSERTED per arm,
# not assumed: a silent mismatch would make this table incomparable to the annex.
.g_step <- function(time, cens_event, g_min = GSENS_GMIN) {
  f <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, cens_event) ~ 1, conf.type = "none")
  ft <- f$time; fs <- f$surv
  function(x) {
    if (!length(ft)) return(rep(1, length(x)))
    i <- findInterval(as.numeric(x), ft)
    v <- rep(1, length(x)); v[i > 0L] <- fs[i[i > 0L]]
    pmax(v, g_min)
  }
}
.g_slow <- function(time, cens_event, g_min = GSENS_GMIN) {
  sf <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, cens_event) ~ 1)
  function(x) {
    req <- pmax(as.numeric(x), 0); u <- sort(unique(req))
    g <- as.numeric(summary(sf, times = u, extend = TRUE)$surv)
    pmax(g[match(req, u)], g_min)
  }
}
# ---- 2. Recover the out-of-fold survival matrices --------------------------------
.need_refit <- !exists("S_oof_readmit") || !exists("S_oof_death_full") || !exists("S_oof_death_shap")
if (.need_refit) {
  cat("Out-of-fold survival matrices are not in the session; refitting on the same fold partition.\n")
  cat("This is the slow branch. Re-run the annex with ANNEXD_KEEP_S <- TRUE to avoid it.\n"); flush.console()
  stopifnot(exists(".dev"), exists("FOLDS"), exists("F_READMIT"),
            exists("F_DEATH_FULL"), exists("F_DEATH_SHAP"))
  if (!requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("future.apply", repos = "https://cran.dcc.uchile.cl/")
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(future.apply))
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 8 * 1024^3)
  .nw <- max(1L, min(if (exists("ANNEXD_WORKERS")) ANNEXD_WORKERS else 5L, future::availableCores() - 1L))
  if (.nw > 1L) future::plan(future::multisession, workers = .nw) else future::plan(future::sequential)
  on.exit(try(future::plan(future::sequential), silent = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  .oof <- function(formula, label) {
    K <- length(ANNEXD_GRID); acc <- matrix(0, .N_dev, K)
    for (im in seq_along(FOLDS)) {
      d <- .dev[[im]]; fl <- FOLDS[[im]]
      r <- future.apply::future_lapply(fl, function(vi) {
        fit <- survival::coxph(formula, data = d[-vi, , drop = FALSE], ties = "efron",
                               x = TRUE, y = TRUE, model = TRUE)
        matrix(as.numeric(pec::predictSurvProb(fit, newdata = d[vi, , drop = FALSE],
                                               times = ANNEXD_GRID)), length(vi), K)
      }, future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival", "pec"))
      for (j in seq_along(fl)) acc[fl[[j]], ] <- acc[fl[[j]], ] + r[[j]]
      rm(r); cat("."); flush.console()
    }
    cat(sprintf(" %s done\n", label)); acc / length(FOLDS)
  }
  if (!exists("S_oof_readmit"))    S_oof_readmit    <- .oof(F_READMIT, "readmission")
  if (!exists("S_oof_death_full")) S_oof_death_full <- .oof(F_DEATH_FULL, "death-full")
  if (!exists("S_oof_death_shap")) S_oof_death_shap <- .oof(F_DEATH_SHAP, "death-shap")
  future::plan(future::sequential)
}
# ---- 3. Arm specifications --------------------------------------------------------
# Per arm: the observed time, who is COUNTED once past their own event, the value
# of Y0 for those counted, the censoring indicator that defines G, the name of the
# survival matrix, and the point object the annex produced. The censoring
# indicators reproduce exactly what the engine builds internally: 1 - event for the
# two single-outcome arms, and first-event administrative censoring for the
# competing-risk arm.
.cr <- .ibsb_cr(.rt, .re, .dt, .de)
GSENS_ARMS <- list(
  list(key = "readmission-cs", pt = ibs_dev_readmit_cs, S = "S_oof_readmit",
       time = .rt, counted = .re == 1L, y0 = rep(0, .N_dev), cens = 1L - .re),
  list(key = "readmission-aj", pt = ibs_dev_readmit_aj, S = "S_oof_readmit",
       time = .cr$ftime, counted = .cr$fstatus %in% c(1L, 2L),
       y0 = as.numeric(.cr$fstatus == 2L), cens = as.integer(.cr$fstatus == 0L)),
  list(key = "death-full", pt = ibs_dev_death_full, S = "S_oof_death_full",
       time = .dt, counted = .de == 1L, y0 = rep(0, .N_dev), cens = 1L - .de),
  list(key = "death-shap", pt = ibs_dev_death_shap, S = "S_oof_death_shap",
       time = .dt, counted = .de == 1L, y0 = rep(0, .N_dev), cens = 1L - .de))
# ---- 4. One arm, both censoring designs, on the SAME resamples ---------------------
.gsens_one <- function(a) {
  pt <- a$pt
  # The working grid is the one the annex actually kept. For readmission the
  # competing-risk builder truncates it at the IPCW tau, so reading it back from
  # brier_curve is the only way to stay aligned with contrib_trapezoid.
  gp <- as.numeric(pt$brier_curve$time_months)
  jj <- match(gp, ANNEXD_GRID); stopifnot(!anyNA(jj))
  Sm <- get(a$S, inherits = TRUE)
  stopifnot(nrow(Sm) == .N_dev, ncol(Sm) == length(ANNEXD_GRID))
  S  <- Sm[, jj, drop = FALSE]
  h  <- pt$horizons; W <- .ibc_trap_weights(gp, h)
  n  <- .N_dev
  tt <- as.numeric(a$time); cnted <- a$counted; y0 <- a$y0
  stopifnot(nrow(pt$contrib_trapezoid) == n, length(tt) == n)
  .gf <- .g_step(tt, a$cens); .gs <- .g_slow(tt, a$cens)
  .probe <- c(gp, pmax(tt - GSENS_EPS, 0))
  .err <- max(abs(.gf(.probe) - .gs(.probe)))
  if (.err > 1e-12)
    stop(sprintf("%s: fast and slow censoring lookups disagree by %.3e; this table would not be comparable to the annex.", a$key, .err), call. = FALSE)
  AR <- outer(tt, gp, ">")
  A  <- AR * (1 - S)^2
  B  <- (!AR & cnted) * (y0 - S)^2
  rm(AR, S); invisible(gc())
  set.seed(GSENS_SEED)
  idx <- lapply(seq_len(GSENS_B), function(b) sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE))
  Cw <- pt$contrib_trapezoid
  fix <- matrix(NA_real_, GSENS_B, length(h)); res <- fix
  ge_full <- 1 / .gf(pmax(tt - GSENS_EPS, 0)); gg_full <- 1 / .gf(gp)
  for (b in seq_len(GSENS_B)) {
    cnt <- tabulate(idx[[b]], nbins = n)
    # Arm A, the annex design: G frozen at the full-sample estimate, read off the
    # already trapezoided contributions. This is what the annex bootstrap does.
    fix[b, ] <- as.numeric(cnt %*% Cw) / n / h
    # Arm B, the sensitivity: G re-estimated on the replicate itself.
    gr <- .g_step(tt[idx[[b]]], a$cens[idx[[b]]])
    cm <- (1 / gr(gp)) * as.numeric(cnt %*% A) +
          as.numeric((cnt / gr(pmax(tt - GSENS_EPS, 0))) %*% B)
    res[b, ] <- as.numeric(cm %*% W) / n / h
    # FAILABLE CHECK on the first replicates: it is the DECOMPOSITION that is being
    # tested, not the arithmetic of any particular draw. Rebuilding the fixed-G
    # value from A and B must equal the engine's trapezoided contributions. If it
    # does not, A and B do not represent the same estimand and nothing below means
    # anything.
    if (b <= 5L) {
      cmf <- gg_full * as.numeric(cnt %*% A) + as.numeric((cnt * ge_full) %*% B)
      .d  <- max(abs(as.numeric(cmf %*% W) / n / h - fix[b, ]), na.rm = TRUE)
      if (!is.finite(.d) || .d > 1e-9)
        stop(sprintf("%s: the factorised reconstruction differs from the annex contributions by %.3e on replicate %d. Do not report this table.", a$key, .d, b), call. = FALSE)
    }
    if (b %% 200L == 0L) { cat(sprintf("  %s: %d/%d\n", a$key, b, GSENS_B)); flush.console() }
  }
  rm(A, B); invisible(gc())
  q <- function(M, p) apply(M, 2, stats::quantile, p, na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  na_h <- is.na(pt$ibs$ibs)
  lo_f <- q(fix, 0.025); hi_f <- q(fix, 0.975)
  lo_r <- q(res, 0.025); hi_r <- q(res, 0.975)
  lo_f[na_h] <- NA_real_; hi_f[na_h] <- NA_real_; lo_r[na_h] <- NA_real_; hi_r[na_h] <- NA_real_
  data.frame(arm = a$key, horizon_months = h, ibs = pt$ibs$ibs,
             ibs_lo_fixed_g = lo_f, ibs_hi_fixed_g = hi_f,
             ibs_lo_resampled_g = lo_r, ibs_hi_resampled_g = hi_r,
             width_fixed_g = hi_f - lo_f, width_resampled_g = hi_r - lo_r,
             width_ratio = (hi_r - lo_r) / (hi_f - lo_f),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}

# the entire input to every bootstrap the engine runs, since a replicate is
# cnt %*% contrib / n / h, so from this file any bootstrap, any B, any seed, any
# paired difference and any skill score can be recomputed in seconds with no Cox
# fitting at all. The nulls are stored for the same reason, otherwise IPA would
# have to be rebuilt from scratch.
# The raw bootstrap replicate matrices are archived too, because the dev chunk set
# options(ibsclassical.keep_replicates = TRUE). That is what lets a reviewer

# ===========================================================================
# ANNEX EXTENSION. READMISSION FULLER VERSUS SHAP-INFORMED, PAIRED DELTA IBS.
# Runs after p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev (which must have run in THIS kernel,
# either refitting or on a cache hit); adds content, replaces nothing.
# The classical annex fixed three specifications (readmission SHAP 26 cov + 2
# strata, death-full 63 + 2, death-shap 14 + 2); the FULLER readmission
# specification was never fitted out of fold, and the two readmission arms
# already scored (readmission-cs, readmission-aj) are two estimands of that
# one SHAP model, not two models. This chunk fits the missing fourth arm on
# the SAME fold partition and computes the paired delta IBS (fuller minus
# SHAP) with ibs_classical_delta_boot, the engine's own paired bootstrap and
# the same function that produced the mortality delta: one shared index list,
# G fixed at the pooled estimate, each replicate a matrix-vector product over
# the precomputed trapezoided contributions. The G sensitivity chunk showed
# fixed G is the correct design for paired contrasts. Because the bootstrap
# reads contrib_trapezoid off the point objects, this chunk does NOT need the
# S_oof_* matrices of the existing arms and does not depend on ANNEXD_KEEP_S;
# the only refit is the fuller arm itself (~5-7 min on 5 workers, ~22 serial).
# MANDATORY CONTROL: before the readmission pair is touched, the mortality
# pair is recomputed and must reproduce the reported deltas bit for bit (same
# function, same seed, deterministic). If it does not, the session state is
# not what this chunk assumes and nothing below is comparable.
# ===========================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
.t0 <- proc.time()
stopifnot(exists("ibs_dev_readmit_cs"), exists("ibs_dev_readmit_aj"),
          exists("ibs_dev_death_full"), exists("ibs_dev_death_shap"),
          exists("ibs_dev_delta_death"), exists("F_READMIT"),
          exists(".dev"), exists("FOLDS"), exists(".N_dev"),
          exists("ANNEXD_GRID"), exists("ANNEXD_HORIZONS"), exists("ANNEXD_B"),
          exists("ANNEXD_SEED"), exists("ANNEXD_STRATA"), exists("ANNEXD_WORKERS"),
          exists(".mk_readmit_pred"), exists("ibs_classical_readmit"),
          exists("ibs_classical_delta_boot"), exists(".annex_out_dir"),
          exists("project_root"))
# ---- 1. Recover the fuller readmission formula --------------------------------
# Verified 2026-07-29: the element is mx$formulas$formula_readmit_updated2 in
# the metrics artifact, deparse-identical to formula_readmit_updated2 in
# _val_inputs/formulas.rds. Priority: session copy, metrics artifact,

# The fit helper asserts the 10 baseline strata on every fold fit (the
# 2026-07-12 strata-demoted-to-covariate failure mode) and rejects NA or
# out-of-range survival. If the annex refitted in this kernel, its helper
# .annex_oof_surv is already here. If the annex hit its cache, that helper
# was never defined, so a verbatim copy is defined locally, the same fallback
# the G sensitivity chunk uses with its .oof; only the fuller arm is fitted.
if (!exists(".annex_oof_surv")) {
  cat("The annex hit its cache, so its refit helper is not in the session; defining the same out-of-fold fit locally (one arm only).\n")
  .annex_oof_surv <- function(formula, dev_list, fold_map, grid,
                              expected_strata = ANNEXD_STRATA, label = "") {
    N <- nrow(dev_list[[1]]); K <- length(grid); S_acc <- matrix(0, N, K)
    for (im in seq_along(fold_map)) {
      d <- dev_list[[im]]; folds <- fold_map[[im]]
      res <- future.apply::future_lapply(folds, function(vi) {
        fit <- survival::coxph(formula, data = d[-vi, , drop = FALSE], ties = "efron",
                               x = TRUE, y = TRUE, model = TRUE)
        bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
        ns <- if (is.null(bh$strata)) 1L else nlevels(droplevels(factor(bh$strata)))
        list(n_strata = ns, S = matrix(as.numeric(
          pec::predictSurvProb(fit, newdata = d[vi, , drop = FALSE], times = grid)),
          length(vi), K))
      }, future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival", "pec"))
      for (j in seq_along(folds)) {
        if (!is.null(expected_strata) && res[[j]]$n_strata != expected_strata)
          stop(sprintf("%s, imputation %d, fold %d: %d baseline strata, expected %d. A strata() term may have been fitted as a covariate.",
                       label, im, j, res[[j]]$n_strata, expected_strata), call. = FALSE)
        S_acc[folds[[j]], ] <- S_acc[folds[[j]], ] + res[[j]]$S
      }
      rm(res); cat("."); flush.console()
    }
    S <- S_acc / length(fold_map)
    if (anyNA(S)) stop(sprintf("%s: out-of-fold survival contains NA; predictSurvProb failed on some fold.", label), call. = FALSE)
    stopifnot(min(S) >= 0, max(S) <= 1)
    cat(sprintf(" %s done\n", label))
    S
  }
}

# ============================================================================
# REBUILD the DeepSurv-informed common-grid cache from the newest prediction24
# sidecars, refitting only the arms whose formula changed.
# Produces ds_dual_fits, ds_specs and DS_CACHE_NEW in the session, and writes
# data/20241015_out/pred225_ds_common_grid__<newest stem>__v1.rds.
# Kernel prerequisites: py_corrected_datasets_boot if you want to avoid a 5.6 GB
# load. Everything else is resolved here.
# Place BEFORE the annex build cells. Never modifies the existing cache.
# ============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
.dsr_t0 <- proc.time()
if (!exists("DSR_FORCE_FULL_REFIT", inherits = TRUE)) DSR_FORCE_FULL_REFIT <- FALSE
DSR_GRID  <- c(3, 6, 12, 36, 60)
DSR_FOLDS <- 5L
DSR_SEED  <- 2125L
# ---- 1. Root and engine ------------------------------------------------------
.dsr_root <- local({
  cand <- character(0)
  if (exists("project_root", inherits = TRUE) && is.character(project_root) &&
      length(project_root) == 1L && !is.na(project_root))
    cand <- c(cand, project_root, sub("(/|\\\\)?cons(/|\\\\)?$", "", project_root))
  pr <- tryCatch(here::here(), error = function(e) NA_character_)
  if (length(pr) == 1L && !is.na(pr)) cand <- c(cand, pr, sub("(/|\\\\)?cons(/|\\\\)?$", "", pr))
  wd <- normalizePath(getwd(), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  cand <- c(cand, wd, sub("(/|\\\\)?cons(/|\\\\)?$", "", wd))
  cand <- unique(cand[nzchar(cand)])
  ok <- cand[vapply(cand, function(p) dir.exists(file.path(p, "data", "20241015_out")), logical(1))]
  if (!length(ok)) stop("annex-ds-refresh: cannot locate the project root.", call. = FALSE)
  normalizePath(ok[1L], winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
})
project_root <- .dsr_root
.dsr_out <- file.path(.dsr_root, "data", "20241015_out")
message("annex-ds-refresh: project root ", .dsr_root)
if (!exists("evaluate_dual_cox_python_style", mode = "function", inherits = TRUE))
  source(file.path(.dsr_root, "cons", "_alt_scripts", "evaluate_dual_cox_python_style_boot.R"))
stopifnot("the dual-Cox engine is unavailable" =
  exists("evaluate_dual_cox_python_style", mode = "function", inherits = TRUE))
# ---- 2. Newest complete sidecar triplet -------------------------------------
.dsr_suf <- c(base = "dual_shap_ds_py", nph = "dual_shap_ds_upd_py", interact = "dual_shap_ds_int_py")
.dsr_all <- list.files(.dsr_out, pattern = paste0("^pred24.*__(", paste(.dsr_suf, collapse = "|"), ")[.]rds$"))
stopifnot("no prediction24 DS sidecars found under data/20241015_out" = length(.dsr_all) > 0L)
.dsr_stems <- unique(sub(paste0("__(", paste(.dsr_suf, collapse = "|"), ")[.]rds$"), "", .dsr_all))
.dsr_complete <- .dsr_stems[vapply(.dsr_stems, function(s)
  all(file.exists(file.path(.dsr_out, paste0(s, "__", .dsr_suf, ".rds")))), logical(1))]
stopifnot("no complete sidecar triplet found" = length(.dsr_complete) > 0L)

  max(file.info(file.path(.dsr_out, paste0(s, "__", .dsr_suf, ".rds")))$mtime),
  as.POSIXct("1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"))

# ---- 3. Formulas from the sidecars, exactly as deltaCIBS-ds-common-grid reads them
.dsr_parse <- function(v, label) {
  f <- if (inherits(v, "formula")) v else if (is.character(v) && length(v) == 1L && nzchar(v))
    stats::as.formula(v, env = globalenv()) else stop("invalid DS formula in ", label, call. = FALSE)
  environment(f) <- globalenv()
  f
}
.dsr_key <- function(v) gsub("[[:space:]]+", "", paste(deparse(.dsr_parse(v, "key")), collapse = " "))
.dsr_sets <- lapply(names(DSR_PATHS), function(lab) {
  sc <- readRDS(DSR_PATHS[[lab]])
  cfg <- sc$results$risk$config
  stopifnot("sidecar grid differs from the common grid" =
    identical(as.numeric(cfg$eval_times), DSR_GRID))
  out <- list(formula_readmit = .dsr_parse(cfg$formula_readmit, paste(lab, "readmission")),
              formula_death   = .dsr_parse(cfg$formula_death,   paste(lab, "death")))
  rm(sc, cfg); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
  out
})

  ds_interact_readmit = list(formula_readmit = .dsr_sets$interact$formula_readmit, formula_death = .dsr_sets$base$formula_death),
  ds_nph_death        = list(formula_readmit = .dsr_sets$base$formula_readmit,     formula_death = .dsr_sets$nph$formula_death),
  ds_interact_death   = list(formula_readmit = .dsr_sets$base$formula_readmit,     formula_death = .dsr_sets$interact$formula_death))

            sum(!.dsr_reuse), length(ds_specs), sum(!.dsr_reuse) * 2L * 5L * DSR_FOLDS))

if (any(!.dsr_reuse)) {
  if (!exists("py_corrected_datasets_boot", inherits = TRUE)) {
    .dsr_rd <- file.path(.dsr_out, "pred22_ndp_2026_07_13.Rdata")
    stopifnot("the canonical pred22 RData is unavailable" = file.exists(.dsr_rd))

    .dsr_e <- new.env(parent = emptyenv()); load(.dsr_rd, envir = .dsr_e)
    py_corrected_datasets_boot <- get("py_corrected_datasets_boot", envir = .dsr_e)
    rm(.dsr_e); invisible(gc())
  }
  stopifnot("expected five canonical imputations" =
    is.list(py_corrected_datasets_boot) && length(py_corrected_datasets_boot) == 5L)
}
# ---- 6. Refit what changed ---------------------------------------------------
# Sequential on purpose: evaluate_dual_cox_python_style already parallelises
# internally, and nesting a second layer is the oversubscription problem this
# notebook has hit before.
ds_dual_fits <- vector("list", length(ds_specs)); names(ds_dual_fits) <- names(ds_specs)
for (nm in names(ds_specs)) {
  if (.dsr_reuse[[nm]]) {
    ds_dual_fits[[nm]] <- .dsr_old[[nm]]
    cat(sprintf("annex-ds-refresh: carried over %s\n", nm)); flush.console()
    next
  }
  cat(sprintf("annex-ds-refresh: refitting %s (%.1f min elapsed)\n", nm,
              (proc.time() - .dsr_t0)[["elapsed"]] / 60)); flush.console()
  .dsr_opt <- options(dualcox.concordance_score = "lp", dualcox.concordance_within_strata = FALSE)
  ds_dual_fits[[nm]] <- evaluate_dual_cox_python_style(
    formula_readmit = ds_specs[[nm]]$formula_readmit,
    formula_death   = ds_specs[[nm]]$formula_death,
    imputed_list    = py_corrected_datasets_boot,
    k_folds = DSR_FOLDS, eval_times = DSR_GRID, seed = DSR_SEED, verbose = TRUE)
  options(.dsr_opt)
  invisible(gc())
}
# ---- 7. Validate every arm the way deltaCIBS-ds-common-grid validates it ------
.dsr_ref_folds <- ds_dual_fits[[1]]$fold_assignments
for (nm in names(ds_specs)) {
  f <- ds_dual_fits[[nm]]
  stopifnot("incomplete raw predictions" =
    !is.null(f$raw_predictions) && length(f$raw_predictions) == 5L * DSR_FOLDS)
  stopifnot("grid differs" = identical(as.numeric(f$config$eval_times), DSR_GRID))
  stopifnot("stored formulas differ from the new specification" =
    identical(.dsr_key(f$config$formula_readmit), .dsr_sig[[nm]][["readmission"]]) &&
    identical(.dsr_key(f$config$formula_death),   .dsr_sig[[nm]][["death"]]))
  # One fold assignment across every arm, carried over or freshly fitted. If a
  # reused arm disagreed here, mixing it with a new fit would silently break the
  # pairing that all the annex comparisons rest on.
  stopifnot("fold assignments differ across arms" =
    identical(f$fold_assignments, .dsr_ref_folds))
}
cat("annex-ds-refresh: all five arms validated; one shared fold assignment.\n")

.apdc_extract <- function(res, outcome = c("readmission", "death")) {
  # Reassemble the out-of-fold predictions into one per-subject matrix, pooled
  # over imputations. VERBATIM port of .cv_extract() from `deltaCIBS-cv-engine`,
  # except that it returns the RISK 1 - S(t) instead of S(t) and drops the
  # linear predictor, which this table does not use. The is.null(o$lp_val)
  # validity test is kept exactly as in the original, so a block the engine
  # considers unusable is skipped identically here.
  outcome <- match.arg(outcome)
  rp <- res$raw_predictions
  if (is.null(rp) || !length(rp))
    stop("no raw_predictions (stripped object or a calibration result, not a dual evaluation)", call. = FALSE)
  et <- as.numeric(res$config$eval_times)
  N <- max(vapply(rp, function(b) max(as.integer(b$original_val_idx)), 1L))
  imps <- sort(unique(vapply(rp, function(b) as.integer(b$imp_idx), 1L)))
  time_v <- rep(NA_real_, N); event_v <- rep(NA_real_, N); S_imp <- list()
  for (im in imps) {
    S <- matrix(NA_real_, N, length(et))
    for (b in rp) {
      if (as.integer(b$imp_idx) != im) next
      o <- b[[outcome]]
      if (is.null(o) || !is.null(o$error) || is.null(o$lp_val)) next
      idx <- as.integer(b$original_val_idx)
      S[idx, ] <- as.matrix(o$surv_val_matrix)
      yv <- o$y_val
      time_v[idx] <- as.numeric(yv[, 1]); event_v[idx] <- as.numeric(yv[, 2])
    }
    S_imp[[length(S_imp) + 1L]] <- S
  }
  S_pooled <- Reduce(`+`, S_imp) / length(S_imp)
  list(time = time_v, event = event_v,
       risk = pmin(pmax(1 - S_pooled, 0), 1), eval_times = et)
}
.apdc_fold_signature <- function(fit) {
  # A compact fingerprint of the out-of-fold partition, per imputation. Folds
  # are identified by their sorted membership, then ordered by first element so
  # that a mere relabelling of fold 1 and fold 2 does not read as a different
  # partition. Same idea as the .same_folds check in `p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev`.
  rp <- fit$raw_predictions
  imps <- sort(unique(vapply(rp, function(b) as.integer(b$imp_idx), 1L)))
  paste(vapply(imps, function(im) {
    fl <- lapply(Filter(function(b) as.integer(b$imp_idx) == im, rp),
                 function(b) sort(as.integer(b$original_val_idx)))
    fl <- fl[order(vapply(fl, function(v) v[1L], 1L))]
    paste(vapply(fl, function(v) sprintf("%d:%d:%d", length(v), v[1L], v[length(v)]), ""), collapse = "|")
  }, ""), collapse = "//")
}

# ============================================================================
# EXTENDED PAIRED DELTA C ON PREDICTED RISK, STEP 2/2: build the table.
# THE PRIMARY INTERVAL IS A NONPARAMETRIC PAIRED BOOTSTRAP. The analytic
# infinitesimal-jackknife interval is still computed and reported alongside, as a
# secondary column, because it costs one extra call and a visible disagreement
# between the two is itself diagnostic.
#
# HOW THE BOOTSTRAP IS MADE AFFORDABLE, because the obvious design is not.
# Bootstrapping one PAIR at a time, which is what a naive extension of
# `paired-delta-c-absolute-risk` does, means one survival::concordance() call per
# pair per replicate. Measured at n = 70,521 on this machine that is about 16.5
# seconds per replicate for ten arms, so B = 500 over two outcomes and four
# horizons runs for roughly 18 hours. Two changes remove that.
# 1. SCORE EVERY ARM ONCE PER REPLICATE, NOT EVERY PAIR. Within one outcome and
#    horizon all arms share the same follow-up, the same event indicator and the
#    same resampled subjects, so one pass over the ten markers yields all ten
#    concordances, and every one of the forty-five paired differences is then a
#    subtraction. The differences stay exactly as paired as before: they come
#    from one and the same resample.
# 2. USE THE LOW-LEVEL COUNTER AND SKIP THE PER-REPLICATE VARIANCE.
#    survival::concordance() computes an influence-function variance on every
#    call, which the bootstrap does not use because the bootstrap IS the variance
#    estimate. survival:::concordancefit(..., std.err = FALSE) returns the
#    concordant, discordant and tied.x counts without it, and
#    C = (concordant + tied.x / 2) / (concordant + discordant + tied.x)
#    reproduces concordance()$concordance exactly. Verified on this data layout
#    at 1e-16 for continuous, one-decimal and integer-month time granularities,
#    with tied markers, and on bootstrap resamples where almost every follow-up
#    time is duplicated.
# Together those take the same B = 500 from about 18 hours to about 40 minutes
# sequential, and to a few minutes across workers. Nothing about the estimand,
# the weights or the pairing changes: only how many times the same number is
# recomputed.
# concordancefit is INTERNAL to survival, so it is never trusted blindly. The
# equivalence gate below recomputes every arm, outcome and horizon on the
# OBSERVED data through both routes and refuses the fast path unless they agree
# to 1e-10, falling back to concordance() and saying so.
#
# ONE SUBJECT SET FOR EVERY ARM. `paired-delta-c-analytic` masks per PAIR. That
# is equivalent to masking once across all arms whenever every arm has the same
# finite rows, which is the normal case here because five-fold cross-validation
# gives every subject exactly one out-of-fold prediction. The chunk asserts it
# rather than assuming it, and says how many rows differ if it fails, because a
# shared resample is only possible on a shared subject set.
#
# Produces:
#   annex_pdc_table    the extended manuscript table, bootstrap interval first.
#   annex_pdc_bymodel  each arm's own horizon-specific Uno's C with a bootstrap
#                      interval from the same replicates.
#   annex_pdc_skipped  the pairs excluded by the identical-formula rule.
#   annex_pdc_boot     the replicate array [arm, horizon, B] per outcome, kept so
#                      any further comparison can be added without rescoring.
#
# Requires in kernel: `annex_pdc` and `.apdc_root` from the cell
# `annex-paired-delta-c-risk-ext-build`. Place AFTER it. Adds objects; replaces
# nothing, and in particular does not touch delta_C_analytic_table.
# ============================================================================
stopifnot("run the cell `annex-paired-delta-c-risk-ext-build` first" = exists("annex_pdc", inherits = TRUE))
stopifnot("run the cell `annex-paired-delta-c-risk-ext-build` first" = exists(".apdc_root", inherits = TRUE))
stopifnot(requireNamespace("survival", quietly = TRUE))

if (!exists("ANNEX_PDC_SEED", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_PDC_SEED <- 2125L

# sequentially. An integer starts that many PSOCK workers here and stops them
# before the chunk ends. The workers are started WITHOUT project startup files,
# the construction `p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev` settled on, because the renv

if (!exists("ANNEX_PDC_WORKERS", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_PDC_WORKERS <- NULL

# ASSIGNED UNCONDITIONALLY, on purpose. An earlier draft guarded this with
# if (!exists(...)) so the list could be overridden, and that guard silently

# delta_boot_upper, so the first print died with "undefined columns selected"

.apdc_colj <- function(h) {

if (.apdc_mask_ok)

.apdc_arms <- annex_pdc$models
.apdc_K <- length(.apdc_arms)
.apdc_data <- list()
for (oc in c("readmission", "death")) {

    colnames(M) <- .apdc_arms

}
# ---- Scoring routes, and the gate that decides which one the bootstrap uses --
.apdc_c_ref <- function(tt, ee, marker, horizon) {
  unname(survival::concordance(survival::Surv(tt, ee) ~ marker, timewt = "n/G2",
                               reverse = TRUE, ymax = horizon)$concordance)
}
.apdc_cfit <- if (isTRUE(ANNEX_PDC_FAST_COUNTER) &&
                  exists("concordancefit", where = asNamespace("survival")))
  get("concordancefit", envir = asNamespace("survival")) else NULL
.apdc_c_fast <- function(y, marker, horizon) {
  r <- .apdc_cfit(y, marker, timewt = "n/G2", reverse = TRUE, ymax = horizon, std.err = FALSE)
  cn <- r$count
  unname((cn[["concordant"]] + cn[["tied.x"]] / 2) /
         (cn[["concordant"]] + cn[["discordant"]] + cn[["tied.x"]]))
}
.apdc_use_fast <- FALSE
if (!is.null(.apdc_cfit)) {
  .apdc_gap <- 0
  for (oc in names(.apdc_data)) {
    dd <- .apdc_data[[oc]]; y <- survival::Surv(dd$time, dd$event)
    for (hh in names(dd$markers)) for (k in seq_len(.apdc_K)) {
      a <- tryCatch(.apdc_c_fast(y, dd$markers[[hh]][, k], as.numeric(hh)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
      b <- .apdc_c_ref(dd$time, dd$event, dd$markers[[hh]][, k], as.numeric(hh))
      .apdc_gap <- max(.apdc_gap, abs(a - b), na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  .apdc_use_fast <- is.finite(.apdc_gap) && .apdc_gap < 1e-10
  cat(sprintf("annex-pdc run: fast-counter equivalence gate, max |concordancefit - concordance| over %d arm-outcome-horizon cells = %.3e -> %s\n",
              .apdc_K * 2L * length(annex_pdc$horizons), .apdc_gap,
              if (.apdc_use_fast) "fast route accepted" else "REFUSED, falling back to concordance()"))
} else {
  cat("annex-pdc run: the fast counter is unavailable or disabled; using survival::concordance() throughout.\n")
}
.apdc_score_all <- function(tt, ee, M, horizon) {
  # All arms, one resample, one pass. This is the whole bootstrap inner loop.
  if (.apdc_use_fast) {
    y <- survival::Surv(tt, ee)
    vapply(seq_len(ncol(M)), function(k) .apdc_c_fast(y, M[, k], horizon), numeric(1))
  } else {
    vapply(seq_len(ncol(M)), function(k) .apdc_c_ref(tt, ee, M[, k], horizon), numeric(1))
  }
}
# ---- Point estimates and the analytic covariance, one call per cell ---------
# All markers on one right-hand side, so a single call returns every arm's C and
# the full K x K infinitesimal-jackknife covariance, from which every paired
# se(delta) = sqrt(v_aa + v_bb - 2 v_ab) follows without another fit.
cat(sprintf("annex-pdc run: point estimates and analytic covariance for %d arms x 2 outcomes x %d horizons...\n",
            .apdc_K, length(annex_pdc$horizons))); flush.console()
.apdc_point <- list(); .apdc_V <- list()
for (oc in names(.apdc_data)) {
  dd <- .apdc_data[[oc]]
  .apdc_point[[oc]] <- list(); .apdc_V[[oc]] <- list()
  for (hh in names(dd$markers)) {
    M <- dd$markers[[hh]]
    dfr <- data.frame(time = dd$time, event = dd$event, M, check.names = FALSE)
    fml <- stats::as.formula(paste("survival::Surv(time, event) ~",
                                   paste(sprintf("`%s`", .apdc_arms), collapse = " + ")))
    fit <- survival::concordance(fml, data = dfr, timewt = "n/G2", reverse = TRUE, ymax = as.numeric(hh))
    est <- unname(fit$concordance)
    nmv <- names(fit$concordance)
    if (!is.null(nmv)) {
      ord <- match(.apdc_arms, gsub("^`|`$", "", nmv))
      stopifnot("concordance returned markers in an unexpected order" = !anyNA(ord))
      est <- est[ord]
      V <- as.matrix(fit$var)[ord, ord, drop = FALSE]
    } else {
      V <- as.matrix(fit$var)
    }
    names(est) <- .apdc_arms; dimnames(V) <- list(.apdc_arms, .apdc_arms)
    .apdc_point[[oc]][[hh]] <- est; .apdc_V[[oc]][[hh]] <- V
  }
}
# ---- The bootstrap ----------------------------------------------------------
# One job per outcome and horizon; inside a job, B replicates, each resampling
# the subjects ONCE and scoring every arm on that resample. Jobs are independent,
# so they parallelise cleanly and each worker receives one marker matrix.
.apdc_jobs_b <- list()
for (oc in names(.apdc_data)) for (hh in names(.apdc_data[[oc]]$markers))
  .apdc_jobs_b[[length(.apdc_jobs_b) + 1L]] <- list(outcome = oc, horizon = hh)
# A timed pilot on the real data, so the runtime announced below is measured
# rather than guessed, and a run that would take all night is visible up front.
.apdc_pilot <- local({
  dd <- .apdc_data[[1]]; M <- dd$markers[[1]]; h <- as.numeric(names(dd$markers)[1])
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (i in 1:3) { s <- sample.int(dd$n, dd$n, replace = TRUE)
    .apdc_score_all(dd$time[s], dd$event[s], M[s, , drop = FALSE], h) }
  as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")) / 3
})
cat(sprintf("annex-pdc run: measured %.3f s per replicate for %d arms; %d jobs x B = %d -> about %.1f min sequential.\n",
            .apdc_pilot, .apdc_K, length(.apdc_jobs_b), ANNEX_PDC_B,
            .apdc_pilot * ANNEX_PDC_B * length(.apdc_jobs_b) / 60)); flush.console()
.apdc_cluster <- NULL
if (!is.null(ANNEX_PDC_WORKERS) && as.integer(ANNEX_PDC_WORKERS) > 1L &&
    requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
  nw <- as.integer(ANNEX_PDC_WORKERS)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 4 * 1024^3)
  if (requireNamespace("parallelly", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat(sprintf("annex-pdc run: starting %d PSOCK workers without project startup files.\n", nw)); flush.console()
    .apdc_cluster <- parallelly::makeClusterPSOCK(nw, rscript_args = "--no-init-file",
                                                  rscript_libs = .libPaths(), connectTimeout = 300,
                                                  validate = TRUE, autoStop = FALSE)
    future::plan(future::cluster, workers = .apdc_cluster)
  } else {
    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = nw)
  }
  cat(sprintf("annex-pdc run: with %d workers expect about %.1f min.\n",
              nw, .apdc_pilot * ANNEX_PDC_B * length(.apdc_jobs_b) / 60 / nw))
}
.apdc_one_job <- function(job_index) {
  job <- .apdc_jobs_b[[job_index]]
  dd <- .apdc_data[[job$outcome]]; M <- dd$markers[[job$horizon]]; h <- as.numeric(job$horizon)
  set.seed(ANNEX_PDC_SEED + job_index, kind = "Mersenne-Twister")
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, ncol(M), ANNEX_PDC_B, dimnames = list(colnames(M), NULL))
  for (b in seq_len(ANNEX_PDC_B)) {
    s <- sample.int(dd$n, dd$n, replace = TRUE)
    out[, b] <- .apdc_score_all(dd$time[s], dd$event[s], M[s, , drop = FALSE], h)
  }
  out
}
cat("annex-pdc run: bootstrapping...\n"); flush.console()
.apdc_t0 <- Sys.time()
.apdc_use_par <- requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE) && future::nbrOfWorkers() > 1L
.apdc_res <- if (.apdc_use_par) {

} else {
  lapply(seq_along(.apdc_jobs_b), function(i) {
    r <- .apdc_one_job(i)

                .apdc_jobs_b[[i]]$outcome, .apdc_jobs_b[[i]]$horizon,
                as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .apdc_t0, units = "mins")))); flush.console()
    r
  })
}

}

            as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .apdc_t0, units = "mins"))))
annex_pdc_boot <- list()
for (i in seq_along(.apdc_jobs_b)) {
  job <- .apdc_jobs_b[[i]]
  if (is.null(annex_pdc_boot[[job$outcome]])) annex_pdc_boot[[job$outcome]] <- list()
  annex_pdc_boot[[job$outcome]][[job$horizon]] <- .apdc_res[[i]]
}
.apdc_q <- function(v, p) { f <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (length(f) < 20L) NA_real_ else stats::quantile(f, probs = p, names = FALSE) }
# ---- Per-arm C, with the bootstrap interval from the same replicates --------
annex_pdc_bymodel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.apdc_data), function(oc) {
  dd <- .apdc_data[[oc]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(dd$markers), function(hh) {
    h <- as.numeric(hh); est <- .apdc_point[[oc]][[hh]]; V <- .apdc_V[[oc]][[hh]]
    B <- annex_pdc_boot[[oc]][[hh]]
    se <- sqrt(pmax(diag(V), 0))
    data.frame(outcome = oc, model = .apdc_arms, family = unname(annex_pdc$family[.apdc_arms]),
               horizon = h, n = dd$n, events_by_horizon = sum(dd$event == 1 & dd$time <= h),
               C = unname(est[.apdc_arms]),
               C_boot_lower = vapply(.apdc_arms, function(a) .apdc_q(B[a, ], 0.025), 0),
               C_boot_upper = vapply(.apdc_arms, function(a) .apdc_q(B[a, ], 0.975), 0),
               C_ij_lower = pmax(0, unname(est[.apdc_arms]) - .apdc_crit * se[.apdc_arms]),
               C_ij_upper = pmin(1, unname(est[.apdc_arms]) + .apdc_crit * se[.apdc_arms]),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
rownames(annex_pdc_bymodel) <- NULL
# ---- Pairwise table, with the identical-formula skip made explicit ----------
.apdc_key <- function(x) gsub("[[:space:]]+", "", x)

annex_pdc_skipped <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("readmission", "death"), function(oc) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(.apdc_prs, function(p) {
    if (!identical(.apdc_key(annex_pdc$f_txt[[oc]][[p[1]]]), .apdc_key(annex_pdc$f_txt[[oc]][[p[2]]]))) return(NULL)
    data.frame(outcome = oc, model_A = p[1], model_B = p[2],
               family_A = unname(annex_pdc$family[[p[1]]]), family_B = unname(annex_pdc$family[[p[2]]]),
               reason = "identical formula for this outcome: 1 - S(t) is the same marker, delta C is exactly 0",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))
annex_pdc_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("readmission", "death"), function(oc) {
  dd <- .apdc_data[[oc]]

    if (identical(.apdc_key(annex_pdc$f_txt[[oc]][[p[1]]]), .apdc_key(annex_pdc$f_txt[[oc]][[p[2]]]))) return(NULL)
    do.call(rbind, lapply(names(dd$markers), function(hh) {
      h <- as.numeric(hh); est <- .apdc_point[[oc]][[hh]]; V <- .apdc_V[[oc]][[hh]]
      B <- annex_pdc_boot[[oc]][[hh]]
      d_boot <- B[p[1], ] - B[p[2], ]
      delta <- unname(est[p[1]] - est[p[2]])
      se_ij <- sqrt(max(V[p[1], p[1]] + V[p[2], p[2]] - 2 * V[p[1], p[2]], 0))
      lo <- .apdc_q(d_boot, 0.025); hi <- .apdc_q(d_boot, 0.975)

        outcome = oc, model_A = p[1], model_B = p[2],
        family_A = unname(annex_pdc$family[[p[1]]]), family_B = unname(annex_pdc$family[[p[2]]]),
        horizon = h, n = dd$n, events_by_horizon = sum(dd$event == 1 & dd$time <= h),
        C_A = unname(est[p[1]]), C_B = unname(est[p[2]]), delta_C = delta,
        delta_boot_lower = lo, delta_boot_upper = hi,
        boot_mean = mean(d_boot[is.finite(d_boot)]),
        centering_bias = mean(d_boot[is.finite(d_boot)]) - delta,
        point_inside_boot_ci = is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi) && delta >= lo && delta <= hi,
        B_valid = sum(is.finite(d_boot)), B_requested = ANNEX_PDC_B,

        delta_ij_upper = delta + .apdc_crit * se_ij,
        boot_over_ij_width = if (se_ij > 0 && is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi))
          (hi - lo) / (2 * .apdc_crit * se_ij) else NA_real_,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
    }))
  }))
}))
annex_pdc_table$favours <- ifelse(
  is.finite(annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_lower) & annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_lower > 0, annex_pdc_table$model_A,
  ifelse(is.finite(annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_upper) & annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_upper < 0, annex_pdc_table$model_B,
         "No clear difference"))
annex_pdc_table$comparison <- ifelse(
  annex_pdc_table$family_A != annex_pdc_table$family_B, "Cox vs prediction24",
  ifelse(annex_pdc_table$family_A == "cox", "within Cox", "within prediction24"))
annex_pdc_table$excludes_zero <- is.finite(annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_lower) &
  is.finite(annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_upper) &
  (annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_lower > 0 | annex_pdc_table$delta_boot_upper < 0)
annex_pdc_table$meets_promotion_threshold <-
  is.finite(annex_pdc_table$delta_C) & abs(annex_pdc_table$delta_C) >= ANNEX_PDC_PROMOTION_DELTA
annex_pdc_table <- annex_pdc_table[order(annex_pdc_table$outcome, annex_pdc_table$horizon,
                                         -abs(annex_pdc_table$delta_C)), ]
rownames(annex_pdc_table) <- NULL
# ---- Diagnostics on the bootstrap itself ------------------------------------
# Two things a reviewer will ask. Is the bootstrap centred on the point estimate,
# and does its interval agree with the analytic one. A ratio near 1 means the two
# routes concur and the analytic interval was never the problem; a ratio far from
# 1 is the reason for having run the bootstrap in the first place.
cat(sprintf("\nBootstrap diagnostics: max |centering bias| = %.5f; point inside its own interval in %d of %d rows.\n",
            max(abs(annex_pdc_table$centering_bias), na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(annex_pdc_table$point_inside_boot_ci, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(annex_pdc_table)))
cat(sprintf("Bootstrap interval width relative to the analytic one: median %.3f, range %.3f to %.3f.\n",
            stats::median(annex_pdc_table$boot_over_ij_width, na.rm = TRUE),
            min(annex_pdc_table$boot_over_ij_width, na.rm = TRUE),
            max(annex_pdc_table$boot_over_ij_width, na.rm = TRUE)))
if (any(!annex_pdc_table$point_inside_boot_ci, na.rm = TRUE))
  warning("annex-pdc: ", sum(!annex_pdc_table$point_inside_boot_ci, na.rm = TRUE),
          " point estimates fall outside their own bootstrap interval. Inspect before reporting.", call. = FALSE)
# ---- Reconciliation against the existing table ------------------------------
# The point estimates use the same estimator and the same subject set as
# `paired-delta-c-analytic`, so the within-Cox delta_C values must reproduce
# delta_C_analytic_table exactly. This is checked, not asserted. The interval is
# not compared: that table's interval is analytic and this one's is bootstrap.
annex_pdc_reconciliation <- NULL
if (exists("delta_C_analytic_table", inherits = TRUE) && is.data.frame(delta_C_analytic_table)) {
  .apdc_k2 <- function(d) paste(d$outcome, d$model_A, d$model_B, d$horizon, sep = "|")
  .apdc_old <- delta_C_analytic_table
  .apdc_new <- annex_pdc_table[annex_pdc_table$comparison == "within Cox", , drop = FALSE]
  mm <- match(.apdc_k2(.apdc_old), .apdc_k2(.apdc_new)); hit <- !is.na(mm)
  if (any(hit)) {
    d_delta <- abs(.apdc_old$delta_C[hit] - .apdc_new$delta_C[mm[hit]])
    d_ca <- abs(.apdc_old$C_A[hit] - .apdc_new$C_A[mm[hit]])
    d_ij <- abs(.apdc_old$delta_C_lower[hit] - .apdc_new$delta_ij_lower[mm[hit]])
    annex_pdc_reconciliation <- data.frame(
      rows_in_existing_table = nrow(.apdc_old), rows_matched = sum(hit),
      max_abs_diff_delta_C = max(d_delta, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_abs_diff_C_A = max(d_ca, na.rm = TRUE),
      max_abs_diff_analytic_lower = max(d_ij, na.rm = TRUE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    cat("\nReconciliation against the live delta_C_analytic_table:\n")
    print(annex_pdc_reconciliation, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
    if (max(d_delta, na.rm = TRUE) > 1e-8)
      warning("annex-pdc: the within-Cox point estimates do NOT reproduce delta_C_analytic_table ",
              "(max |difference| = ", signif(max(d_delta, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
              "). Investigate before presenting this as an extension of that table.", call. = FALSE)
    else cat("The within-Cox point estimates reproduce the existing table exactly.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("\ndelta_C_analytic_table is not in the kernel, so no reconciliation was run.\n")
}
# ---- Report ------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\n-- Per-arm horizon-specific Uno's C on predicted risk, out-of-fold development sample --\n")
print(annex_pdc_bymodel[, c("outcome", "model", "family", "horizon", "n", "events_by_horizon",
                            "C", "C_boot_lower", "C_boot_upper")], row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
cat("\n-- NEW ROWS: Cox versus prediction24 candidates (bootstrap interval) --\n")
.apdc_cross <- annex_pdc_table[annex_pdc_table$comparison == "Cox vs prediction24", , drop = FALSE]
if (nrow(.apdc_cross)) {

      else

} else {

}

# re-read from the CSVs this chunk itself wrote, so it still works after a kernel
# restart. Either way nothing is recomputed.

  .f <- file.path(.apdc_csv, "pred225_annex_paired_delta_c_risk_ext.csv")
  stopifnot("neither annex_pdc_table nor its CSV is available" = file.exists(.f))
  annex_pdc_table <- utils::read.csv(.f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  message("annex-pdc report: annex_pdc_table re-read from ", basename(.f))
}

  stopifnot("neither annex_pdc_bymodel nor its CSV is available" = file.exists(.f))
  annex_pdc_bymodel <- utils::read.csv(.f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  message("annex-pdc report: annex_pdc_bymodel re-read from ", basename(.f))
}
if (!exists("ANNEX_PDC_PROMOTION_DELTA", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_PDC_PROMOTION_DELTA <- 0.01
# Defined UNCONDITIONALLY and then intersected with the columns the table really
# has, so neither a stale value from an earlier cell version nor a later column
# rename can break the printing again. This is the actual fix.
.apdc_wanted <- c("outcome", "comparison", "model_A", "family_A", "model_B", "family_B",
                  "horizon", "n", "events_by_horizon",
                  "C_A", "C_A_boot_lower", "C_A_boot_upper", "C_A_ij_lower", "C_A_ij_upper",
                  "C_B", "C_B_boot_lower", "C_B_boot_upper", "C_B_ij_lower", "C_B_ij_upper",
                  "delta_C", "delta_boot_lower", "delta_boot_upper", "boot_mean",
                  "centering_bias", "se_delta_ij", "delta_ij_lower", "delta_ij_upper")

# manuscript name is used without recomputing anything. "prediction24" and
# "deepsurv_informed" were both used while these annexes were being written; the
# reported name is DeepSurv-informed.
.apdc_fam_map <- c(cox = "Cox", Cox = "Cox", prediction24 = "DeepSurv-informed",
                   deepsurv_informed = "DeepSurv-informed",
                   `DeepSurv-informed` = "DeepSurv-informed")
.apdc_relabel <- function(v) { out <- unname(.apdc_fam_map[as.character(v)])
  ifelse(is.na(out), as.character(v), out) }

cat("Family labels in use:", paste(sort(unique(c(annex_pdc_table$family_A, annex_pdc_table$family_B))), collapse = ", "), "
")
# ---- Each arm's OWN interval, attached to the pairwise table ---------------
# annex_pdc_bymodel already carries every arm's C with its bootstrap and analytic
# bounds, from the SAME replicates, so the pairwise table gets them by a join and
# nothing is recomputed. Joined on outcome, model and horizon, which is the key
# that identifies an arm-horizon cell uniquely.
# READ THIS BEFORE USING THE NEW COLUMNS. C_A and C_B with their own intervals are
# MARGINAL: they say how precisely each arm's C is estimated on its own. Two
# marginal intervals that overlap do NOT mean the difference is compatible with
# zero. The two markers are almost perfectly correlated, so the paired interval
# delta_boot_lower to delta_boot_upper is far narrower and is the only one that
# answers whether the models differ. Report the marginal bounds as description of
# each arm, never as the comparison.
.apdc_bm <- annex_pdc_bymodel[, intersect(c("outcome", "model", "horizon", "C_boot_lower",
                                            "C_boot_upper", "C_ij_lower", "C_ij_upper"),
                                          names(annex_pdc_bymodel)), drop = FALSE]
if (all(c("outcome", "model", "horizon") %in% names(.apdc_bm)) && nrow(.apdc_bm)) {
  .apdc_key3 <- function(o, m, h) paste(o, m, h, sep = "|")
  .apdc_src <- .apdc_key3(.apdc_bm$outcome, .apdc_bm$model, .apdc_bm$horizon)
  for (side in c("A", "B")) {
    idx <- match(.apdc_key3(annex_pdc_table$outcome, annex_pdc_table[[paste0("model_", side)]],
                            annex_pdc_table$horizon), .apdc_src)
    if (anyNA(idx))
      warning("annex-pdc report: ", sum(is.na(idx)), " rows of arm ", side,
              " found no match in annex_pdc_bymodel; their interval columns stay NA.", call. = FALSE)
    for (nm in c("C_boot_lower", "C_boot_upper", "C_ij_lower", "C_ij_upper"))
      if (nm %in% names(.apdc_bm))
        annex_pdc_table[[sub("^C_", paste0("C_", side, "_"), nm)]] <- .apdc_bm[[nm]][idx]
  }
  cat("Per-arm intervals attached to the pairwise table from annex_pdc_bymodel.
")
} else {
  warning("annex-pdc report: annex_pdc_bymodel lacks the join keys or the interval columns; ",
          "the pairwise table keeps C_A and C_B without their own bounds.", call. = FALSE)
}

.acrc_extract <- function(res, outcome = c("readmission", "death")) {
  # Reassemble the out-of-fold predictions into one per-subject matrix, pooled
  # over imputations. This is a VERBATIM port of .cv_extract() from the cell
  # `deltaCIBS-cv-engine`, minus the linear predictor, which the annex does not
  # use. Ported rather than sourced so the chunk runs on a cold kernel; the
  # is.null(o$lp_val) validity test is kept exactly as in the original so a
  # block the engine considers unusable is skipped identically here.
  outcome <- match.arg(outcome)
  rp <- res$raw_predictions
  if (is.null(rp) || !length(rp))
    stop("no raw_predictions (stripped object or a calibration result, not a dual evaluation)", call. = FALSE)
  et <- as.numeric(res$config$eval_times)
  N <- max(vapply(rp, function(b) max(as.integer(b$original_val_idx)), 1L))
  imps <- sort(unique(vapply(rp, function(b) as.integer(b$imp_idx), 1L)))
  time_v <- rep(NA_real_, N); event_v <- rep(NA_real_, N); S_imp <- list()
  for (im in imps) {
    S <- matrix(NA_real_, N, length(et))
    for (b in rp) {
      if (as.integer(b$imp_idx) != im) next
      o <- b[[outcome]]
      if (is.null(o) || !is.null(o$error) || is.null(o$lp_val)) next
      idx <- as.integer(b$original_val_idx)
      S[idx, ] <- as.matrix(o$surv_val_matrix)
      yv <- o$y_val
      time_v[idx] <- as.numeric(yv[, 1]); event_v[idx] <- as.numeric(yv[, 2])
    }
    S_imp[[length(S_imp) + 1L]] <- S
  }
  list(time = time_v, event = event_v, S = Reduce(`+`, S_imp) / length(S_imp), eval_times = et)
}
.acrc_cif_product_integral <- function(S1, S2) {
  # Cause-specific cumulative incidence by discrete product integration on the
  # prediction grid, VERBATIM from the cell `paired-delta-c-competing-risks`:
  #   CIF_1(t_k) = sum_j S_all(t_{j-1}) * [H_1(t_j) - H_1(t_{j-1})]
  # with H_1 = -log S_1 and S_all = S_1 * S_2. No refitting is involved: both
  # survival matrices already exist for the same subjects, folds and imputations.
  # NOTE on the order of operations: the survival matrices handed in here are
  # ALREADY averaged over the five imputations, so this pools first and
  # integrates second. Integrating within each imputation and pooling after
  # would not give the identical number, because the product integral is not
  # linear in S. Pooling first is what `paired-delta-c-competing-risks` does,
  # and matching it matters more than the third-decimal difference, since the
  # whole point of the annex is to be comparable with the existing cells.
  H1 <- -log(pmax(S1, 1e-12))
  S_all <- S1 * S2
  n <- nrow(S1); K <- ncol(S1)
  cif <- matrix(0, n, K)
  S_prev <- rep(1, n); H1_prev <- rep(0, n); acc <- rep(0, n)
  for (k in seq_len(K)) {
    acc <- acc + S_prev * (H1[, k] - H1_prev)
    cif[, k] <- acc
    S_prev <- S_all[, k]; H1_prev <- H1[, k]
  }
  pmin(pmax(cif, 0), 1)
}
.acrc_status <- function(ex_r, ex_d) {
  # Competing-risk cause, using the convention of the cell
  # `paired-delta-c-competing-risks`: readmission follow-up is censored at
  # death, so a subject who dies without readmission carries event 0 in the
  # readmission extract and the same time in both extracts.
  died_first <- ex_r$event == 0 & ex_d$event == 1 & (ex_d$time <= ex_r$time + 1e-8)
  ifelse(ex_r$event == 1, 1L, ifelse(died_first, 2L, 0L))
}
.acrc_first_event_alt <- function(ex_r, ex_d) {
  # Independent reconstruction using the pmin first-event rule of
  # .vhm_first_event() / .holdout_cr_first_event(), ties resolved to death.
  # Computed only to CROSS-CHECK the convention above: the two rules agree
  # whenever readmission follow-up really is censored at death, and a
  # disagreement count above zero means that assumption fails somewhere and the
  # competing-risk status cannot be trusted.
  ft <- pmin(ex_r$time, ex_d$time)
  r1 <- ex_r$event == 1 & is.finite(ft) & abs(ex_r$time - ft) <= 1e-8
  d1 <- ex_d$event == 1 & is.finite(ft) & abs(ex_d$time - ft) <= 1e-8
  st <- rep(0L, length(ft))
  st[r1 & !d1] <- 1L
  st[d1 & !r1] <- 2L
  st[r1 & d1]  <- 2L
  st
}

  .acrc_fits <- .acrc_fits[.acrc_hasrp]
  if (!is.null(ANNEX_CRC_MODELS)) {
    stopifnot("ANNEX_CRC_MODELS names a model that is not available" =
      all(ANNEX_CRC_MODELS %in% names(.acrc_fits)))
    .acrc_fits <- .acrc_fits[ANNEX_CRC_MODELS]
  }
  stopifnot("at least two models are needed for the pairwise table" = length(.acrc_fits) >= 2L)
  # 4. Grid guard. A model evaluated on a different grid is not comparable and
  #    its horizon columns would not line up with the others.
  .acrc_grids <- vapply(.acrc_fits, function(f) paste(as.numeric(f$config$eval_times), collapse = ","), "")
  .acrc_want <- paste(ANNEX_CRC_GRID, collapse = ",")
  if (any(.acrc_grids != .acrc_want))
    stop("annex-cr-cindex: these models are not on the canonical grid ", .acrc_want, ": ",
         paste(names(.acrc_fits)[.acrc_grids != .acrc_want], collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  message("annex-cr-cindex build: models in play: ", paste(names(.acrc_fits), collapse = ", "))
  # 5. Extract, build the CIF, and record each model's own finite mask.
  .acrc_nm <- names(.acrc_fits)
  .acrc_net <- list(); .acrc_cif <- list(); .acrc_okm <- list()
  .acrc_ref <- NULL; .acrc_status_v <- NULL; .acrc_mismatch <- 0L
  for (m in .acrc_nm) {
    ex_r <- .acrc_extract(.acrc_fits[[m]], "readmission")
    ex_d <- .acrc_extract(.acrc_fits[[m]], "death")
    okm <- is.finite(ex_r$time) & is.finite(ex_r$event) &
           is.finite(ex_d$time) & is.finite(ex_d$event) &
           rowSums(is.finite(ex_r$S)) == ncol(ex_r$S) &
           rowSums(is.finite(ex_d$S)) == ncol(ex_d$S)
    .acrc_okm[[m]] <- okm
    .acrc_net[[m]] <- pmin(pmax(1 - ex_r$S, 0), 1)
    .acrc_cif[[m]] <- .acrc_cif_product_integral(ex_r$S, ex_d$S)
    if (is.null(.acrc_ref)) {
      .acrc_ref <- list(time_r = ex_r$time, event_r = ex_r$event,
                        time_d = ex_d$time, event_d = ex_d$event)
      .acrc_status_v <- .acrc_status(ex_r, ex_d)
      .acrc_mismatch <- sum(.acrc_status_v[okm] != .acrc_first_event_alt(ex_r, ex_d)[okm])
    } else {
      # Every model is fit on the same data, so the observed outcomes must be
      # identical. If they are not, the models are not comparable at all and a
      # paired delta would be meaningless.
      stopifnot("models disagree on the observed readmission outcome" =
        max(abs(ex_r$time[okm] - .acrc_ref$time_r[okm]), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-8 &&
        all(ex_r$event[okm] == .acrc_ref$event_r[okm], na.rm = TRUE))
      stopifnot("models disagree on the observed mortality outcome" =
        max(abs(ex_d$time[okm] - .acrc_ref$time_d[okm]), na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-8 &&
        all(ex_d$event[okm] == .acrc_ref$event_d[okm], na.rm = TRUE))
    }

  .acrc_ok <- Reduce(`&`, .acrc_okm)
  .acrc_n_all <- length(.acrc_ok)
  message(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex build: common analysable rows %d of %d (dropped %d)",
                  sum(.acrc_ok), .acrc_n_all, .acrc_n_all - sum(.acrc_ok)))
  stopifnot("fewer than 100 rows survive the common mask; something is wrong upstream" = sum(.acrc_ok) >= 100L)
  annex_crc <- list(
    models = .acrc_nm,
    f_readmit_txt = vapply(.acrc_fits, function(f) paste(as.character(f$config$formula_readmit), collapse = " "), ""),
    f_death_txt   = vapply(.acrc_fits, function(f) paste(as.character(f$config$formula_death), collapse = " "), ""),
    time_r = .acrc_ref$time_r[.acrc_ok], event_r = .acrc_ref$event_r[.acrc_ok],
    status_cr = .acrc_status_v[.acrc_ok],
    netrisk = lapply(.acrc_net, function(M) M[.acrc_ok, , drop = FALSE]),
    cif     = lapply(.acrc_cif, function(M) M[.acrc_ok, , drop = FALSE]),
    netrisk_own = .acrc_net, ok_own = .acrc_okm,
    time_r_all = .acrc_ref$time_r, event_r_all = .acrc_ref$event_r,
    eval_times = ANNEX_CRC_GRID, horizons = ANNEX_CRC_HORIZONS,
    n = sum(.acrc_ok), n_all = .acrc_n_all, n_dropped_common = .acrc_n_all - sum(.acrc_ok),
    status_rule_mismatch = .acrc_mismatch,
    provenance = paste(.acrc_prov, collapse = "; "),
    created = as.character(Sys.time())
  )
  rm(.acrc_fits, .acrc_net, .acrc_cif, .acrc_okm); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
  if (ANNEX_CRC_USE_DISK_CACHE) {
    saveRDS(annex_crc, ANNEX_CRC_CACHE_RDS)
    message("annex-cr-cindex build: cached to ", ANNEX_CRC_CACHE_RDS, " (",
            round(file.info(ANNEX_CRC_CACHE_RDS)$size / 1024^2), " MB)")
  }

# ============================================================================
# ANNEX COMPETING-RISK READMISSION C INDEX, STEP 2/2: tables A and B.
# EVERY INTERVAL HERE IS A NONPARAMETRIC PAIRED BOOTSTRAP. The analytic
# infinitesimal-jackknife interval is still computed and kept as a secondary
# column, because it costs one extra call and a visible disagreement between the
# two routes is itself diagnostic.
#
# TABLE A, `annex_crc_bymodel`. For every model and horizon, Uno's C for
# readmission in the 2 x 2 of scoring and marker:
#   C_cs_netrisk  cause-specific scoring, net risk marker. THIS is what the
#                 notebook reports today, and the column C_cs_netrisk_ownmask
#                 recomputes it on the model's OWN finite subset so it can be
#                 reconciled with `paired-delta-c-absolute-risk`.
#   C_cs_cif      cause-specific scoring, CIF marker
#   C_cr_netrisk  competing-risk (Wolbers) scoring, net risk marker
#   C_cr_cif      competing-risk scoring, CIF marker. The coherent quantity,
#                 aligned with calibration (calibrate_cscox_aj_grouped_corr) and
#                 with the DCA engine, which are Aalen-Johansen based.
# delta_marker_cs and delta_marker_cr are bootstrapped: within one replicate the
# same resampled subjects are scored on both markers, so the difference is paired
# by construction. delta_scoring_netrisk stays a POINT ESTIMATE with no interval:
# the two scorings define different risk sets and different censoring
# distributions, so no single resample pairs them and any interval would be wrong.
#
# TABLE B, `annex_crc_pairs`. Paired delta C between models on the CIF marker
# under competing-risk scoring, from the SAME replicates, with the column
# shared_readmission_formula marking the pairs the notebook's other cells skip.
#
# HOW THE BOOTSTRAP IS MADE AFFORDABLE, because the obvious design is not.
# Bootstrapping one PAIR at a time means one survival::concordance() call per pair
# per replicate; at n around 70,500 with ten models that is roughly eighteen hours
# for B = 500. Two changes remove it.
# 1. SCORE EVERY MARKER ONCE PER REPLICATE, NOT EVERY PAIR. Within one scoring
#    and horizon all markers share the same follow-up, the same event indicator
#    and the same resampled subjects, so one pass over the 2K markers yields every
#    C, and each difference in tables A and B is then a subtraction of two numbers
#    that came from the same resample.
# 2. USE THE LOW-LEVEL COUNTER AND SKIP THE PER-REPLICATE VARIANCE.
#    survival::concordance() computes an influence-function variance on every
#    call, which a bootstrap does not use because the bootstrap IS the variance
#    estimate. survival:::concordancefit(..., std.err = FALSE) returns the counts,
#    and C = (concordant + tied.x / 2) / (concordant + discordant + tied.x)
#    reproduces concordance()$concordance exactly. That function is INTERNAL to
#    survival, so it is never trusted blindly: the gate below recomputes every
#    marker, scoring and horizon on the OBSERVED data through both routes and
#    refuses the fast path unless they agree to 1e-10.
#
# WOLBERS CONVENTION. A subject who dies before readmission can never be
# readmitted; censoring them, the cause-specific convention, silently drops those
# pairs. Instead their follow-up is pushed far beyond the cohort and they are kept
# event free, so they stay comparable with every readmission case.
# KNOWN CAVEAT, stated so a reviewer does not have to find it: pushing them out
# keeps them in the at-risk set of the censoring Kaplan-Meier that supplies the
# n/G2 weights, so G is slightly optimistic. It is identical for every model and
# every marker here, so it cancels in all the paired differences; it can shift the
# absolute level of C a little, not the deltas.
#
# Requires in kernel: `annex_crc` and `.acrc_root` from the cell
# `annex-cr-cindex-readmit-build`. Place AFTER it. Adds objects; replaces nothing.
# ============================================================================
stopifnot("run the cell `annex-cr-cindex-readmit-build` first" = exists("annex_crc", inherits = TRUE))
stopifnot("run the cell `annex-cr-cindex-readmit-build` first" = exists(".acrc_root", inherits = TRUE))
