# ---- Scoring routes, and the gate that decides which one the bootstrap uses --
.acrc_c_ref <- function(tt, ee, marker, horizon)
  unname(survival::concordance(survival::Surv(tt, ee) ~ marker, timewt = "n/G2",
                               reverse = TRUE, ymax = horizon)$concordance)
.acrc_cfit <- if (isTRUE(ANNEX_CRC_FAST_COUNTER) &&
                  exists("concordancefit", where = asNamespace("survival")))
  get("concordancefit", envir = asNamespace("survival")) else NULL
.acrc_c_fast <- function(y, marker, horizon) {
  r <- .acrc_cfit(y, marker, timewt = "n/G2", reverse = TRUE, ymax = horizon, std.err = FALSE)
  cn <- r$count
  unname((cn[["concordant"]] + cn[["tied.x"]] / 2) /
         (cn[["concordant"]] + cn[["discordant"]] + cn[["tied.x"]]))
}
.acrc_scorings <- list(cs = list(time = .acrc_tr, event = .acrc_er),
                       cr = list(time = .acrc_tw, event = .acrc_ew))
.acrc_use_fast <- FALSE
if (!is.null(.acrc_cfit)) {
  gap <- 0
  for (sc in names(.acrc_scorings)) {
    ss <- .acrc_scorings[[sc]]; y <- survival::Surv(ss$time, ss$event)
    for (hh in names(.acrc_M)) for (k in seq_along(.acrc_arms)) {
      a <- tryCatch(.acrc_c_fast(y, .acrc_M[[hh]][, k], as.numeric(hh)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
      b <- .acrc_c_ref(ss$time, ss$event, .acrc_M[[hh]][, k], as.numeric(hh))
      gap <- max(gap, abs(a - b), na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }
  .acrc_use_fast <- is.finite(gap) && gap < 1e-10
  cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: fast-counter equivalence gate over %d marker-scoring-horizon cells, max |concordancefit - concordance| = %.3e -> %s\n",
              length(.acrc_arms) * 2L * length(annex_crc$horizons), gap,
              if (.acrc_use_fast) "fast route accepted" else "REFUSED, falling back to concordance()"))
} else {
  cat("annex-cr-cindex run: the fast counter is unavailable or disabled; using survival::concordance() throughout.\n")
}
.acrc_score_all <- function(tt, ee, M, horizon) {
  if (.acrc_use_fast) {
    y <- survival::Surv(tt, ee)
    vapply(seq_len(ncol(M)), function(k) .acrc_c_fast(y, M[, k], horizon), numeric(1))
  } else {
    vapply(seq_len(ncol(M)), function(k) .acrc_c_ref(tt, ee, M[, k], horizon), numeric(1))
  }
}
# ---- Point estimates and the analytic covariance, one call per cell ---------
# All 2K markers on one right-hand side, so a single call returns every C and the
# full covariance, from which every paired se(delta) = sqrt(v_aa + v_bb - 2 v_ab)
# follows without another fit.
cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: point estimates for %d markers x 2 scorings x %d horizons...\n",
            length(.acrc_arms), length(annex_crc$horizons))); flush.console()
.acrc_point <- list(); .acrc_V <- list()
for (sc in names(.acrc_scorings)) {
  ss <- .acrc_scorings[[sc]]; .acrc_point[[sc]] <- list(); .acrc_V[[sc]] <- list()
  for (hh in names(.acrc_M)) {
    M <- .acrc_M[[hh]]
    dfr <- data.frame(time = ss$time, event = ss$event, M, check.names = FALSE)
    fml <- stats::as.formula(paste("survival::Surv(time, event) ~",
                                   paste(sprintf("`%s`", .acrc_arms), collapse = " + ")))
    fit <- survival::concordance(fml, data = dfr, timewt = "n/G2", reverse = TRUE, ymax = as.numeric(hh))
    est <- unname(fit$concordance); V <- as.matrix(fit$var)
    nmv <- names(fit$concordance)
    if (!is.null(nmv)) {
      ord <- match(.acrc_arms, gsub("^`|`$", "", nmv))
      stopifnot("concordance returned markers in an unexpected order" = !anyNA(ord))
      est <- est[ord]; V <- V[ord, ord, drop = FALSE]
    }
    names(est) <- .acrc_arms; dimnames(V) <- list(.acrc_arms, .acrc_arms)
    .acrc_point[[sc]][[hh]] <- est; .acrc_V[[sc]][[hh]] <- V
  }
}
# ---- The bootstrap ----------------------------------------------------------
.acrc_jobs <- list()
for (sc in names(.acrc_scorings)) for (hh in names(.acrc_M))
  .acrc_jobs[[length(.acrc_jobs) + 1L]] <- list(scoring = sc, horizon = hh)
.acrc_pilot <- local({
  M <- .acrc_M[[1]]; h <- as.numeric(names(.acrc_M)[1]); ss <- .acrc_scorings[["cr"]]
  t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (i in 1:3) { s <- sample.int(.acrc_n, .acrc_n, replace = TRUE)
    .acrc_score_all(ss$time[s], ss$event[s], M[s, , drop = FALSE], h) }
  as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs")) / 3
})
cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: measured %.3f s per replicate for %d markers; %d jobs x B = %d -> about %.1f min sequential.\n",
            .acrc_pilot, length(.acrc_arms), length(.acrc_jobs), ANNEX_CRC_B,
            .acrc_pilot * ANNEX_CRC_B * length(.acrc_jobs) / 60)); flush.console()
.acrc_cluster <- NULL
if (!is.null(ANNEX_CRC_WORKERS) && as.integer(ANNEX_CRC_WORKERS) > 1L &&
    requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
  nw <- as.integer(ANNEX_CRC_WORKERS)
  options(future.globals.maxSize = 4 * 1024^3)
  if (requireNamespace("parallelly", quietly = TRUE)) {
    cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: starting %d PSOCK workers without project startup files.\n", nw)); flush.console()
    .acrc_cluster <- parallelly::makeClusterPSOCK(nw, rscript_args = "--no-init-file",
                                                  rscript_libs = .libPaths(), connectTimeout = 300,
                                                  validate = TRUE, autoStop = FALSE)
    future::plan(future::cluster, workers = .acrc_cluster)
  } else {
    future::plan(future::multisession, workers = nw)
  }
  cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: with %d workers expect about %.1f min.\n",
              nw, .acrc_pilot * ANNEX_CRC_B * length(.acrc_jobs) / 60 / nw))
}
.acrc_one_job <- function(i) {
  job <- .acrc_jobs[[i]]
  ss <- .acrc_scorings[[job$scoring]]; M <- .acrc_M[[job$horizon]]; h <- as.numeric(job$horizon)
  set.seed(ANNEX_CRC_SEED + i, kind = "Mersenne-Twister")
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, ncol(M), ANNEX_CRC_B, dimnames = list(colnames(M), NULL))
  for (b in seq_len(ANNEX_CRC_B)) {
    s <- sample.int(.acrc_n, .acrc_n, replace = TRUE)
    out[, b] <- .acrc_score_all(ss$time[s], ss$event[s], M[s, , drop = FALSE], h)
  }
  out
}
cat("annex-cr-cindex run: bootstrapping...\n"); flush.console()
.acrc_t0 <- Sys.time()
.acrc_par <- requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE) && future::nbrOfWorkers() > 1L
.acrc_res <- if (.acrc_par) {
  future.apply::future_lapply(seq_along(.acrc_jobs), .acrc_one_job,
                              future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = "survival")
} else {
  lapply(seq_along(.acrc_jobs), function(i) {
    r <- .acrc_one_job(i)
    cat(sprintf("  job %d/%d (%s scoring @ %s m) done, %.1f min elapsed\n", i, length(.acrc_jobs),
                .acrc_jobs[[i]]$scoring, .acrc_jobs[[i]]$horizon,
                as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .acrc_t0, units = "mins")))); flush.console()
    r
  })
}
if (!is.null(.acrc_cluster)) {
  try(future::plan(future::sequential), silent = TRUE)
  try(parallel::stopCluster(.acrc_cluster), silent = TRUE); .acrc_cluster <- NULL
}
cat(sprintf("annex-cr-cindex run: bootstrap finished in %.1f min.\n",
            as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), .acrc_t0, units = "mins"))))
annex_crc_boot <- list()
for (i in seq_along(.acrc_jobs)) {
  j <- .acrc_jobs[[i]]
  if (is.null(annex_crc_boot[[j$scoring]])) annex_crc_boot[[j$scoring]] <- list()
  annex_crc_boot[[j$scoring]][[j$horizon]] <- .acrc_res[[i]]
}
.acrc_q <- function(v, p) { f <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (length(f) < 20L) NA_real_ else stats::quantile(f, probs = p, names = FALSE) }
.acrc_se_ij <- function(V, a, b) sqrt(max(V[a, a] + V[b, b] - 2 * V[a, b], 0))
# ---- TABLE A: per model, scoring x marker ----------------------------------
annex_crc_bymodel <- do.call(rbind, lapply(annex_crc$models, function(m) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(annex_crc$horizons, function(h) {
    hh <- as.character(h); j <- .acrc_colj(h)
    an <- paste0("net::", m); ac <- paste0("cif::", m)
    pcs <- .acrc_point$cs[[hh]]; pcr <- .acrc_point$cr[[hh]]
    bcs <- annex_crc_boot$cs[[hh]]; bcr <- annex_crc_boot$cr[[hh]]
    d_cs <- bcs[ac, ] - bcs[an, ]; d_cr <- bcr[ac, ] - bcr[an, ]
    # Reconciliation with the existing cells: same estimator, but on the model's
    # OWN finite subset instead of the common one, which is how
    # `paired-delta-c-absolute-risk` computes it. Point estimate only.
    okm <- annex_crc$ok_own[[m]]
    own <- tryCatch(.acrc_c_ref(annex_crc$time_r_all[okm], annex_crc$event_r_all[okm],
                                annex_crc$netrisk_own[[m]][okm, j], h), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    data.frame(
      model = m, horizon = h, n_common = .acrc_n, n_own = sum(okm),
      readmissions_by_horizon = sum(.acrc_er == 1L & .acrc_tr <= h),
      competing_deaths_by_horizon = sum(.acrc_st == 2L & .acrc_tr <= h),
      C_cs_netrisk = unname(pcs[an]),
      C_cs_netrisk_lower = .acrc_q(bcs[an, ], 0.025), C_cs_netrisk_upper = .acrc_q(bcs[an, ], 0.975),
      C_cs_cif = unname(pcs[ac]),
      delta_marker_cs = unname(pcs[ac] - pcs[an]),
      delta_marker_cs_lower = .acrc_q(d_cs, 0.025), delta_marker_cs_upper = .acrc_q(d_cs, 0.975),
      delta_marker_cs_se_ij = .acrc_se_ij(.acrc_V$cs[[hh]], ac, an),
      C_cr_netrisk = unname(pcr[an]),
      C_cr_cif = unname(pcr[ac]),
      C_cr_cif_lower = .acrc_q(bcr[ac, ], 0.025), C_cr_cif_upper = .acrc_q(bcr[ac, ], 0.975),
      delta_marker_cr = unname(pcr[ac] - pcr[an]),
      delta_marker_cr_lower = .acrc_q(d_cr, 0.025), delta_marker_cr_upper = .acrc_q(d_cr, 0.975),
      delta_marker_cr_se_ij = .acrc_se_ij(.acrc_V$cr[[hh]], ac, an),
      delta_scoring_netrisk_point_only = unname(pcr[an] - pcs[an]),
      C_cs_netrisk_ownmask = own,
      spearman_netrisk_cif = stats::cor(annex_crc$netrisk[[m]][, j], annex_crc$cif[[m]][, j], method = "spearman"),
      B_valid = sum(is.finite(d_cr)), B_requested = ANNEX_CRC_B,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))
rownames(annex_crc_bymodel) <- NULL
# ---- TABLE B: pairwise paired delta C on the CIF marker --------------------
.acrc_key <- function(x) gsub("[[:space:]]+", "", x)
.acrc_prs <- utils::combn(annex_crc$models, 2L, simplify = FALSE)
annex_crc_pairs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.acrc_prs, function(pr) {
  shared <- identical(.acrc_key(annex_crc$f_readmit_txt[[pr[1]]]), .acrc_key(annex_crc$f_readmit_txt[[pr[2]]]))
  shared_d <- identical(.acrc_key(annex_crc$f_death_txt[[pr[1]]]), .acrc_key(annex_crc$f_death_txt[[pr[2]]]))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(annex_crc$horizons, function(h) {
    hh <- as.character(h); j <- .acrc_colj(h)
    aA <- paste0("cif::", pr[1]); aB <- paste0("cif::", pr[2])
    p <- .acrc_point$cr[[hh]]; B <- annex_crc_boot$cr[[hh]]
    d <- B[aA, ] - B[aB, ]; delta <- unname(p[aA] - p[aB])
    lo <- .acrc_q(d, 0.025); hi <- .acrc_q(d, 0.975)
    se <- .acrc_se_ij(.acrc_V$cr[[hh]], aA, aB)
    data.frame(
      model_A = pr[1], model_B = pr[2], horizon = h, n = .acrc_n,
      shared_readmission_formula = shared, shared_death_formula = shared_d,
      readmissions_by_horizon = sum(.acrc_er == 1L & .acrc_tr <= h),
      competing_deaths_by_horizon = sum(.acrc_st == 2L & .acrc_tr <= h),
      C_A = unname(p[aA]), C_B = unname(p[aB]), delta_C = delta,
      delta_boot_lower = lo, delta_boot_upper = hi,
      boot_mean = mean(d[is.finite(d)]), centering_bias = mean(d[is.finite(d)]) - delta,
      point_inside_boot_ci = is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi) && delta >= lo && delta <= hi,
      se_delta_ij = se, delta_ij_lower = delta - .acrc_crit * se, delta_ij_upper = delta + .acrc_crit * se,
      boot_over_ij_width = if (se > 0 && is.finite(lo) && is.finite(hi)) (hi - lo) / (2 * .acrc_crit * se) else NA_real_,
      spearman_rho = stats::cor(annex_crc$cif[[pr[1]]][, j], annex_crc$cif[[pr[2]]][, j], method = "spearman"),
      B_valid = sum(is.finite(d)), B_requested = ANNEX_CRC_B,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  }))
}))

# annex_ibs_classical_pred24_p225_chunk.R  (2026-08-22)
# ============================================================================
# CLASSICAL (Graf) IBS EXTENDED TO THE PREDICTION24 CANDIDATES, OUT OF FOLD ON
# THE DEVELOPMENT COHORT (py_corrected_datasets_boot, the 80 percent training
# split; the frozen 20 percent test set is never touched here).
# Produces:
#   annex_ibsg_table     per-arm IBS with bootstrap 95 percent intervals, in the
#                        SAME column layout as ibs_dev_table (arm, estimand,
#                        horizon_months, ibs_oof, ibs_lo95, ibs_hi95), so the new
#                        rows can be rbind-ed straight onto it.
#   annex_ibsg_pairwise  paired differences across every arm, old and new, from
#                        one shared subject bootstrap.
#   annex_ibsg_points    the point objects, kept so a later chunk can bootstrap
#                        further comparisons without refitting.
# Kernel prerequisites: NONE, but everything already in the session is reused:
# .dev or py_corrected_datasets_boot, FOLDS, S_oof_readmit, S_oof_death_full,
# S_oof_death_shap, dual_fits, ds_dual_fits and the classical-IBS bundle.
# Place at the END of the notebook. Adds objects; replaces nothing.
# ============================================================================
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))
stopifnot(requireNamespace("pec", quietly = TRUE))
.annexg_t0 <- proc.time()
if (!exists("ANNEXG_REFIT", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEXG_REFIT <- FALSE
if (!exists("ANNEXG_INCLUDE_SHAP_READMIT", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEXG_INCLUDE_SHAP_READMIT <- TRUE
# When TRUE the prediction24 readmission arms are ALSO paired with the
# prediction24 mortality models, which adds three more prediction definitions and
# roughly triples the readmission arm count. Left FALSE so the new arms use the
# same three definitions as the existing twelve (net risk, CIF with Full PH
# death, CIF with SHAP-informed death) and slot into that table unchanged.
if (!exists("ANNEXG_DS_DEATH_PAIRINGS", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEXG_DS_DEATH_PAIRINGS <- FALSE
# Assigned only when absent, so a caller can lower them for a trial run. The

# ---- DS PROVENANCE GUARD ---------------------------------------------------
# The DeepSurv-informed common-grid cache is named after the prediction24 sidecar
# stem it was built from. Those sidecars get regenerated, and on 2026-08-23 the
# cache on disk was still the 2026-07-26 one while 2026-08-11 sidecars existed,
# whose `interact` formulas had grown (readmission gained 8 interactions;
# mortality gained 5 main effects and 12 interactions). Reporting arms built from
# a superseded stem is exactly the silent staleness this project cannot afford,
# so the newest COMPLETE sidecar triplet is located and compared against the stem
# in the cache filename, and a mismatch STOPS here. The fix is to re-run the cell
# `deltaCIBS-ds-common-grid`, which selects the newest stem itself and writes a
# new cache without touching the old one. Set ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM <- TRUE
# only to reproduce an older table on purpose.
if (!exists("ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM <- FALSE
.ds_stem_check <- function(cache_file) {
  dir0 <- dirname(cache_file)
  suf <- c("dual_shap_ds_py", "dual_shap_ds_upd_py", "dual_shap_ds_int_py")
  pat <- paste0("^pred24.*__(", paste(suf, collapse = "|"), ")[.]rds$")
  ff <- list.files(dir0, pattern = pat)
  if (!length(ff)) return(invisible(NULL))
  stems <- unique(sub(paste0("__(", paste(suf, collapse = "|"), ")[.]rds$"), "", ff))
  complete <- stems[vapply(stems, function(s)
    all(file.exists(file.path(dir0, paste0(s, "__", suf, ".rds")))), logical(1))]
  if (!length(complete)) return(invisible(NULL))
  mt <- vapply(complete, function(s)
    max(file.info(file.path(dir0, paste0(s, "__", suf, ".rds")))$mtime),
    as.POSIXct("1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"))
  newest <- complete[which.max(mt)]
  used <- sub("^pred225_ds_common_grid__", "", sub("__v1[.]rds$", "", basename(cache_file)))
  if (identical(used, newest)) {
    message("annex: DS sidecar stem check passed; the cache matches the newest complete triplet (", newest, ").")
  } else if (isTRUE(ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM)) {
    warning("annex: the DS cache was built from ", used, " but ", newest,
            " is newer. Proceeding because ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM is TRUE.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    stop("annex: the DeepSurv-informed cache was built from sidecar stem ", used,
         " but a newer complete triplet exists, ", newest,
         ". Re-run the cell `deltaCIBS-ds-common-grid` to rebuild the cache from it, then rerun this cell. ",
         "Set ANNEX_DS_ALLOW_STALE_STEM <- TRUE only if you deliberately want the older arms.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(newest)
}
.annexg_get_fits <- function(nm, file_pattern, field) {
  if (exists(nm, envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) return(get(nm, envir = globalenv()))
  ff <- list.files(.annexg_data_out, pattern = file_pattern, full.names = TRUE)
  if (!length(ff)) return(NULL)
  ff <- ff[order(file.info(ff)$mtime, decreasing = TRUE)][1L]
  message("annex-ibs-g: reading ", basename(ff), " (", round(file.info(ff)$size / 1024^2), " MB).")
  # Any cache read here that is a DS common-grid bundle must come from the newest
  # sidecar triplet; see the DS provenance guard above.
  if (grepl("^pred225_ds_common_grid__", basename(ff))) .ds_stem_check(ff)
  tryCatch(readRDS(ff)[[field]], error = function(e) {
    message("annex-ibs-g: could not read ", basename(ff), " (", conditionMessage(e), ").")
    NULL })
}

            1L + length(.annexg_cif_death),
            length(unique(vapply(Filter(function(t) t$outcome == "mortality", .annexg_target), `[[`, "", "model"))),
            paste(unique(vapply(Filter(function(t) t$outcome == "mortality", .annexg_target), `[[`, "", "model")), collapse = ", "),
            length(.annexg_target)))
# ---- 4c. Which target arms are ALREADY scored -------------------------------
# The legacy bundle stores a scored point per arm, and a point is all the shared
# bootstrap needs, so any target arm it already holds costs nothing. Loading it
# here rather than at merge time is what lets the refit list below be the minimum.
.annexg_have <- list()
if (exists("ibs_dev_pairwise_points", inherits = TRUE) && is.list(ibs_dev_pairwise_points)) {
  .annexg_have <- ibs_dev_pairwise_points
  cat("annex-ibs-g: reusing scored arms from the live ibs_dev_pairwise_points.\n")
} else if (file.exists(ANNEXG_LEGACY_BUNDLE)) {
  cat("annex-ibs-g: reading the classical-annex bundle", basename(ANNEXG_LEGACY_BUNDLE), "for arms already scored.\n")
  .annexg_have <- tryCatch(readRDS(ANNEXG_LEGACY_BUNDLE)$points, error = function(e) list())
}
.annexg_have <- .annexg_have[vapply(.annexg_have, function(p)
  is.list(p) && !is.null(p$contrib_trapezoid) && !is.null(p$horizons) &&
  identical(as.numeric(p$horizons), as.numeric(ANNEXG_HORIZONS)) &&
  nrow(p$contrib_trapezoid) == .annexg_N, logical(1))]
.annexg_todo_arms <- setdiff(names(.annexg_target), names(.annexg_have))
cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: %d of %d target arms are already scored; %d must be built here.\n",
            length(.annexg_target) - length(.annexg_todo_arms), length(.annexg_target),
            length(.annexg_todo_arms)))
# ---- 5. Expected baseline strata, derived per formula ------------------------
# Imposing the ten-stratum updated2 design on every model would be wrong, so the
# count is derived from each formula against the development data. The assertion
# on every fit is what catches the 2026-07-12 failure mode, a strata() term
# silently fitted as a covariate.
.annexg_strata_calls <- function(e) {
  if (!is.call(e)) return(list())
  nm <- paste(deparse(e[[1]]), collapse = "")
  if (nm %in% c("strata", "survival::strata")) return(list(e))
  unlist(lapply(as.list(e)[-1L], .annexg_strata_calls), recursive = FALSE)
}
.annexg_n_strata <- function(f, data) {
  cs <- .annexg_strata_calls(f[[3]])
  if (!length(cs)) return(1L)
  vals <- list()
  for (cl in cs) for (a in as.list(cl)[-1L])
    vals[[length(vals) + 1L]] <- eval(a, envir = data, enclos = environment(f))
  if (!length(vals) || any(vapply(vals, length, integer(1)) != nrow(data)))
    stop("annex-ibs-g: could not evaluate the strata terms of ", paste(deparse(f), collapse = " "), call. = FALSE)
  comb <- if (length(vals) == 1L) droplevels(factor(vals[[1]]))
          else do.call(interaction, c(lapply(vals, factor), list(drop = TRUE, lex.order = TRUE)))
  as.integer(nlevels(droplevels(comb)))
}
# ---- 6. Which dense-grid matrices are needed, and which already exist --------
# Only the arms that are NOT already scored drive a refit, and a CIF arm needs its
# readmission matrix and its mortality matrix, so the set is derived from the
# to-do list instead of being declared by hand.
.annexg_need <- list()
for (a in .annexg_todo_arms) {
  t <- .annexg_target[[a]]
  if (!is.na(t$readmit)) .annexg_need[[paste0("readmit__", t$readmit)]] <- .annexg_readmit_models[[t$readmit]]
  if (!is.na(t$death))   .annexg_need[[paste0("death__", t$death)]]     <- .annexg_death_models[[t$death]]
}
.annexg_valid <- function(S) is.matrix(S) && identical(dim(S), c(.annexg_N, length(ANNEXG_GRID))) && all(is.finite(S))
.annexg_S <- list()
.annexg_session <- list()
for (nm in names(.annexg_cif_death)) {
  if (identical(nm, "full-death")) .annexg_session[[paste0("death__", .annexg_cif_death[[nm]])]] <- "S_oof_death_full"
  if (identical(nm, "shap-death")) .annexg_session[[paste0("death__", .annexg_cif_death[[nm]])]] <- "S_oof_death_shap"
}
if ("readmit__shap" %in% names(.annexg_need)) .annexg_session[["readmit__shap"]] <- "S_oof_readmit"
for (key in names(.annexg_session)) {
  obj <- .annexg_session[[key]]
  if (key %in% names(.annexg_need) && exists(obj, inherits = TRUE)) {
    cand <- get(obj, inherits = TRUE)
    if (.annexg_valid(cand)) {
      .annexg_S[[key]] <- cand
      message("annex-ibs-g: reusing ", obj, " from the session, no refit for ", key, ".")
    }
  }
}
# ---- 7. Dense-grid out-of-fold refitting ------------------------------------
.annexg_cache_hit <- FALSE
if (!ANNEXG_REFIT && file.exists(ANNEXG_CACHE)) {
  .annexg_cc <- tryCatch(readRDS(ANNEXG_CACHE), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(.annexg_cc) &&
      identical(as.numeric(.annexg_cc$meta$grid), as.numeric(ANNEXG_GRID)) &&
      identical(as.numeric(.annexg_cc$meta$horizons), as.numeric(ANNEXG_HORIZONS)) &&
      identical(.annexg_cc$meta$formula_keys, vapply(.annexg_need, .annexg_key, "")) &&
      all(.annexg_todo_arms %in% names(.annexg_cc$points))) {
    annex_ibsg_points <- .annexg_cc$points[.annexg_todo_arms]
    .annexg_arm_meta <- .annexg_cc$arm_metadata
    .annexg_cache_hit <- TRUE
    cat("annex-ibs-g: cache hit, dense-grid refitting skipped.\n")
  } else {
    cat("annex-ibs-g: cache present but its grid, horizons, formulas or arm coverage differ; rebuilding.\n")
  }
  rm(.annexg_cc)
}
if (!.annexg_cache_hit) {
  .annexg_todo <- setdiff(names(.annexg_need), names(.annexg_S))
  .annexg_exp <- vapply(.annexg_need[.annexg_todo], .annexg_n_strata, integer(1), data = .annexg_dev[[1]])
  cat("annex-ibs-g: dense-grid matrices to fit: ",
      paste(sprintf("%s (expect %d strata)", .annexg_todo, .annexg_exp), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: %d formulas x %d imputations x %d folds = %d Cox fits on %d grid nodes.\n",
              length(.annexg_todo), length(.annexg_dev), length(.annexg_folds[[1]]),
              length(.annexg_todo) * length(.annexg_dev) * length(.annexg_folds[[1]]), length(ANNEXG_GRID)))
  flush.console()
  .annexg_cluster <- NULL
  if (requireNamespace("future", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
    nw <- if (!is.null(ANNEXG_WORKERS)) as.integer(ANNEXG_WORKERS) else
      max(1L, min(5L, tryCatch(parallel::detectCores(logical = TRUE), error = function(e) 4L) - 2L))
    options(future.globals.maxSize = max(8 * 1024^3, 3 * as.numeric(utils::object.size(.annexg_dev[[1]]))))
    if (nw > 1L && requireNamespace("parallelly", quietly = TRUE)) {
      # PSOCK workers started WITHOUT project startup files: the renv activation
      # script in this project's .Rprofile is what makes plain multisession
      # workers slow to start and occasionally fail, which is why
      # `p225-annex-ibs-classical-dev` uses this same construction.
      cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: starting %d PSOCK workers without startup files.\n", nw)); flush.console()
      .annexg_cluster <- parallelly::makeClusterPSOCK(nw, rscript_args = "--no-init-file",
                                                      rscript_libs = .libPaths(), connectTimeout = 300,
                                                      validate = TRUE, autoStop = FALSE)
      future::plan(future::cluster, workers = .annexg_cluster)
    } else if (nw > 1L) {
      future::plan(future::multisession, workers = nw)
    } else {
      future::plan(future::sequential)
    }
  }
  on.exit({
    try(future::plan(future::sequential), silent = TRUE)
    if (!is.null(.annexg_cluster)) try(parallel::stopCluster(.annexg_cluster), silent = TRUE)
  }, add = TRUE)
  .annexg_oof <- function(formula, expected_strata, label) {
    K <- length(ANNEXG_GRID); acc <- matrix(0, .annexg_N, K)
    for (im in seq_along(.annexg_dev)) {
      d <- .annexg_dev[[im]]; folds <- .annexg_folds[[im]]
      res <- if (requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
        future.apply::future_lapply(folds, function(vi) {
          fit <- survival::coxph(formula, data = d[-vi, , drop = FALSE], ties = "efron",
                                 x = TRUE, y = TRUE, model = TRUE)
          bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
          ns <- if (is.null(bh$strata)) 1L else nlevels(droplevels(factor(bh$strata)))
          list(n_strata = ns, S = matrix(as.numeric(pec::predictSurvProb(
            fit, newdata = d[vi, , drop = FALSE], times = ANNEXG_GRID)), length(vi), K))
        }, future.seed = TRUE, future.packages = c("survival", "pec"))
      } else {
        lapply(folds, function(vi) {
          fit <- survival::coxph(formula, data = d[-vi, , drop = FALSE], ties = "efron",
                                 x = TRUE, y = TRUE, model = TRUE)
          bh <- survival::basehaz(fit, centered = FALSE)
          ns <- if (is.null(bh$strata)) 1L else nlevels(droplevels(factor(bh$strata)))
          list(n_strata = ns, S = matrix(as.numeric(pec::predictSurvProb(
            fit, newdata = d[vi, , drop = FALSE], times = ANNEXG_GRID)), length(vi), K))
        })
      }
      for (j in seq_along(folds)) {
        if (res[[j]]$n_strata != expected_strata)
          stop(sprintf("%s, imputation %d, fold %d: %d baseline strata, expected %d. A strata() term may have been fitted as a covariate.",
                       label, im, j, res[[j]]$n_strata, expected_strata), call. = FALSE)
        acc[folds[[j]], ] <- acc[folds[[j]], ] + res[[j]]$S
      }
      rm(res); cat("."); flush.console()
    }
    S <- acc / length(.annexg_dev)
    if (anyNA(S)) stop(sprintf("%s: out-of-fold survival contains NA.", label), call. = FALSE)
    stopifnot(min(S) >= -1e-10, max(S) <= 1 + 1e-10)
    cat(sprintf(" %s done (%.1f min elapsed)\n", label, (proc.time() - .annexg_t0)[["elapsed"]] / 60))
    pmin(pmax(S, 0), 1)
  }
  for (mn in .annexg_todo)
    .annexg_S[[mn]] <- .annexg_oof(.annexg_need[[mn]], .annexg_exp[[mn]], mn)
  try(future::plan(future::sequential), silent = TRUE)
  if (!is.null(.annexg_cluster)) { try(parallel::stopCluster(.annexg_cluster), silent = TRUE); .annexg_cluster <- NULL }
  invisible(gc())
  # ---- 8. Exact competing-hazard CIF, with its mandatory control -------------
  .annexg_cif <- function(S_r, S_d) {
    if (!identical(dim(S_r), dim(S_d))) stop("annex-ibs-g: CIF inputs have different dimensions.", call. = FALSE)
    H_r <- -log(pmax(S_r, 1e-12)); H_d <- -log(pmax(S_d, 1e-12)); S_all <- S_r * S_d
    n <- nrow(S_r); K <- ncol(S_r); cif <- matrix(0, n, K)
    prev_S <- rep(1, n); prev_Hr <- rep(0, n); prev_Hd <- rep(0, n); acc <- rep(0, n)
    for (k in seq_len(K)) {
      dr <- pmax(H_r[, k] - prev_Hr, 0); dd <- pmax(H_d[, k] - prev_Hd, 0); da <- dr + dd
      frac <- ifelse(da > 0, dr / da, 0); pev <- -expm1(-da)
      acc <- acc + prev_S * frac * pev
      cif[, k] <- acc
      prev_S <- S_all[, k]; prev_Hr <- H_r[, k]; prev_Hd <- H_d[, k]
    }
    pmin(pmax(cif, 0), 1)
  }
  local({
    g <- c(0, 0.25, 1, 6, 12, 36, 60)
    Sr <- rbind(exp(-0.01 * g), exp(-0.10 * g))
    no_d <- matrix(1, nrow(Sr), ncol(Sr)); with_d <- rbind(exp(-0.02 * g), exp(-0.20 * g))
    e1 <- max(abs(.annexg_cif(Sr, no_d) - (1 - Sr)))
    e2 <- max(.annexg_cif(Sr, with_d) - (1 - Sr))
    if (!is.finite(e1) || e1 > 1e-12 || !is.finite(e2) || e2 > 1e-12)
      stop("annex-ibs-g: the exact competing-hazard CIF control failed.", call. = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: exact CIF control passed (no-death error %.3e, competing-death excess %.3e).\n", e1, e2))
  })
  # ---- 9. Score exactly the target arms that are not already scored ---------
  .annexg_mk_death <- function(S) list(S = S, grid = ANNEXG_GRID, n_imp = length(.annexg_dev),
    y_test = data.frame(time = .annexg_dt, event = .annexg_de),
    y_train = data.frame(time = .annexg_dt, event = .annexg_de))
  .annexg_mk_readmit <- function(S) list(S = S, grid = ANNEXG_GRID, n_imp = length(.annexg_dev),
    rt_val = .annexg_rt, re_val = .annexg_re, dt_val = .annexg_dt, de_val = .annexg_de,
    rt_tr = .annexg_rt, re_tr = .annexg_re, dt_tr = .annexg_dt, de_tr = .annexg_de)
  annex_ibsg_points <- list(); .annexg_meta <- list()
  .annexg_add <- function(arm, point, t) {
    point$method <- if (identical(t$outcome, "mortality")) "death" else "readmission-aj"
    annex_ibsg_points[[arm]] <<- point
    .annexg_meta[[length(.annexg_meta) + 1L]] <<- data.frame(
      arm = arm, outcome = t$outcome, model = t$model,
      prediction_definition = t$definition, family = t$family, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
  # The CIF is rebuilt per arm from its own two matrices. Both controls travel with
  # it: a cumulative incidence must be nondecreasing on the grid, and it can never
  # exceed the net risk of the same readmission model, since removing the competing
  # cause can only take probability away.
  .annexg_score_target <- function(arm) {
    t <- .annexg_target[[arm]]
    if (identical(t$outcome, "mortality")) {
      S <- .annexg_S[[paste0("death__", t$death)]]
      return(ibs_classical_point(.annexg_mk_death(S), horizons = ANNEXG_HORIZONS))
    }
    Sr <- .annexg_S[[paste0("readmit__", t$readmit)]]
    if (identical(t$definition, "net-risk"))
      return(ibs_classical_readmit(.annexg_mk_readmit(Sr), ANNEXG_HORIZONS, method = "aalen-johansen"))
    Sd <- .annexg_S[[paste0("death__", t$death)]]
    cif <- .annexg_cif(Sr, Sd)
    if (any(cif[, -1L, drop = FALSE] + 1e-10 < cif[, -ncol(cif), drop = FALSE]))
      stop("annex-ibs-g: a computed CIF is not nondecreasing for ", arm, ".", call. = FALSE)
    ex <- max(cif - (1 - Sr), na.rm = TRUE)
    if (!is.finite(ex) || ex > 1e-10)
      stop(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: a computed CIF exceeds its net risk for %s by %.3e.", arm, ex), call. = FALSE)
    out <- ibs_classical_readmit(.annexg_mk_readmit(1 - cif), ANNEXG_HORIZONS, method = "aalen-johansen")
    rm(cif); invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))
    out
  }
  for (arm in .annexg_todo_arms) {
    .annexg_add(arm, .annexg_score_target(arm), .annexg_target[[arm]])
    cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: scored %-52s (%.1f min elapsed)\n", arm,
                (proc.time() - .annexg_t0)[["elapsed"]] / 60)); flush.console()
  }
  .annexg_arm_meta <- do.call(rbind, .annexg_meta); rownames(.annexg_arm_meta) <- NULL
  rm(.annexg_S); invisible(gc())
  saveRDS(list(points = annex_ibsg_points, arm_metadata = .annexg_arm_meta,
               meta = list(grid = ANNEXG_GRID, horizons = ANNEXG_HORIZONS,
                           formula_keys = vapply(.annexg_need, .annexg_key, ""),
                           target_arms = names(.annexg_target),
                           scored_arms = .annexg_todo_arms,
                           n = .annexg_N, created = as.character(Sys.time()))),
          ANNEXG_CACHE)
  cat("annex-ibs-g: cached to ", ANNEXG_CACHE, "\n", sep = "")
}
cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: %d arm(s) scored in this run.\n", length(annex_ibsg_points)))
# ---- 10. Union of scored arms, and the completeness assertion ----------------
# Arms already scored elsewhere are taken exactly as stored: only
# $contrib_trapezoid and $horizons feed the shared bootstrap, so nothing is
# rescored and pred225_annex_ibs_pairwise_all_arms_v2.rds is never written to.
# The union is then checked against the declared inventory, so a table that
# quietly lost a candidate cannot reach the manuscript.
.annexg_all_points <- c(.annexg_have[intersect(names(.annexg_target), names(.annexg_have))],
                        annex_ibsg_points)
.annexg_reused <- intersect(names(.annexg_target), names(.annexg_have))
.annexg_all_meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.annexg_all_points), function(a) {
  t <- .annexg_target[[a]]
  data.frame(arm = a, outcome = t$outcome, model = t$model,
             prediction_definition = t$definition, family = t$family,
             source = if (a %in% .annexg_reused) "reused" else "scored here",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
rownames(.annexg_all_meta) <- NULL
.annexg_missing <- setdiff(names(.annexg_target), names(.annexg_all_points))
if (length(.annexg_missing))
  stop("annex-ibs-g: the table does not cover the declared inventory. Missing arms: ",
       paste(.annexg_missing, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: inventory complete, %d arms (%d reused, %d scored here).\n",
            length(.annexg_all_points), length(.annexg_reused), length(annex_ibsg_points)))
print(table(.annexg_all_meta$outcome, .annexg_all_meta$family))
# ---- 11. ONE shared subject bootstrap over every arm ------------------------
# G is fixed by the pooled cohort, so each subject's trapezoided contribution is
# constant and one replicate is a matrix-vector product. Using the SAME resampled
# subjects for every arm in every replicate is what makes all the differences
# below genuinely paired, old against old, new against new, and old against new.
cat(sprintf("annex-ibs-g: shared subject bootstrap, %d arms x %d horizons x B = %d.\n",
            length(.annexg_all_points), length(ANNEXG_HORIZONS), ANNEXG_B)); flush.console()
.annexg_C <- lapply(.annexg_all_points, `[[`, "contrib_trapezoid")
.annexg_h <- as.numeric(ANNEXG_HORIZONS)
set.seed(ANNEXG_SEED, kind = "Mersenne-Twister")
.annexg_boot <- array(NA_real_, c(length(.annexg_C), length(.annexg_h), ANNEXG_B),
                      dimnames = list(names(.annexg_C), as.character(.annexg_h), paste0("b", seq_len(ANNEXG_B))))
for (b in seq_len(ANNEXG_B)) {
  cnt <- tabulate(sample.int(.annexg_N, .annexg_N, replace = TRUE), nbins = .annexg_N)
  for (a in seq_along(.annexg_C))
    .annexg_boot[a, , b] <- as.numeric(cnt %*% .annexg_C[[a]]) / .annexg_N / .annexg_h
  if (b %% 100L == 0L) { cat(sprintf(" %d", b)); flush.console() }
}
cat("\n")
.annexg_q <- function(M, p) apply(M, 1L, function(x) {
  f <- x[is.finite(x)]; if (length(f) < 20L) NA_real_ else stats::quantile(f, probs = p, names = FALSE) })
# ---- 12. Per-arm table, in the layout of ibs_dev_table ----------------------
annex_ibsg_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(.annexg_all_points), function(a) {
  md <- .annexg_all_meta[match(a, .annexg_all_meta$arm), , drop = FALSE]
  bm <- .annexg_boot[a, , , drop = TRUE]
  data.frame(arm = a, family = md$family, outcome = md$outcome, model = md$model,
             estimand = md$prediction_definition,
             horizon_months = .annexg_h, ibs_oof = .annexg_all_points[[a]]$ibs$ibs,
             ibs_lo95 = .annexg_q(bm, 0.025), ibs_hi95 = .annexg_q(bm, 0.975),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
annex_ibsg_table <- annex_ibsg_table[order(annex_ibsg_table$outcome, annex_ibsg_table$horizon_months,
                                           annex_ibsg_table$estimand, annex_ibsg_table$ibs_oof), ]
rownames(annex_ibsg_table) <- NULL
# ---- 13. Paired differences across every arm --------------------------------
.annexg_pairs <- c(
  utils::combn(.annexg_all_meta$arm[.annexg_all_meta$outcome == "readmission"], 2L, simplify = FALSE),
  utils::combn(.annexg_all_meta$arm[.annexg_all_meta$outcome == "mortality"], 2L, simplify = FALSE))
annex_ibsg_pairwise <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.annexg_pairs, function(pr) {
  mA <- .annexg_all_meta[match(pr[1], .annexg_all_meta$arm), , drop = FALSE]
  mB <- .annexg_all_meta[match(pr[2], .annexg_all_meta$arm), , drop = FALSE]
  bA <- .annexg_boot[pr[1], , , drop = TRUE]; bB <- .annexg_boot[pr[2], , , drop = TRUE]
  bd <- bA - bB
  pA <- .annexg_all_points[[pr[1]]]$ibs$ibs; pB <- .annexg_all_points[[pr[2]]]$ibs$ibs
  data.frame(
    outcome = mA$outcome,
    comparison = if (mA$family == mB$family) paste("within", mA$family) else "Cox vs DeepSurv-informed",
    definition_scope = if (mA$outcome == "mortality") "mortality pair"
                       else if (mA$prediction_definition == mB$prediction_definition) "within prediction definition"
                       else "cross prediction definition",
    model_A = mA$model, model_B = mB$model, family_A = mA$family, family_B = mB$family,
    prediction_A = mA$prediction_definition, prediction_B = mB$prediction_definition,
    arm_A = pr[1], arm_B = pr[2], horizon_months = .annexg_h, n = .annexg_N,
    ibs_A = pA, ibs_A_lo = .annexg_q(bA, 0.025), ibs_A_hi = .annexg_q(bA, 0.975),
    ibs_B = pB, ibs_B_lo = .annexg_q(bB, 0.025), ibs_B_hi = .annexg_q(bB, 0.975),
    delta_ibs = pA - pB, delta_lo = .annexg_q(bd, 0.025), delta_hi = .annexg_q(bd, 0.975),
    bootstrap_mean = rowMeans(bd, na.rm = TRUE),
    centering_bias = rowMeans(bd, na.rm = TRUE) - (pA - pB),
    bootstrap_valid = rowSums(is.finite(bd)), bootstrap_requested = ANNEXG_B,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}))
annex_ibsg_pairwise <- annex_ibsg_pairwise[order(annex_ibsg_pairwise$outcome,
                                                 annex_ibsg_pairwise$horizon_months,
                                                 -abs(annex_ibsg_pairwise$delta_ibs)), ]
rownames(annex_ibsg_pairwise) <- NULL
# ---- 14. Report -------------------------------------------------------------
# delta_ibs = IBS_A - IBS_B, so a NEGATIVE difference favours A: lower prediction
# error is better. That is the opposite sign convention from the delta C tables,

# ============================================================================
# ANNEX CALIBRATION FIGURE, STEP 2/6: build the two canonical data inputs.
#   annex_cal_bins  : binned calibration estimates with pointwise 95% CIs
#                     (model, time_horizon, horizon_label, bin, n_bin,
#                      bin_mean_pred, bin_obs_prop, bin_obs_lower, bin_obs_upper)
#   annex_cal_preds : individual predicted risks feeding the marginal densities
#                     (model, time_horizon, horizon_label, pred_risk)
# Prediction sources (FROZEN holdout predictions, no refitting here; MI-pooled
# by simple average across the imputation items, the convention used by
# .holdout_bootstrap_calibration_readmit_from_raw and
# bootstrap_calibration_indices):
#   A_readmit_cif : results_boot_val_bp2_cif$raw_predictions[[i]]$readmission
#                   (joint CIF: CSC readmission paired with the SHAP-informed
#                   mortality model, panel A of the main-text figure)
#   B_death_full  : results_boot_val_bp1$raw_predictions[[i]]$death
#   C_death_shap  : results_boot_val_bp2$raw_predictions[[i]]$death
# Observed side, computed WITHIN each bin of the MI-pooled predicted risk
# (outcomes are identical across imputations, so item 1's y_val is used):
#   readmission -> Aalen-Johansen CIF, death as a competing risk
#   mortality   -> Kaplan-Meier risk, 1 - S(t)
#
# UNCERTAINTY, and why there are two options (ANNEX_CI_METHOD):
#   "analytic"  (default) pointwise 95% log-log CI of the within-bin
#               Aalen-Johansen or Kaplan-Meier estimate. It answers "given
#               this group of patients, how precisely is THEIR observed risk
#               known", holding the grouping fixed. This is what grouped
#               calibration plots conventionally display and it is cheap.
#   "bootstrap" resamples the VALIDATION ROWS B times with replacement,
#               recomputing the bin boundaries and the observed estimate in
#               every replicate, then takes 2.5/97.5 percentiles per bin
#               index. It matches the convention the rest of this project
#               uses for evaluation uncertainty: `holdout-cindex-bootstrap`
#               and `holdout-ici-bootstrap-run` both resample PATIENTS with
#               B = 1000 while holding the frozen predictions fixed, never
#               refitting the models.
#               Do NOT assume the bootstrap interval is the wider of the two:
#               choose the method for the estimand, not for its width. The two
#               answer different questions. The analytic interval conditions on
#               the observed grouping. The bootstrap targets "the observed risk
#               in the k-th quantile group of the predicted-risk distribution",
#               re-estimating the group boundaries in every replicate. Because
#               the boundaries are re-quantiled, each replicate's bin holds
#               about n/g rows by construction, so this design SUPPRESSES
#               bin-occupancy variance rather than adding it.
#               Measured on this held-out sample, median bootstrap width
#               relative to analytic was 0.944 at B = 200, 0.978 at B = 500
#               and 0.986 at B = 1000: the same interval for practical
#               purposes, converging upward as B grows because small B biases
#               extreme percentiles inward. At B = 1000 the bootstrap was the
#               wider of the two in 40 of 96 bins, no bin lost a single
#               replicate to the min_bin_n rule, and the interval contained
#               the full-sample point estimate in 100% of bins, though a
#               percentile interval carries no guarantee that it will.
#               Runtime at B = 1000 was about 2.5 minutes with 8 future
#               workers, roughly 13 minutes sequentially.
#               Further caveat: percentiles are taken per bin INDEX, so a bin
#               is only approximately the same group across replicates.
#   Neither option propagates between-imputation uncertainty in the predicted
#   risks; both condition on the MI-pooled prediction, exactly as the
#   project's own bootstrap engines do.
#
# NOTE ON THE OBJECT NAMES: the `_boot` in results_boot_val_* is legacy. The
# cell `holdout-cindex-ibs-run` does NOT bootstrap; it fits on train and
# predicts on val once per imputation. Resampling in this project lives in the
# dedicated bootstrap cells only.
# Requires in kernel: results_boot_val_bp1, results_boot_val_bp2,
# results_boot_val_bp2_cif, all guaranteed by the cell `annex-calfig-ensure`.
# Place AFTER `annex-calfig-ensure`. Adds new objects; replaces nothing.
# ============================================================================
.annex_to01 <- function(e) {
  # Event coercion for the ALREADY-0/1 y_val$event written by
  # evaluate_dual_cox_holdout_dualscore(). This is deliberately NOT the
  # project's general to01(): it does not handle 1/2 coding (it would invert
  # the indicator) nor label-coded factors (it would return all NA, which
  # .annex_first_event() would read as "nobody had an event", silently
  # producing a zero-risk calibration panel). The stopifnot below turns that
  # latent failure into a loud one if the upstream encoding ever changes.
  out <- if (is.logical(e)) as.integer(e) else suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.integer(as.character(e)) == 1L))
  stopifnot("y_val$event must already be coded 0/1; got something else, refusing to guess" =
    all(!is.na(out)) && all(out %in% c(0L, 1L)))
  out
}
.annex_first_event <- function(r_yval, d_yval) {
  # First-event time and cause. VERBATIM logic of .holdout_cr_first_event() in
  # holdout_cif_cache.R, tie convention included (simultaneous readmission and
  # death counts as death first), duplicated so the annex stays self-contained.
  rt <- as.numeric(r_yval$time)
  re <- .annex_to01(r_yval$event)
  dt <- as.numeric(d_yval$time)
  de <- .annex_to01(d_yval$event)
  ftime <- pmin(rt, dt)
  r_first <- !is.na(re) & re == 1L & is.finite(ftime) & abs(rt - ftime) <= 1e-8
  d_first <- !is.na(de) & de == 1L & is.finite(ftime) & abs(dt - ftime) <= 1e-8
  fstatus <- rep(0L, length(ftime))
  fstatus[r_first & !d_first] <- 1L
  fstatus[d_first & !r_first] <- 2L
  fstatus[r_first & d_first] <- 2L
  list(ftime = ftime, fstatus = fstatus)
}
.annex_pooled_risk <- function(results_boot, block, times) {
  # MI-pooled predicted risk matrix (n_val x length(times)) for one outcome.
  rp <- results_boot$raw_predictions
  stopifnot(is.list(rp), length(rp) >= 1L)
  stopifnot("raw_predictions item lacks the requested outcome block" = !is.null(rp[[1L]][[block]]$surv_val_matrix))
  et <- as.numeric(rp[[1L]]$eval_times)
  cols <- match(times, et)
  stopifnot("requested horizons must be a subset of eval_times" = all(!is.na(cols)))
  n_val <- nrow(as.matrix(rp[[1L]][[block]]$surv_val_matrix))
  acc <- matrix(0, nrow = n_val, ncol = length(times))
  for (item in rp) {
    blk <- item[[block]]
    stopifnot("raw prediction block carries an error" = is.null(blk$error))
    sm <- as.matrix(blk$surv_val_matrix)
    stopifnot("surv_val_matrix row count differs across imputations" = nrow(sm) == n_val)
    acc <- acc + (1 - sm[, cols, drop = FALSE])
  }
  pmin(pmax(acc / length(rp), 0), 1)
}
.annex_obs_aj <- function(ftime, fstatus, horizon, ci = TRUE) {
  # Observed readmission CIF: Aalen-Johansen with death as a competing risk.
  # ci = FALSE is the bootstrap hot path, where only the point estimate per
  # replicate is used. Note it is se.fit = FALSE, not conf.type = "none", that
  # actually skips the Aalen/Greenwood variance: conf.type only suppresses
  # building the interval from a variance that was computed anyway. Measured
  # on survival 3.6.4, dropping se.fit is roughly a fourfold speedup, and the
  # point estimate (pstate) is bit-identical either way.
  st <- factor(fstatus, levels = c(0L, 1L, 2L), labels = c("censor", "readmit", "death"))
  fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(ftime, st) ~ 1,
                           conf.type = if (ci) "log-log" else "none",
                           se.fit = ci, conf.int = 0.95)
  sm <- summary(fit, times = horizon, extend = TRUE)
  k <- match("readmit", fit$states)
  stopifnot("readmit state not found in survfit states" = !is.na(k))
  est <- pmin(pmax(as.numeric(sm$pstate[1L, k]), 0), 1)
  if (!ci) return(c(est = est, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  c(est = est,
    lower = pmin(pmax(as.numeric(sm$lower[1L, k]), 0), 1),
    upper = pmin(pmax(as.numeric(sm$upper[1L, k]), 0), 1))
}
.annex_obs_km <- function(time, event, horizon, ci = TRUE) {
  # Observed all-cause mortality risk: Kaplan-Meier 1 - S(t). CI bounds flip
  # when moving from the survival scale to the risk scale.
  fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1,
                           conf.type = if (ci) "log-log" else "none",
                           se.fit = ci, conf.int = 0.95)
  sm <- summary(fit, times = horizon, extend = TRUE)
  est <- pmin(pmax(1 - as.numeric(sm$surv[1L]), 0), 1)
  if (!ci) return(c(est = est, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  c(est = est,
    lower = pmin(pmax(1 - as.numeric(sm$upper[1L]), 0), 1),
    upper = pmin(pmax(1 - as.numeric(sm$lower[1L]), 0), 1))
}
.annex_bins_cut <- function(pred, g = 10L) {
  # Quantile binning. VERBATIM logic of .vhm_deciles() in
  # validate_holdout_metrics.R (type-8 quantiles, interior cuts, left-closed
  # findInterval, duplicate breaks collapsed), so bin membership matches what
  # the project's calibration engines compute on the same predictions. Engine
  # quirk kept on purpose: findInterval(all.inside = TRUE) merges each extreme
  # decile into its neighbour, so g = 10 yields up to 8 displayed bins with
  # double-width tails, exactly as in cal_*$calibration_curves.
  cuts <- unique(stats::quantile(pred, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = g + 1L), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 8))
  cuts <- cuts[-c(1L, length(cuts))]
  if (length(cuts)) findInterval(pred, cuts, all.inside = TRUE) + 1L else rep(1L, length(pred))
}
.annex_hlab <- function(x) {
  factor(paste0(x, " months"), levels = paste0(c(6L, 12L, 36L, 60L), " months"))
}

# ---- Bootstrap engine, used only when ANNEX_CI_METHOD == "bootstrap" -------
.annex_boot_bin_ci <- function(pv, obs, kind, horizon, keep_bins, B, seed, parallel) {
  # Resample the validation rows, recompute bins AND the within-bin observed
  # estimate in each replicate, then take percentiles per bin index. The model
  # and its predictions are held fixed, mirroring the project's other
  # bootstrap engines, which resample the evaluation data and never the fit.
  #
  # SEEDING: each replicate seeds itself from seed + horizon_index * 100000 + b,
  # the exact pattern .holdout_cindex_boot_dualscore() uses in
  # evaluate_dual_cox_holdout_dualscore.R. Seeding INSIDE the replicate, rather
  # than once before the loop, makes the resample a pure function of b, so the
  # sequential and parallel branches return bit-identical intervals. Verified:
  # without this, the two branches disagreed by up to 0.010 on interval
  # endpoints whose total width is about 0.013, i.e. the same ANNEX_BOOT_SEED
  # silently gave different answers depending on ANNEX_BOOT_PARALLEL.
  # The stream varies by horizon but NOT by model, so all three model rows
  # share their resamples at a given horizon (common random numbers), which is
  # what makes any across-arm comparison of these intervals paired.
  n <- length(pv)
  hi <- match(horizon, ANNEX_TIMES)
  one_rep <- function(.b) {
    set.seed(seed + hi * 100000L + .b, kind = "Mersenne-Twister")
    idx <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    pvb <- pv[idx]
    binsb <- .annex_bins_cut(pvb, .annex_g)
    vapply(keep_bins, function(k) {
      ii <- idx[binsb == k]
      if (length(ii) < .annex_min_bin_n) return(NA_real_)
      if (identical(kind, "aj")) {
        .annex_obs_aj(obs$ftime[ii], obs$fstatus[ii], horizon, ci = FALSE)[["est"]]
      } else {
        .annex_obs_km(obs$time[ii], obs$event[ii], horizon, ci = FALSE)[["est"]]
      }
    }, numeric(1L))
  }
  if (parallel && !requireNamespace("future.apply", quietly = TRUE)) {
    # Never degrade silently: without this the same ANNEX_BOOT_PARALLEL <- TRUE
    # would run in two different ways depending on whether a package happens to
    # be installed, with nothing in the log to say which one happened.
    warning("annex-calfig: ANNEX_BOOT_PARALLEL is TRUE but future.apply is not installed; running sequentially. Results are unaffected (seeding is per replicate) but this will be slower.", call. = FALSE)
    parallel <- FALSE
  }
  if (parallel) {
    # future.seed = TRUE only keeps future.apply's RNG bookkeeping quiet; the
    # set.seed() inside one_rep() runs afterwards and is what actually fixes
    # the resample. VERIFIED 2026-08-20: this branch is bit-identical to the
    # sequential one at the same seed, and about 2.3 times faster.
    reps <- future.apply::future_lapply(seq_len(B), one_rep, future.seed = TRUE)
  } else {
    reps <- lapply(seq_len(B), one_rep)
  }
  mat <- do.call(rbind, reps)
  data.frame(
    bin = keep_bins,
    lower = apply(mat, 2L, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper = apply(mat, 2L, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_rep_ok = apply(mat, 2L, function(z) sum(is.finite(z)))
  )
}

    }
    .annex_bins_acc[[paste(.annex_mc, .annex_h, sep = "_")]] <- .annex_df_h
  }
}

# HORIZONTAL DODGE, DELIBERATELY DISABLED BY DEFAULT.
# A dodge was requested so the two overlaid mortality series stop sitting on
# top of each other, and it is implemented below, but it ships OFF because on
# a calibration plot it corrupts the one reading the figure exists to support.
# The reference line is y = x, so drawing a marker at (x + d, y) turns its
# vertical distance from the diagonal into y - (x + d) instead of y - x. With
# a symmetric dodge the two mortality models are pushed in OPPOSITE
# directions, so their apparent miscalibration is biased in opposite
# directions too, and at 6 and 12 months the offset is comparable to the
# predicted risk itself. Shape and line type already separate the series.
# Set to a small positive fraction of the row range to re-enable, in which
# case the offset and its size MUST be stated in the figure note.
if (!exists("ANNEX_MORT_DODGE_FRAC", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_MORT_DODGE_FRAC <- 0
# Axis range policy. FALSE keeps ONE range per row across all four horizons,
# which makes the horizons directly comparable and lets the tick labels be
# printed once per row, but leaves the 6 and 12 month mortality panels nearly
# empty since observed risk there reaches only about 0.02 on a 0 to 0.15 axis.
# TRUE gives each horizon its own range, driven by that horizon's calibration
# data, and then EVERY panel is labelled, because unlabelled panels on
# differing scales would be read on the first panel's scale. x and y always
# share the same range within a panel, and panels are square, so the identity
# line is a true 45 degree diagonal either way.
if (!exists("ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS", inherits = TRUE)) ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS <- FALSE
ANNEX_POINT_SIZE <- 0.7#1.05
ANNEX_POINT_STROKE <- 0.42#0.45
.annex_theme_main <- function(base_family = .annex_font) {

  # tall, the dashed identity line is not a 45 degree diagonal, and vertical
  # departures from calibration are visually exaggerated relative to

  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = base_family) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,

      axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 1)),
      axis.line = ggplot2::element_line(linewidth = 0.55, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_line(linewidth = 0.55, color = "black"),
      axis.ticks.length = ggplot2::unit(1.6, "pt"),
      axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      #plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 0, r = 1, b = 0, l = 1)
      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 10, r = 1, b = 0, l = 1)
    )

# ============================================================================
# ANNEX CALIBRATION FIGURE, STEP 4/6: panel and row builders.
# .annex_build_panel() returns ONE time-horizon panel: the calibration plot
# plus two marginal density strips composed with patchwork::area(), the same
# arrangement as create_cal_published(). The strips are theme_void(), so they
# carry no axis line, no ticks and no background.
# Panel contents: dashed identity line; binned observed vs mean predicted
# risk, joined; pointwise 95% CI error bars; a bottom strip with the density
# of INDIVIDUAL predicted risks; and a right strip with that same
# distribution projected onto the observed axis, i.e. where observed risks
# would fall under perfect calibration.
# AXIS LABELS: the y tick label at the panel minimum is always suppressed,
# since the x axis already labels the origin. x tick marks and numbers are
# drawn on EVERY panel so each can be read on its own. y tick numbers are
# kept to the leftmost panel of a row when all four share one range, and are
# drawn on every panel under ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS, where the ranges
# genuinely differ and an unlabelled panel would be read on the neighbour.
# Column headers are printed on the top row only.
# Panel letters and row descriptions are drawn INSIDE the first panel of each
# row, in the empty upper-left corner, which is where the journal expects the
# panel letter and where nothing else competes for space.
# Every reduction the drawing performs (bins outside the range, error bars
# clipped at the edge, bins with no estimable CI, predictions excluded from
# the density) is both messaged and accumulated for the figure note.
# Requires in kernel: annex_cal_bins, annex_cal_preds (from
# `annex-calfig-data`) and the constants from `annex-calfig-theme`.
# Place AFTER `annex-calfig-theme`. Adds new objects; replaces nothing.
# ============================================================================
.annex_diag <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.annex_diag$rec <- list()
.annex_diag_reset <- function() .annex_diag$rec <- list()
.annex_diag_add <- function(kind, value, txt) {
  # Records are kept STRUCTURED, not as prose, so the figure note can report a
  # single summary per kind instead of replaying one sentence per panel.
  .annex_diag$rec[[length(.annex_diag$rec) + 1L]] <- list(kind = kind, value = value)
  message("annex-calfig ", txt)
}
.annex_dodge_for <- function(mc, lim) {
  # Display-only horizontal offset, zero unless ANNEX_MORT_DODGE_FRAC was set.
  # See the long note in `annex-calfig-theme` for why this ships disabled.
  if (identical(mc, "B_death_full")) return(-ANNEX_MORT_DODGE_FRAC * diff(lim) / 2)
  if (identical(mc, "C_death_shap")) return(+ANNEX_MORT_DODGE_FRAC * diff(lim) / 2)
  0
}
.annex_limits_for <- function(row_spec, horizon) {
  # One range per row (default) or one per horizon. The per-horizon top is
  # driven by the CALIBRATION data only: the highest bin mean prediction, the
  # highest observed value and the highest CI upper bound. The density strip
  # long right tail is deliberately NOT allowed to set the range, since doing
  # so pushes every panel back into being mostly empty, which is the problem
  # per-horizon ranges exist to solve; the strip simply clips its own tail.
  if (!isTRUE(ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS)) {
    return(list(lim = row_spec$lim, breaks = row_spec$breaks, acc = row_spec$acc))
  }
  b <- dplyr::filter(annex_cal_bins, model %in% row_spec$models, time_horizon == horizon)
  hi <- max(c(b$bin_mean_pred, b$bin_obs_prop, b$bin_obs_upper), na.rm = TRUE)
  step <- 10^floor(log10(hi)) / 2
  top <- ceiling(hi / step) * step
  # At most four ticks, otherwise the labels collide into one unreadable
  # numeric string at print size.
  brk <- pretty(c(0, top), n = 3L)
  brk <- brk[brk >= 0 & brk <= top + 1e-12]
  while (length(brk) > 4L) brk <- brk[seq(1L, length(brk), by = 2L)]
  # Accuracy comes from the BREAK SPACING, not from the range top: deriving it
  # from the top produced labels that were numerically wrong and duplicated,
  # including an interior tick printed as if it were the panel minimum.
  stp <- if (length(brk) > 1L) min(diff(brk)) else top
  acc <- 10^floor(log10(stp))
  lab <- scales::number(brk[brk > 0], accuracy = acc)
  stopifnot("per-horizon tick labels collide; widen the accuracy" = !any(duplicated(lab)))
  list(lim = c(0, top), breaks = brk, acc = acc)
}
.annex_build_panel <- function(row_spec, horizon, show_x, show_y, show_legend, show_tag, show_title) {
  mcs <- row_spec$models
  .lm <- .annex_limits_for(row_spec, horizon)
  lim <- .lm$lim
  who <- paste(mcs, collapse = "+")
  bins <- dplyr::filter(annex_cal_bins, model %in% mcs, time_horizon == horizon)
  preds <- dplyr::filter(annex_cal_preds, model %in% mcs, time_horizon == horizon)
  stopifnot(nrow(bins) > 0L, nrow(preds) > 0L)
  bins$model <- factor(bins$model, levels = mcs)
  preds$model <- factor(preds$model, levels = mcs)
  # Membership is judged on the TRUE mean predicted risk, never on the dodged
  # one, so a purely cosmetic offset can never delete a bin that genuinely
  # belongs in the panel.
  keep <- bins$bin_mean_pred >= lim[1L] & bins$bin_mean_pred <= lim[2L] &
    bins$bin_obs_prop >= lim[1L] & bins$bin_obs_prop <= lim[2L]
  if (any(!keep)) {
    .annex_diag_add("outside", sum(!keep),
                    sprintf("%s at %d months: %d bins fall outside the panel range and are not drawn.",
                            who, horizon, sum(!keep)))
    bins <- bins[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  }
  bins$x_plot <- bins$bin_mean_pred + vapply(as.character(bins$model), .annex_dodge_for, numeric(1L), lim = lim)
  bins$x_plot <- pmin(pmax(bins$x_plot, lim[1L]), lim[2L])
  bins$lo_d <- pmax(bins$bin_obs_lower, lim[1L])
  bins$hi_d <- pmin(bins$bin_obs_upper, lim[2L])
  .n_trunc <- sum(bins$bin_obs_upper > lim[2L] | bins$bin_obs_lower < lim[1L], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (.n_trunc > 0L) {
    .annex_diag_add("trunc", .n_trunc,
                    sprintf("%s at %d months: %d error bars truncated at the panel edge.",
                            who, horizon, .n_trunc))
  }
  .n_noci <- sum(is.na(bins$bin_obs_lower) | is.na(bins$bin_obs_upper))
  if (.n_noci > 0L) {
    .annex_diag_add("noci", .n_noci,
                    sprintf("%s at %d months: %d bins have no estimable CI and are drawn without an error bar.",
                            who, horizon, .n_noci))
  }
  # Break the joining line wherever a bin was removed, so the curve is never
  # drawn straight through a region whose bin exists but is not shown.
  bins <- bins[order(bins$model, bins$bin), , drop = FALSE]
  bins$seg <- unlist(lapply(split(bins$bin, bins$model), function(z)
    cumsum(c(0L, as.integer(diff(z) != 1L)))), use.names = FALSE)
  bins$grp <- paste(bins$model, bins$seg, sep = "_")
  preds_in <- dplyr::filter(preds, pred_risk >= lim[1L], pred_risk <= lim[2L])
  .n_out <- nrow(preds) - nrow(preds_in)
  if (.n_out > 0L) {
    .annex_diag_add("density", 100 * .n_out / nrow(preds),
                    sprintf("%s at %d months: %.2f%% of individual predictions lie beyond the panel cap and are excluded from the density strips.",
                            who, horizon, 100 * .n_out / nrow(preds)))
  }
  shp <- vapply(mcs, function(m) .annex_aes[[m]]$shape, numeric(1L))
  lty <- vapply(mcs, function(m) .annex_aes[[m]]$linetype, character(1L))
  cols <- vapply(mcs, .annex_col, character(1L))
  fills <- vapply(mcs, .annex_fill, character(1L))
  labs <- vapply(mcs, function(m) .annex_aes[[m]]$label, character(1L))
  .ylab_fmt <- function(b) {
    out <- scales::number(b, accuracy = .lm$acc)
    out[is.finite(b) & abs(b - lim[1L]) < 1e-12] <- ""
    out
  }
  .xlab_fmt <- function(b) if (show_x) scales::number(b, accuracy = .lm$acc) else rep("", length(b))
  main <- ggplot2::ggplot(bins, ggplot2::aes(x = x_plot, y = bin_obs_prop)) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.3, color = "gray70") +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lo_d, ymax = hi_d, color = model),
                           width = 0, linewidth = 0.42, alpha = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(color = model, linetype = model, group = grp), linewidth = 0.55) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = model, shape = model),
                        size = ANNEX_POINT_SIZE, stroke = ANNEX_POINT_STROKE, fill = "white") +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = cols, labels = labs, name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = shp, labels = labs, name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_linetype_manual(values = lty, labels = labs, name = NULL) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = lim, breaks = .lm$breaks, labels = .xlab_fmt,
                                expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.012, 0.012))) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = lim, breaks = .lm$breaks, labels = .ylab_fmt,
                                expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.012, 0.012))) +
    ggplot2::labs(subtitle = if (show_title) paste0(horizon, " months") else NULL) +
    .annex_theme_main()
  if (show_tag) {
    main <- main +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = lim[1L], y = lim[2L],
                        #label = paste0(row_spec$tag, "  ", row_spec$desc),
                        label = row_spec$tag,
                        #hjust = 0, vjust = 1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.15,
                        #hjust = 0, vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 3.15,
                        hjust = 1.4, vjust = -0.4, fontface = "bold", size = 3.15,
                        family = .annex_font, color = "black")
  }
  # Every panel now carries x tick numbers, and the outermost of those extend
  # past the panel edge, so without a gutter the last label of one panel butts
  # against the first label of the next (they rendered as "0.150.00"). A left
  # inset on each panel supplies that gutter.
  main <- main + ggplot2::theme(plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 0, r = 1, b = 0, l = if (show_tag) 0 else 8))
  if (!show_y) {
    # An unlabelled axis must not keep its ticks: orphan tick marks beside a
    # neighbouring density strip are what made the previous version look as if
    # a black line ran down the density.
    main <- main + ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                  axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank())
  }
  if (show_legend && length(mcs) > 1L) {
    main <- main + ggplot2::theme(
      legend.position = c(0.02, 0.95), legend.justification = c(0, 1),
      legend.background = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.key = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.key.height = ggplot2::unit(8, "pt"), legend.key.width = ggplot2::unit(13, "pt"),
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, family = .annex_font),
      legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.spacing.y = ggplot2::unit(0, "pt"))
  }
  .dens <- function(flip) {
    g <- ggplot2::ggplot(preds_in, ggplot2::aes(x = pred_risk, group = model, fill = model)) +
      ggplot2::geom_density(color = NA, alpha = 0.55, adjust = 1, trim = TRUE) +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = fills) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = lim, expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.012, 0.012))) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      .annex_theme_dens()
    if (flip) g + ggplot2::coord_flip() else g
  }
  design <- c(patchwork::area(1, 1, 12, 12), patchwork::area(1, 13, 12, 13), patchwork::area(13, 1, 13, 12))
  main + .dens(TRUE) + .dens(FALSE) + patchwork::plot_layout(design = design)
}
.annex_build_row <- function(row_spec, horizons = ANNEX_TIMES, show_title = TRUE) {
  # Column headers ("6 months" ...) are printed on the TOP row only: the
  # columns are the same horizons in every row, so repeating the headers costs
  # vertical space that the panels can use instead.
  # x tick marks and numbers, by contrast, are drawn on EVERY panel of every
  # row, so each panel can be read on its own without tracing back to a
  # neighbour, which also keeps the figure honest under
  # ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS where the ranges genuinely differ.
  .per_h <- isTRUE(ANNEX_PER_HORIZON_LIMITS)
  panels <- lapply(seq_along(horizons), function(i)
    .annex_build_panel(row_spec, horizons[i],
                       show_x = TRUE, show_y = (.per_h || i == 1L),
                       #show_legend = (i == 1L), show_tag = (i == 1L),
                       show_legend = (i == 1L), show_tag = FALSE,
                       show_title = show_title))
  patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, ncol = length(horizons))
}

line type. Points are observed against mean predicted risk within quantile groups of predicted risk
(up to 8 groups; groups with fewer than 20 individuals suppressed). Error bars are pointwise 95%
confidence intervals: bootstrap percentile (B = 1000, validation rows resampled). Predicted risks
are the frozen held-out predictions averaged across the five imputations. The dotted line marks
perfect calibration; x and y share the same range and the panels are square, so it is a true 45
degree diagonal. Shaded marginal strips show the distribution of individual predicted risks; the
strip on the right projects that distribution onto the observed-probability axis, representing
where observed risks would fall under perfect calibration. Within each row all four horizons share
one risk range, so panels are directly comparable across horizons; tick labels are shown once per
row. For display, the marginal strips exclude individual predictions above the plotted range, at
